kK5dgC2n6K.one_liner: Shows on-policy distillation works with a +1/-1 reward on whether teacher probability exceeds student's, without KL divergence.
kK5dgC2n6K.problem: On-policy distillation inherits KL divergence as its default loss, but it is unclear whether KL is needed for effective distillation.
kK5dgC2n6K.method: They assign a reward of +1 to tokens where the teacher probability exceeds the student probability and -1 where it is lower, which reproduces almost the same training behavior as OPD with reverse KL, and show that only a small subset of tokens with strong teacher-student disagreement matters. As an application they introduce Consensus Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation (C-MOPD) to improve multi-teacher OPD.
kK5dgC2n6K.key_idea: Reward each token by the sign of teacher minus student probability so updates move toward the teacher, with the direction of high-disagreement tokens carrying the effect.
kK5dgC2n6K.evidence: Experiments on Qwen-derived and Llama models at different scales on math and code benchmarks under matched training settings, plus multi-teacher OPD.
kK5dgC2n6K.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the question is clear and that the finding that the simple sign reward (BinaryOPD) stays close to OPD is cleanly demonstrated by extensive, honest experiments.
kK5dgC2n6K.main_concern: Prior non-KL distillation objectives are missing from the framing, and the sign-reward estimator is not tied explicitly to an L1 (total variation) matching objective, so the claim about distribution matching is not fully established.

OIKmF1KLHC.one_liner: Uses minimal-pair relation-word edits and workspace interventions to test whether a language model's Jacobian-lens workspace holds graph edges.
OIKmF1KLHC.problem: The Jacobian lens reads a language model's workspace as words (nodes), but multi-step reasoning also needs relations, and it is unknown whether the workspace holds edges or only nodes.
OIKmF1KLHC.method: They compare questions about the same story that differ in one relation word and edit the workspace to see which changes affect the answer, across multiple models. Editing a person matters where the name appears and at every depth, while editing a relation matters only at the relation word and in middle layers.
OIKmF1KLHC.key_idea: Causal interventions on workspace coordinates at specific token positions and layers show entity and relation information live at different positions and times, so no connected graph exists at once.
OIKmF1KLHC.evidence: Minimal-pair interventions across token positions and layers with matched controls, plus subspace transfer and probing, on models of at most 4B parameters including Qwen and Gemma, with 60 items per condition by default (per reviewers).
OIKmF1KLHC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the minimal-pair design and position- and layer-specific causal interventions with matched controls make the comparison of entity and relation roles convincing and well controlled.
OIKmF1KLHC.main_concern: The evaluation is limited to models of at most 4B parameters and closely related synthetic templates with single-token concepts, so generalization to larger models and general relational reasoning is not established.

MiA5ItRJ3E.one_liner: Training-free guidance that projects the classifier-free guidance update onto new-event and state-preserving directions for consistent interleaved generation
MiA5ItRJ3E.problem: Interleaved image-text generation struggles to preserve visual subjects, temporal consistency and physical plausibility, and most existing MLLM solutions rely on computationally expensive additional training with augmented data.
MiA5ItRJ3E.method: SCO treats the classifier-free guidance update as a reference and applies minimal self-correction under a new-event constraint for temporal consistency and a state-preserving constraint for subject coherence; reviewers describe an exact closed-form two-variable solution that combines four predicted velocities.
MiA5ItRJ3E.key_idea: Take the CFG update as a reference and minimally correct it under two constraints, one promoting the new event and one preserving the prior visual state.
MiA5ItRJ3E.evidence: Interleaved multimodal generation benchmarks (OpenING per reviewers) on seven image-text models and three video models, plus an extension to video generation for robot manipulation and handcrafting.
MiA5ItRJ3E.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem practical and the split of the CFG update into new-event and state-preserving directions intuitive, training-free and broadly applicable across models.
MiA5ItRJ3E.main_concern: Inference overhead (four velocity predictions per step, LLM prompt rewriting) is unreported, and the need for the joint projection over simpler combinations is not ablated.

foEizau8LN.one_liner: Learns a linear latent Koopman generator from unpaired distribution snapshots via a weak continuity equation, with memory for branching.
foEizau8LN.problem: Neural-ODE and flow-matching methods interpolate population snapshots but struggle to extrapolate beyond the training horizon and lack an explicit mechanism for developmental branching.
foEizau8LN.method: KoopCell jointly learns representations and linear latent dynamics under Koopman-Mori-Zwanzig theory, with a closed-form least-squares estimator of the Koopman generator derived from the weak continuity equation. KoopCell-M adds non-Markovian memory to the latent dynamics through a Markovian embedding to model branching.
foEizau8LN.key_idea: Fit a linear Koopman generator in latent space by closed-form least squares on the weak continuity equation, and add memory variables for branching.
foEizau8LN.evidence: Synthetic systems (Koopman spectrum recovery, branching) and three scRNA-seq datasets testing interpolation, extrapolation and high-dimensional gene-expression distribution prediction, plus convergence guarantees under stated assumptions.
foEizau8LN.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract only claims best performance among the evaluated methods, with no numbers.
foEizau8LN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the unpaired weak-form population loss, the closed-form generator update with cheap matrix-exponential rollout, and the biologically informed memory extension.
foEizau8LN.main_concern: KoopCell-M needs extra supervision (a pretrained cell-state classifier and a specified lineage graph), and the memory ablation does not separate memory from added model capacity.

zzqLU5eSbj.one_liner: Tree search using a predicted target distribution, with expected queries O(H(p) + k log eta) and a matching lower bound.
zzqLU5eSbj.problem: Finding an unknown target vertex in a tree with few queries is hard when only a predicted distribution of unknown quality is available.
zzqLU5eSbj.method: For a tree of pathwidth k, each query on a vertex reveals which neighbor lies on the path to the target, and the algorithm combines weighted-centroid search with boundary compression using the predicted distribution while retaining robustness when the prediction is poor.
zzqLU5eSbj.key_idea: Boundary compression with weighted-centroid search extends entropy-based search from paths to trees, tying query cost to the target's distance from the boundary and to the earth mover's distance.
zzqLU5eSbj.evidence: An upper bound with a matching lower bound showing asymptotic tightness, plus experiments on real-world and synthetic trees against a baseline that trusts the prediction completely.
zzqLU5eSbj.claimed_gains: Expected query complexity O(H(p) + k log eta), where H(p) is the entropy of the true distribution and eta the earth mover's distance, is asymptotically tight and uses substantially fewer queries than a baseline that fully trusts the prediction.
zzqLU5eSbj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is clearly written, the algorithm is simple, and matching upper and lower bounds give a tight characterization for a well-motivated distributional-prediction model.
zzqLU5eSbj.main_concern: The technical originality is limited because the model, the entropy-plus-error form and the recovery procedure come from prior work, with boundary compression the main new ingredient, and experiments lack a prediction-independent baseline.

KIsuZ4ObE5.one_liner: Disaggregated KV cache system that uses CXL cache-line load/store to fetch only top-k KV entries on demand for sparse-attention LLMs.
KIsuZ4ObE5.problem: RDMA-based disaggregated KV pools fetch the entire prefix KV cache before decoding, which is wasteful for sparse attention models that use only a small fraction of entries.
KIsuZ4ObE5.method: SAC exploits the low-latency, cache-line granularity load/store semantics of CXL to fetch only the required top-k KV entries on demand during inference.
KIsuZ4ObE5.key_idea: Replace coarse prefix prefetch over RDMA with on-demand fine-grained CXL access to just the top-k KV entries that sparse attention selects.
KIsuZ4ObE5.evidence: End-to-end evaluation on DeepSeek-V3.2 using SGLang on real hardware, covering context length, concurrency and output configurations.
KIsuZ4ObE5.claimed_gains: 2.1x higher throughput, 9.7x lower TTFT and 1.8x lower TBT compared to RDMA-based baselines.
KIsuZ4ObE5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that aligning disaggregated KV management with sparse attention is sensible and promising, and that the system implementation and end-to-end evaluation are comprehensive and convincing.
KIsuZ4ObE5.main_concern: Hardware evaluation covers only DeepSeek-V3.2 with top-k fixed at 2048 and limited sensitivity analysis, so generality to other sparse-attention models and realistic cache-hit mixes is unvalidated.

ZJIqqHVTnE.one_liner: Fine-tunes an LLM on trajectories from verifiable task families with shared tools or workflows so experience learning transfers across tasks.
ZJIqqHVTnE.problem: Agents can accumulate interaction feedback, but turning it into reusable experience is hard, and training on isolated tasks does not reveal what knowledge stays useful across episodes.
ZJIqqHVTnE.method: MetaExp builds Shared-Tool families (fixed black-box tools) and Shared-Workflow families (preserved latent procedures) with controlled cross-task structure, collects and filters sequential trajectories, and fine-tunes Qwen3.5-122B-A10B on 4,956 trajectories from 1,000 task families.
ZJIqqHVTnE.key_idea: Train on task families that preserve a reusable factor (tools or workflow) while varying task realizations, so the model learns to carry experience across tasks without reusing solutions.
ZJIqqHVTnE.evidence: Fine-tuning on 4,956 trajectories from 1,000 task families, evaluated with parameters frozen during downstream evolution on several benchmarks including SpreadsheetBench, with domain-excluded evaluation and behavioral analyses.
ZJIqqHVTnE.claimed_gains: With parameters frozen during downstream evolution, improves by +8.5 points on SpreadsheetBench and peaks at +2.3 on another benchmark (name cut off in the input).
ZJIqqHVTnE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that making experience learning a transferable capability is an important goal, and that the Shared-Tool and Shared-Workflow task-family construction is a well-motivated, scalable way to supervise it.
ZJIqqHVTnE.main_concern: Gains may reflect general agent skill rather than experience learning, since SFT already lifts performance before any experience is collected and controls such as independent-task SFT and a frozen experience bank are missing.

LYU80Xj5R4.one_liner: SPAR uses sparse-autoencoder features of exogenous-variable representation shifts as an intervention interface for phase-aware forecast correction.
LYU80Xj5R4.problem: Redundant or unstable cross-variable dependencies from exogenous variables can hurt forecasts, and existing methods model or select them with limited ability to regulate their predictive effects inside learned representations.
LYU80Xj5R4.method: Using sparse autoencoders, they find that representation shifts from adding exogenous variables concentrate in a few sparse features. SPAR, a plug-in, learns phase-aware corrections of those features from forecasting error, keeping beneficial cross-variable effects and mitigating harmful ones.
LYU80Xj5R4.key_idea: Correct only the few sparse-autoencoder features that change when exogenous variables are added, with corrections conditioned on periodic phase and trained from forecast error.
LYU80Xj5R4.evidence: Four backbones, seven datasets and four horizons, with ablations on sparse correction, calibration and candidate selection.
LYU80Xj5R4.claimed_gains: Average relative MSE reductions of 5.78%, 8.02%, 6.84% and 5.74% for the four backbones across seven datasets.
LYU80Xj5R4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the representation-level intervention mechanism and the consistent gains across backbones and datasets, supported by relevant ablations.
LYU80Xj5R4.main_concern: Simpler baselines such as a linear residual corrector with matched parameters are missing and baseline coverage is limited, so the need for the sparse, phase-aware design is not established.

d5PLbOmiJM.one_liner: UniForget jointly unlearns concepts in unified multimodal models' generation and understanding pathways, evaluated on the new UUBench.
d5PLbOmiJM.problem: Single-pathway unlearning methods suppress a concept in image generation or in visual understanding but achieve limited joint forgetting across both pathways of unified multimodal models.
d5PLbOmiJM.method: UUBench covers 30 target concepts and 60 neighboring concepts to diagnose cross-pathway forgetting, and UniForget targets joint forgetting while preserving other capabilities. Reviews describe it as generation-side weight editing combined with understanding-side LoRA optimization.
d5PLbOmiJM.key_idea: Combine generation-side weight editing with understanding-side LoRA training in a coordinated sequence so a concept is forgotten in both pathways.
d5PLbOmiJM.evidence: UUBench evaluation on BAGEL-7B-MoT and Janus-Pro-7B against single-pathway methods and their direct compositions, with analysis of forgetting-versus-capability trade-offs.
d5PLbOmiJM.claimed_gains: Joint forgetting rates of 80.0% on BAGEL-7B-MoT and 92.7% on Janus-Pro-7B, outperforming representative baselines.
d5PLbOmiJM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the cross-pathway question meaningful and UUBench a useful diagnostic that checks both pathways, neighboring concepts and utility, with promising gains over baselines.
d5PLbOmiJM.main_concern: The gains are not isolated to pathway coordination as opposed to richer supervision, and the model may merely answer with a generic category instead of truly forgetting the concept.

Bqq0GWJX1w.one_liner: Distills solver feedback into reusable visual skills that guide a VLM in choosing subproblems for decomposition-based large-scale routing.
Bqq0GWJX1w.problem: Decomposition lets solvers handle large routing problems, but picking productive subproblems is hard and existing approaches leave their selection experience implicit and hard to reuse.
Bqq0GWJX1w.method: ViSO distills solver feedback into transferable visual skills that direct optimization toward promising subproblems, coupled with off-the-shelf solvers through a unified decomposition interface for symmetric, asymmetric, and capacitated routing. Per the reviews, reconstructed solutions are checked for feasibility and accepted only if they improve the incumbent.
Bqq0GWJX1w.key_idea: Summarize solver feedback into an explicit bank of visual selection skills that a VLM uses, without parameter updates, to pick subproblems.
Bqq0GWJX1w.evidence: Four routing families with up to 85,900 nodes against LKH-3, HGS, PyVRP, ViTSP, NCO-LLM, and DRAGON, plus transfer to two-dimensional bin packing.
Bqq0GWJX1w.claimed_gains: Reduces mean TSP and CVRP gaps by 10.5% and 11.5% relative to LKH-3 and HGS, gets a mean ACVRP objective 2.72 lower than PyVRP's, and improves TSP by 26.5% over ViTSP and CVRP by 94.8% over NCO-LLM.
Bqq0GWJX1w.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the framework is reasonable and broad, covering several routing families with strong solver baselines and feasibility checks that keep the incumbent solution valid.
Bqq0GWJX1w.main_concern: Novelty is insufficiently isolated, since visual selection and segment contraction build on ViTSP and the distillation resembles ExpeL, so ablations against simpler rules or trajectory summaries are needed.

b4IrzWdpW7.one_liner: Post-hoc OOD detector combining spectrally weighted logit normalization with a score from how projections change under patch shuffling.
b4IrzWdpW7.problem: Post-hoc OOD detection accuracy varies strongly across backbones, and logit-based and activation-shaping methods degrade on well-behaved models, where OOD inputs concentrate on leading singular directions and inflate logits.
b4IrzWdpW7.method: OMASHU has OMA, which normalizes logits with a spectrally weighted norm that attenuates the leading directions, and SHU, which exploits a difference in how ID and OOD projections behave under patch shuffling (the abstract is cut off here). It is motivated by spectral projection profiles over the right singular vectors of the classifier weight matrix.
b4IrzWdpW7.key_idea: Attenuate leading singular directions in logit normalization and add a patch-shuffling projection-difference score, since leading directions encode texture and trailing ones global structure.
b4IrzWdpW7.evidence: Spectral analysis across 11 models for well-behavedness (per reviews); evaluation on ImageNet-1k with four modern backbones, with hyperparameters tuned on OpenOOD validation data.
b4IrzWdpW7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the spectral perspective on why OOD methods differ across models interesting and well motivated, with complementary OMA and SHU components that outperform competitors on the evaluated models.
b4IrzWdpW7.main_concern: Evidence is narrow and some interpretations overreach: the well-behavedness correlation uses 11 models, evaluation covers only ImageNet-1k and four backbones, and links between logit norm, texture or structure encoding, and detection are indirect.

wtI9WuzU2c.one_liner: Incomplete multi-view clustering that recovers missing views by conditional flow matching in a frozen latent space, conditioned on semantic codes.
wtI9WuzU2c.problem: Incomplete multi-view clustering needs missing-view recovery that stays separate from representation learning and avoids recursive error propagation from generated views.
wtI9WuzU2c.method: TRACE learns a dual-level representation separating compact semantic codes from view-specific latents, then trains target-excluded conditional flow matching that treats an observed view as a pseudo-missing target and learns source-to-target transport in the frozen latent space. Each missing view is recovered independently from all genuinely observed views and the candidates are aggregated, with generated views barred from later recovery.
wtI9WuzU2c.key_idea: Learn source-to-target latent transport by flow matching conditioned on semantic codes that exclude the target view, and recover missing views only from observed ones.
wtI9WuzU2c.evidence: Experiments on five datasets against recent methods; reviews note the ablations cover one dataset and one missing-view ratio.
wtI9WuzU2c.claimed_gains: Reports competitive or superior performance against recent state-of-the-art methods on five datasets; no numbers are stated.
wtI9WuzU2c.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the two-stage design that separates representation learning from missing-view recovery is reasonable, and that excluding the target view's semantic code from conditioning is a sensible choice.
wtI9WuzU2c.main_concern: Experimental support is limited: ablations cover one dataset and missing ratio, comparisons are not fully up to date, efficiency and generated-representation quality are unexamined, and some reported numbers are inconsistent.

eD7cww8QVc.one_liner: Tunes time-dependent guidance weights for diffusion and flow-matching posterior sampling offline by solving a two-dimensional least-squares problem per step.
eD7cww8QVc.problem: Training-free posterior sampling methods balance prior and measurement consistency with guidance weights that are usually tuned by heuristics.
eD7cww8QVc.method: At each time step the conditional denoising score-matching or conditional flow-matching objective is least-squares, so optimizing the weights on the unconditional network output and a measurement-guidance term reduces to a two-dimensional linear least-squares problem. Weights are optimized offline for a given measurement operator, noise level, and sampler from one minibatch of sampling trajectories, with no retraining.
eD7cww8QVc.key_idea: Because the conditional matching objective is quadratic in the two guidance weights, fit them in closed form at each time step from a minibatch of trajectories.
eD7cww8QVc.evidence: Instantiated with the standard Tweedie-based measurement-consistency term; reviews note multiple datasets, inverse problems, samplers, and ablations, and the abstract is cut off before the results.
eD7cww8QVc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the least-squares formulation is simple, principled, and computationally cheap, works for both diffusion and flow-matching models, and is supported by experiments across datasets, inverse problems, and samplers.
eD7cww8QVc.main_concern: Novelty over existing guidance-weighting and calibration approaches is unclear, weights adapt only per operator rather than per sample, and results are mostly empirical, with FID on only 100 images and uneven gains.

3AaAwSvSXV.one_liner: Row-normalized degenerate degree-two U-statistics become martingales, giving anytime-valid confidence sequences and tests without spectrum knowledge.
3AaAwSvSXV.problem: Degenerate degree-two U-statistics have non-Gaussian limits, which makes sequential inference much harder than in the nondegenerate case.
3AaAwSvSXV.method: Row normalization preserves the target parameter and makes the centered numerator a martingale on a harmonic variance clock; they prove a strong Gaussian approximation, estimate the variance online, and combine it with Gaussian-mixture and stitched LIL boundaries, then extend to vector-valued kernels with Mahalanobis confidence ellipsoids.
3AaAwSvSXV.key_idea: Row normalization turns the degenerate U-statistic into a martingale on a harmonic variance clock, replacing Gaussian-chaos calibration with ordinary Gaussian calibration at a logarithmic variance cost.
3AaAwSvSXV.evidence: Asymptotic theory (strong Gaussian approximation, time-uniform coverage), numerical experiments against benchmarks (SAGE per reviews), and a customer-response application.
3AaAwSvSXV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the idea is elegant, the theory is carefully developed, and the method is simple to implement and clearly presented.
3AaAwSvSXV.main_concern: Experiments are limited to synthetic settings with essentially one competitor (SAGE), and the asymptotic guarantees leave finite-sample convergence under the harmonic clock unexamined.

P8cMuhbbfz.one_liner: Large-scale study of synthetic pre-pretraining across tasks, mixtures and scales, finding gains persist but not due to a grammatical prior.
P8cMuhbbfz.problem: Pre-pretraining on synthetic data was tested only up to 1B parameters and under 2B tokens of mostly web text, and its gains were attributed to a grammatical prior without scale or realistic-mixture evidence.
P8cMuhbbfz.method: A study spanning six PPT tasks, four pre-training data mixtures, four parameter scales (500M to 7B) and budgets up to 100B tokens, comparing downstream gains against grammatical acceptability and long-range retrieval measures.
P8cMuhbbfz.key_idea: Test the mechanism of pre-pretraining by comparing downstream gains with grammatical-acceptability versus long-range-retrieval measures across tasks and scales.
P8cMuhbbfz.evidence: Six PPT tasks, four data mixtures, 500M to 7B models and up to 100B pre-training tokens, with BLiMP and retrieval-NLL analyses and C4 and Marin runs.
P8cMuhbbfz.claimed_gains: PPT gains persist at scale, e.g., saving at least 21B pre-training tokens at the 3B scale; a review cites downstream gains of 1.6 (C4) and 1.2 (Marin) points for 3B at 100B tokens.
P8cMuhbbfz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the systematic, well-controlled scale study answers an important question and shows PPT gains survive larger models and longer training.
P8cMuhbbfz.main_concern: The retrieval explanation is stated more strongly than the evidence supports, since the retrieval metric averages NLL over the whole text and BLiMP subtask results are mixed.

NLcwgsKnOj.one_liner: Neural Affine Maximizer replaces the finite menu in affine maximizer auctions with a neural boosting function over outcomes.
NLcwgsKnOj.problem: Truthful learned auctions discretize the outcome space into a finite menu, which suffers from the curse of dimensionality in large-scale auctions.
NLcwgsKnOj.method: NAM keeps truthfulness by building on affine maximizer auctions but uses a neural-network-parameterized boosting function over the outcome space instead of a menu, with unbiased gradient estimators enabling first-order optimization.
NLcwgsKnOj.key_idea: Parameterize the boosting function of an affine maximizer auction with a concave neural network over the continuous outcome space, so no menu is enumerated and truthfulness holds by construction.
NLcwgsKnOj.evidence: Experiments on instances with up to 15 buyers or 30 goods against learned baselines; reviews cite compute-matched curves and a theorem showing equal-weight affine maximizers can be reproduced.
NLcwgsKnOj.claimed_gains: With 3 buyers, 30 goods and additive valuations, NAM finds a truthful auction with 10.6% higher revenue and lower training time than the compared baselines.
NLcwgsKnOj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the discretization-free concave boost clean and theoretically sound (exact truthfulness and feasibility), with strong results in many-goods settings and honest reporting of inference cost.
NLcwgsKnOj.main_concern: Reproducibility and guarantees: one reviewer could not reproduce several table entries from the released code (some seeds collapse), and another notes the truthfulness guarantee is not quantified given fixed-iteration inference solvers.

XXW67VWVM2.one_liner: TSFMAudit detects pretraining contamination in time series foundation models from short fine-tuning probe dynamics relative to reference models.
XXW67VWVM2.problem: Time series foundation models may have seen evaluation datasets during pretraining, inflating results, and auditing is hard because signals are continuous, heterogeneous and rarely documented.
XXW67VWVM2.method: TSFMAudit runs a short fine-tuning probe, measures loss reduction and backbone movement, and compares candidate-to-reference differences and ratios across heterogeneous forecasters to flag prior exposure.
XXW67VWVM2.key_idea: Prior exposure should speed adaptation with less backbone movement; compare these probe dynamics against reference models via differences and ratios to debias.
XXW67VWVM2.evidence: Six TSFMs and 137 datasets with documented training-source labels, a separate evaluation on 50 TIME datasets, and ground-truth validation by pretraining Chronos-T5-mini and Moirai-1.0-R-Small from scratch on controlled manifests.
XXW67VWVM2.claimed_gains: Candidate-averaged MCC 0.317 versus 0.050 for the strongest scalar baseline and 0.169 for candidate-only dynamics, and MCCs of 0.356 and 0.618 under ground-truth membership.
XXW67VWVM2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem important, the framework well motivated and the first study of contamination auditing for time series foundation models, with a broad evaluation across models, datasets and baselines.
XXW67VWVM2.main_concern: Absolute performance is modest and unstable: MCC 0.317 +/- 0.211, mean macro-F1 of 0.567, large variation across candidate models, and dependence on the choice of reference models.

FT5FYZTOXK.one_liner: Sample-view quality scores from reconstruction, consistency, and cluster compatibility weight fusion and supervise relations in multi-view clustering.
FT5FYZTOXK.problem: Existing quality-aware multi-view clustering gives coarse quality estimates from limited cues, uses them only to reweight features or fusion, leaves unreliable relations unregulated, and may discard weak relations that other views partly support.
FT5FYZTOXK.method: CGQRL estimates dynamic sample-view quality from reconstruction fidelity, cross-view consistency, and cluster compatibility, uses it to weight view representations for consensus fusion, and transfers it to the relational level to score neighborhood and cross-view assignment relations. A reliability-preserving structural alignment then gives soft structural supervision.
FT5FYZTOXK.key_idea: Carry sample-view quality scores down to relation level so reliable neighborhood and cross-view assignment relations get stronger structural supervision while weak but supported ones are preserved.
FT5FYZTOXK.evidence: Reviewers cite a wide range of datasets and noise contamination rates measured by ACC, NMI, ARI, and RI; the visible abstract is cut off before results.
FT5FYZTOXK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem of heterogeneous observation reliability is significant and the quality-to-relation design is technically solid with comprehensive evaluation across datasets and noise rates.
FT5FYZTOXK.main_concern: Reviewers say the estimated quality scores are not shown to identify corrupted observations, and sensitivity, per-cue ablation, complexity, and experimental-detail analyses are missing.

IeX28QeIGb.one_liner: Item-marginalized maximum likelihood IRT treats model abilities as fixed and benchmark items as random effects for LLM evaluation.
IeX28QeIGb.problem: Conventional IRT estimation assumes many examinees and few items, while LLM evaluation compares a few models on hundreds or thousands of benchmark items.
IeX28QeIGb.method: The authors marginalize over items instead of persons, treating evaluated model abilities as fixed inferential targets and items as random effects, and apply it to model ranking and to item selection for benchmark distillation.
IeX28QeIGb.key_idea: Marginalize out item parameters (random effects with a population prior) rather than person parameters, matching the item-rich response-matrix geometry of LLM evaluation.
IeX28QeIGb.evidence: Simulations calibrated to six benchmarks, item-selection experiments with 12-40 calibration models, and real sparse response matrices.
IeX28QeIGb.claimed_gains: With 12 models, item marginalization reduces average Kendall ranking loss across six benchmarks by 56% relative to person marginalization, and with 12-40 calibration models item-marginalized selection reduces held-out ranking loss by 18%.
IeX28QeIGb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation is clear and well argued and the method is elegant, supported by well-designed experiments, robustness checks, and honest disclosure of limits.
IeX28QeIGb.main_concern: A shrinkage baseline is missing (the gain may come from shrinking item parameters rather than from which axis is marginalized), absolute gains are small behind large relative ones, and theory and binary-response scope are limited.

G3vEKSciGb.one_liner: Propagation-constrained inference over source sets reorders candidates, then order-adaptive conformal scoring gives smaller recall-guaranteed source sets.
G3vEKSciGb.problem: Existing conformal source localization selects candidates by individual confidence, which can require large sets because it ignores how their combined selection meets the recall target.
G3vEKSciGb.method: JCSL is a post hoc framework that uses propagation constraints to infer a distribution over source sets and prioritizes nodes by expected contribution to normalized source recovery. Order-adaptive set scoring uses the original model's information to decide how far to extend the refined ordering to meet the recall target after calibration.
G3vEKSciGb.key_idea: Rank nodes by marginal contribution under a propagation-constrained joint source-set distribution, then calibrate the prefix length with conformal scoring.
G3vEKSciGb.evidence: 15 spreading conditions on three real-world networks with ablations of propagation constraints and order-adaptive scoring, plus a finite-sample marginal recall guarantee under exchangeability.
G3vEKSciGb.claimed_gains: Reduces mean set size by 3.45-95.35% against the best baseline, with a mean rate of meeting the recall target of 0.8999 at nominal confidence 0.90.
G3vEKSciGb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the joint-inference-plus-conformal-calibration design is coherent, assumptions are stated, and the experiments with controls and ablations are comprehensive.
G3vEKSciGb.main_concern: Evaluation uses complete observations taken just after seeding and assumes the candidate set contains all true sources, so robustness to delayed, incomplete, or noisy reports and the cost of joint inference are unproven.

YrFQfNdCBC.one_liner: Analysis showing self-distillation conditioned on sampled demonstrations tilts the policy by pointwise mutual information, collapsing output diversity.
YrFQfNdCBC.problem: On-policy self-distillation achieves strong pass@1 but rollout diversity decreases and pass@k curves flatten, a hidden cost.
YrFQfNdCBC.method: The authors theoretically analyze the optimal self-distillation policy, showing it tilts the base distribution by a pointwise conditional mutual information between the student rollout and the correct rollout used as context. They test this on a controlled graph path-finding task and science question-answering benchmarks against RL.
YrFQfNdCBC.key_idea: A teacher conditioned on a sampled correct rollout rewards rollouts resembling it, amplifying existing probability gaps instead of preserving ratios among equally correct rollouts as on-policy RL does.
YrFQfNdCBC.evidence: Theory, a controlled graph path-finding task, and science QA benchmarks showing competitive average performance but lower functional and semantic diversity than RL and failure on out-of-distribution settings.
YrFQfNdCBC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the theory gives an intuitive explanation of diversity collapse and the controlled experiments across models and tasks show practical relevance.
YrFQfNdCBC.main_concern: The theory assumes a fixed teacher and demonstration distribution unlike practical EMA-teacher training, and diversity on real tasks is inferred mainly from pass@k curves.

D4LqhTwVzh.one_liner: Register tokens help pixel-space diffusion transformers without patch outliers, and Register Guidance amplifies register contribution at sampling.
D4LqhTwVzh.problem: It is unknown whether register tokens, which fix high-norm patch-token outliers in ViTs, also help Diffusion Transformers as they move to pixel-space training.
D4LqhTwVzh.method: The authors compare DiTs with and without registers in pixel-space and latent-space settings, analyze intermediate representations, and propose Register Guidance, which amplifies the contribution of register tokens responsible for visual structure and coherence. Reviews describe it as using the model without registers as the weaker counterpart.
D4LqhTwVzh.key_idea: Contrast predictions with and without register tokens, using the register-free model as the weaker one, to amplify register-driven structure in the manner of autoguidance.
D4LqhTwVzh.evidence: Experiments across model sizes, resolutions, and architectures in pixel-space and latent-space DiTs, feature-norm and total-variation analysis, and ablations on number and insertion layers of registers; registers are reported more effective in pixel-space than latent-space.
D4LqhTwVzh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it is an interesting, rigorous finding that registers help DiTs even without outliers, with larger gains in pixel space and a simple guidance technique.
D4LqhTwVzh.main_concern: Register Guidance closely resembles existing guidance methods (PAG, Skip Layer Guidance, AutoGuidance) without direct comparison, and the explanation of why registers help rests on limited norm and smoothness analyses.

9Lfv5lRBHb.one_liner: Layer-wise interpolation between edited and fine-tuned weights restores edit readout circuitry that fine-tuning disrupts.
9Lfv5lRBHb.problem: Fine-tuning edited LLMs for downstream adaptation erases the intended knowledge edits.
9Lfv5lRBHb.method: Layer-wise ablation shows edited memory is anchored in shallow editing layers while fine-tuning disrupts the deep editing and adjacent post-edit layers that form the readout circuitry. Layer-wise Model Interpolation (LMI) interpolates edited and fine-tuned weights with layer-aware coefficients, up-weighting the edited model in the readout circuitry and the fine-tuned model elsewhere.
9Lfv5lRBHb.key_idea: Revert only the readout-circuitry layers (deep editing and adjacent post-edit layers) toward the edited weights while keeping the fine-tuned weights elsewhere.
9Lfv5lRBHb.evidence: Layer-wise activation restoration, null-space analysis, and attention-based visualization, with LMI tested across four public datasets, three language models, and two editing methods (MEMIT and AlphaEdit per reviews).
9Lfv5lRBHb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper turns an empirical observation into a mechanistic, multi-evidence account of where fine-tuning breaks edits and offers a coherent recovery method.
9Lfv5lRBHb.main_concern: A cheap baseline such as re-applying the editor or freezing edited layers is missing, and generality is unproven beyond MEMIT and AlphaEdit, which edit similar early MLP layers.

FrPuUCsKog.one_liner: Factorization Regret, an information-theoretic gap between joint and Naive Bayes inference, quantifies latent-variable interactions in a POMDP gridworld.
FrPuUCsKog.problem: It is unclear whether barriers to generalizing to novel combinations of latent variables remain once all relevant variables are known.
FrPuUCsKog.method: In the Cognitive Gridworld, a stationary POMDP with parametric latent interactions, the authors define Factorization Regret and use it to explain Echo State Network sub-optimality. They introduce Representation Classification Chains that learn interactions and variable inference together via RL, and show imagined experience supports zero-shot control.
FrPuUCsKog.key_idea: Measure the cost of ignoring latent-variable interactions as the divergence between joint and Naive Bayes goal marginals, then learn interactions with a generator-plus-classifier chain trained by RL.
FrPuUCsKog.evidence: Three progressive experiments in the Cognitive Gridworld on RNN and ESN performance, learning latent variables with the chain via RL, and zero-shot control from imagined experience, mostly with two contexts per reviews.
FrPuUCsKog.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the minimal gridworld allows precise analysis against exact Bayesian references and the experiments build progressively in complexity.
FrPuUCsKog.main_concern: The link between Factorization Regret and learning compositional representations is indirect, formal properties are asserted rather than derived, and scalability is untested (the joint target grows exponentially with the number of contexts).

d57mTGAPPY.one_liner: Two-axis, 15-metric suite benchmarking 23 LLM steering methods on efficacy versus side effects, generalization, and data dependence.
d57mTGAPPY.problem: Existing steering evaluations cover efficacy, side effects, robustness, and data dependence only in fragments, so efficacy-side-effect trade-offs are not systematically characterized.
d57mTGAPPY.method: SteerScope scores target efficacy and side effects on language quality, task capabilities, and safety and reliability, adds sample-efficiency and sample-sensitivity metrics, and characterizes trade-off curves across steering strengths rather than a single operating point. It is released as an extensible codebase.
d57mTGAPPY.key_idea: Evaluate each steering method along two axes under matched models, tasks, and protocols, sweeping intervention strength to expose the efficacy-side-effect trade-off.
d57mTGAPPY.evidence: 23 methods across four families (including prompting, LoRA, and SFT baselines) on two model scales of the Gemma-2 family; the finding is that activation steering methods do not surpass the prompting baseline in overall balance.
d57mTGAPPY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the evaluation is extensive, jointly covers capability, safety, and quality side effects, and the strength sweeps give informative trade-off evidence.
d57mTGAPPY.main_concern: Only Gemma-2 models are evaluated and the task design that prioritizes concept insertion partly induces the measured conflict, with limited analysis of why side effects arise.

9D0MMjtW7l.one_liner: Finds power-law spectra in text representations and introduces Haar Delay, a frequency-aware diffusion schedule for continuous language models.
9D0MMjtW7l.problem: Continuous diffusion language models operate on text-encoder representations, but unlike in vision it is not known how their spectra behave or how frequency bands should be treated across diffusion timesteps.
9D0MMjtW7l.method: The authors analyze Fourier spectra of text-model representations across sequence length, probe what low and high bands encode, and introduce a frequency-aware diffusion strategy (Haar Delay per reviews) that processes low- and high-frequency components separately across timesteps without adding parameters.
9D0MMjtW7l.key_idea: Process low- and high-frequency sequence components of text representations on different diffusion timestep schedules, since high frequencies carry token-level positional information.
9D0MMjtW7l.evidence: Spectral, reconstruction, and probing analyses across model families, sizes, layers, and domains, plus generation tests in the ELF framework (for example GSM8K per reviews).
9D0MMjtW7l.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the analysis is thorough and coherent across model families, scales, and domains, showing high-frequency bands carry positional token information, and that Haar Delay adds no parameters while giving gains in some settings.
9D0MMjtW7l.main_concern: The link between analysis and method is not directly shown: no frequency-specific reconstruction or position probes verify that Haar Delay enhances high-frequency information, the analysis uses Fourier bands while the method uses Haar, and the band analysis may be circular.

U8njWm68Kr.one_liner: Agents learn a persistent directed social graph through reward-modulated plasticity, reused for reward diffusion, experience sharing, and deliberation.
U8njWm68Kr.problem: Multi-agent coordination is usually specified per task by a fixed topology, dialogue protocol, or planner, leaving open with whom agents have a relationship.
U8njWm68Kr.method: Directed bonds evolve online: social co-activity makes a pair eligible and later outcomes consolidate or weaken the bond. The learned graph feeds back into learning through reward diffusion and bond-gated experience sharing, and into inference through social deliberation, tested in WIRE, a five-chamber embodied environment.
U8njWm68Kr.key_idea: Hebbian-style eligibility on co-activity, consolidated or weakened by later reward, builds a directed bond graph that gates reward diffusion and experience sharing.
U8njWm68Kr.evidence: Experiments in WIRE, a custom embodied environment with five chambers of increasing coordination demands, comparing RL fine-tuning, inference-time social deliberation versus a centralised orchestrator, and different social interaction regimes.
U8njWm68Kr.claimed_gains: With RL fine-tuning, relational coupling improves cooperative completion in three of four tested configurations, and at inference social plasticity matches a centralised orchestrator's cooperative completion with higher task return.
U8njWm68Kr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree an explicit, inspectable relationship state kept across episodes is an interesting design direction, and credit the paper for reporting failures alongside gains.
U8njWm68Kr.main_concern: Gains are not cleanly attributed: bonds may reflect interaction frequency rather than useful cooperation (communication gives the strongest bonds but poor cooperative completion), reward diffusion and experience sharing are not separated, and evaluation uses one custom environment.

WDa1GpOS5x.one_liner: Feed-forward 2DGS framework that constrains surfel orientation with calibrated normal supervision and propagates tangent-plane depth hypotheses.
WDa1GpOS5x.problem: Rendering-driven supervision leaves the geometry of feed-forward Gaussian primitives ambiguous, since geometric errors can be compensated by appearance parameters.
WDa1GpOS5x.method: Geometry-Calibrated Normal Supervision regularizes primitive orientations to reduce geometric drift. Confidence-Guided Tangent-Plane Depth Propagation turns reliable local orientations into surface-aligned depth hypotheses validated with multi-view geometric evidence.
WDa1GpOS5x.key_idea: Anchor surfel normals to calibrated geometry cues and convert confident normals into multi-view-validated tangent-plane depth hypotheses for global coherence.
WDa1GpOS5x.evidence: Surface reconstruction accuracy on DTU, with zero-shot evaluations on DTU, BlendedMVS, and ETH3D (reviews note BlendedMVS and ETH3D are shown only qualitatively).
WDa1GpOS5x.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the motivation clear and the normal-supervision and depth-propagation modules simple, complementary, and effective, with CoSplat outperforming compared feed-forward Gaussian methods.
WDa1GpOS5x.main_concern: Cross-dataset generalization is supported only qualitatively for BlendedMVS and ETH3D, with no quantitative metrics, so the generalization claim exceeds the evidence.

m440IhB0kZ.one_liner: Contrastive analysis in a frozen representation-autoencoder latent, with a diffusion transformer conditioned on salient factors for subtype generation.
m440IhB0kZ.problem: Contrastive analysis methods have not yielded salient target-specific representations that both reconstruct images well and reveal unlabeled subtypes to guide generation.
m440IhB0kZ.method: SAGE learns salient and common factors directly in the high-dimensional spatial latent of a frozen representation autoencoder, and conditions a diffusion transformer on the salient representation of a reference image. Discovered subtypes can then be inspected, removed, and transferred between images, including subtypes with no name or text description.
m440IhB0kZ.key_idea: Factorize a frozen RAE's spatial latent into salient (target-specific) and common (shared) factors using target and background datasets, then condition a diffusion transformer on the salient factor.
m440IhB0kZ.evidence: Digits-ImageNet, FFHQ eyeglasses, and retinal OCT, compared with contrastive-analysis baselines such as cVAE and a DINOv3 + SepCLR representation baseline, with loss ablations.
m440IhB0kZ.claimed_gains: rFID below 2; digit recovery probe accuracy 0.950 versus at most 0.281 for baselines; salient-conditioned subtype accuracy on Digits-ImageNet 90.5% versus 27.7% for the unfactorized latent; on retinal OCT the salient space separates three diseases using only normal/disease labels.
m440IhB0kZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree SAGE achieves factorization, reconstruction, and generation together, reveals subtypes and mislabeled images without subtype labels, and is backed by multiple qualitative and quantitative evaluations.
m440IhB0kZ.main_concern: Comparisons do not isolate the benefit of the factorization from the pretrained frozen RAE, since generative baselines are trained from scratch and DiffCA is not included as a baseline.

6nqFiXoKS3.one_liner: An audit of self-evolving memory systems finding unstable evaluation feedback, regression-prone edits, and non-accumulating repairs.
6nqFiXoKS3.problem: Self-evolving memory loops often improve early then plateau, and their assumptions that evaluation finds failures, edits repair them, and repairs persist are untested.
6nqFiXoKS3.method: The paper audits this three-link chain in several self-evolution methods on two conversational memory benchmarks, using question-level evidence independent of the agent and pairing each revision with its parent. It then extends MemPro with verified feedback, repair rounds, and paired acceptance.
6nqFiXoKS3.key_idea: Pair every revision with the parent it modifies and count repairs and regressions at question level, to test whether evaluation, edits, and persistence each hold.
6nqFiXoKS3.evidence: Several self-evolution methods audited on two conversational memory benchmarks, with reevaluation of unchanged systems, causal interventions on MemPro, and a judge swap.
6nqFiXoKS3.claimed_gains: Development accuracy rises by up to 16.9 percentage points after extending MemPro; held-out gains are not given in the available abstract text.
6nqFiXoKS3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the question-level, parent-paired audit of three clearly stated assumptions exposes effects that aggregate scores hide, and credit the authors for reporting negative results.
6nqFiXoKS3.main_concern: Causal wording outruns the intervention evidence, and the LLM judge may itself drive much of the reported instability without being separated from system variance.

4hJ82iauw9.one_liner: Block-wise streaming geometric foundation model with block-wise causal attention and confidence-aware KV-cache re-anchoring for long driving sequences.
4hJ82iauw9.problem: Applying feed-forward geometric models to long driving sequences is intractable because of GPU memory limits and quadratic global attention, while causal streaming drifts and chunk-then-align fragments context.
4hJ82iauw9.method: Block-wise causal attention keeps bidirectional context inside each block while propagating history across blocks through a KV cache. Confidence-aware re-anchoring detects unreliable streaming states, re-initializes the KV cache, and stitches the refreshed segments with SE(3) alignment.
4hJ82iauw9.key_idea: Attend bidirectionally within blocks and causally across them, and when confidence drops, reset the KV cache and align the new segment to the old one with an SE(3) transform.
4hJ82iauw9.evidence: Experiments on nuScenes, KITTI, and Waymo against baselines including DVGT-2, with ablations on reset policy and confidence threshold.
4hJ82iauw9.claimed_gains: On nuScenes, improves over the DVGT-2 baseline from 0.1806 to 0.1081 in AbsRel and from 0.6750 to 0.5344 in point-cloud Accuracy, plus a third metric whose result is truncated in the abstract.
4hJ82iauw9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the block-wise design suits multi-camera streaming reconstruction and that depth and point-cloud results on nuScenes and Waymo are strong.
4hJ82iauw9.main_concern: The components (block attention, KV caching, confidence reset, rigid alignment) are individually established, and SE(3) re-anchoring cannot correct scale drift while KITTI uses Sim(3)-aligned ATE.

bU6yZGeVpp.one_liner: FoveaTree prunes Video LLM visual tokens training-free using compressibility-guided regions and query-guided tree pruning.
bU6yZGeVpp.problem: Existing pruning ignores regional compressibility of frames and suffers attention drift from RoPE position effects, so task-relevant tokens get discarded.
bU6yZGeVpp.method: A first stage estimates regional compressibility from feature distortion when merging a region to build a tree, and a second stage prunes the tree with query-guided text-to-vision attention.
bU6yZGeVpp.key_idea: Build a per-frame quadtree from merge-induced feature distortion, then prune it with query-to-vision attention to avoid position-biased token selection.
bU6yZGeVpp.evidence: Reviews cite six benchmarks, four backbones, and three token budgets, with component ablations and latency and memory comparisons.
bU6yZGeVpp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the two-stage training-free design is well motivated and retains accuracy across benchmarks and backbones at low or comparable cost.
bU6yZGeVpp.main_concern: The design is heuristic with fixed, unablated hyperparameters (merge-gain threshold 0.005, per-backbone leaf cap) and lacks temporal modeling.

fISVPczlFi.one_liner: Builds betting-based sequential-test monitors that alarm when a single trajectory shows evidence of violating a supermartingale certificate.
fISVPczlFi.problem: Supermartingale certificates hold only within a mathematical model, so a sim-to-real gap can invalidate them on the deployed stochastic system.
fISVPczlFi.method: An algorithm constructs a monitor from one observed trajectory using betting-based sequential tests that bound the probability of ever raising a false alarm at a user-specified level, with strategies that exploit spatial regularity to improve detection power.
fISVPczlFi.key_idea: Treat certificate violation as a sequential hypothesis test with betting martingales, using bets that exploit spatial regularity to raise detection power while keeping the false-alarm guarantee.
fISVPczlFi.evidence: Supermartingale certificate benchmarks from the literature; per reviews, comparisons are mainly among configurations of the proposed method.
fISVPczlFi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem of connecting certificate guarantees to deployment is important and the approach is sound, with the spatial prediction strategy improving detection.
fISVPczlFi.main_concern: Experiments compare only variants of the same betting structure, without established sequential change-detection or risk-monitoring baselines, and novelty over existing betting-based testing is limited.

gBN64ic4T3.one_liner: Closed-loop NL-to-STL translation back-translates each formula to natural language so users can correct it without reading STL.
gBN64ic4T3.problem: One-shot, open-loop NL-to-STL translation hits an accuracy ceiling because natural language is ambiguous and the intended specification is not fully contained in the input text.
gBN64ic4T3.method: Each generated STL formula is translated back into natural language for the user to check, and natural-language corrections drive revision until the user accepts it. Users never read or write formal syntax.
gBN64ic4T3.key_idea: Close the translation loop with a structured STL-to-language feedback path, which is simpler than the forward path, so users can find and correct errors in plain language.
gBN64ic4T3.evidence: 500 expert-authored requirements and eight LLMs, with a blind fidelity audit and an expert check of accepted formulas per reviews.
gBN64ic4T3.claimed_gains: not stated; the TL;DR says specification correctness improves substantially, but the abstract excerpt gives no numbers.
gBN64ic4T3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the closed-loop reframing is well motivated and non-expert friendly, and that feedback explaining the mistake yields more correct formulas than a plain retry.
gBN64ic4T3.main_concern: User acceptance of a natural-language paraphrase does not prove formal correctness, and there is no baseline loop with self-explanation and checking to show what the workflow adds.

d5E2lwjO32.one_liner: Tests whether web agents pay for content access by completing verifiable tasks, finding they over-pay and ignore cost.
d5E2lwjO32.problem: AI agents return answers without sending users to the source, cutting content owners off from advertising revenue, and it is unclear how agents behave when access must be earned through work.
d5E2lwjO32.method: Agents earn access to content by completing verifiable tasks for the owner, such as writing code or labeling images, studied in controlled browser experiments with eight models and four agent implementations.
d5E2lwjO32.key_idea: Gate content behind verifiable work that is graded independently of the site's access decision, and measure whether agents track the cost of that work.
d5E2lwjO32.evidence: Controlled browser experiments with eight models and four agent implementations on locally hosted website templates with coding and image-labeling tasks, graded against LiveCodeBench private tests or GQA references per reviewers.
d5E2lwjO32.claimed_gains: Agents submit contributions in about 90% of runs, models stating a limit of about three tasks solve 32 problems to retrieve two identifiers, and one model produces responses judged harmful in about half of its agent runs.
d5E2lwjO32.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem setting is important and new, and that independent verification of submitted work and the gap between stated and actual behavior are useful findings.
d5E2lwjO32.main_concern: Reviewers say key conclusions rest on two of eight models and a controlled setup (ten local site templates, mainly coding and image labeling) that may not generalize, with scaffold and context limits confounding the cost-ignoring result.

HIll7SzkSu.one_liner: Self-distillation that limits predictive drift via a Hellinger-weighted loss and a Fisher-Rao penalty to a periodically refreshed student copy.
HIll7SzkSu.problem: In on-policy self-distillation with privileged context, matching a teacher that prefers continuations the student cannot infer induces predictive drift and degrades out-of-distribution reasoning.
HIll7SzkSu.method: GeoSD weights each teacher preference by student-teacher overlap (Hellinger loss) and adds a Fisher-Rao penalty against a periodically refreshed copy of the student. Both terms are optimized jointly with a natural-gradient-motivated preconditioner.
HIll7SzkSu.key_idea: Down-weight teacher preferences by student-teacher overlap and penalize Fisher-Rao distance to a periodically refreshed student copy, optimized with a natural-gradient-style preconditioner.
HIll7SzkSu.evidence: Three model families, five Qwen3 scales from 1.7B to 32B, mathematical OOD benchmarks and transfer to code generation, with component ablations and drift analyses.
HIll7SzkSu.claimed_gains: Improves average mathematical OOD accuracy by 5.7-8.6 points over the base model across three model families while retaining in-distribution gains; OOD gains hold from 1.7B to 32B.
HIll7SzkSu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the empirical evaluation is broad across model families and scales, the components are well motivated with ablations, and the drift analysis is insightful.
HIll7SzkSu.main_concern: Theoretical justification and novelty are weak (Hellinger, Fisher-Rao and K-FAC are established, and why the combination improves OOD is not explained), and the 'OOD' gains are mostly on near-OOD math.

xgUqnLFjzp.one_liner: Mixture-of-experts that reuses one layer-agnostic expert pool across layers to turn depth into 'virtual width' under a fixed activation budget.
xgUqnLFjzp.problem: MoE scaling is limited by physical depth and width, and naive recursive expert reuse causes routing-path explosion and breaks conventional load balancing.
xgUqnLFjzp.method: MoUE shares a universal expert pool across layers using a Staggered Rotational Topology, a Universal Expert Load Balance loss for depth-aware exposure, and a Universal Router with lightweight trajectory state. It can also convert existing MoE checkpoints progressively.
xgUqnLFjzp.key_idea: Share one expert pool across layers through a structured rotational topology and route with a trajectory-aware router, so depth multiplies reachable expert paths without more activated parameters.
xgUqnLFjzp.evidence: Pretraining of 160M and 700M backbones under width and depth expansion against matched MoE baselines, with ablations and conversion of an existing MoE checkpoint (JetMoE per a review).
xgUqnLFjzp.claimed_gains: Outperforms matched MoE baselines by up to 1.3% across scaling regimes and gives up to 4.2% gains when converting existing MoE checkpoints.
xgUqnLFjzp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree cross-layer expert reuse is an interesting, practical design with reasonable routing and load-balancing components and broad experiments, including adaptation of existing MoE models.
xgUqnLFjzp.main_concern: Novelty over looped or parameter-shared transformers and the meaning of 'virtual width' are questioned, and gains are modest (about +0.7 to +1.1 average) with depth scaling confounded by more activated parameters.

6FU81Yj3wT.one_liner: Maps Adam loss-spike behavior over the (beta1, beta2) plane and explains a linear boundary with superquadratic core-wall loss geometry.
6FU81Yj3wT.problem: How Adam's two momentum timescales govern macroscopic loss spikes is unclear, and a quadratic loss model predicts a different boundary than the one seen in practice.
6FU81Yj3wT.method: The authors map spiky versus non-spiky training across (beta1, beta2) in several model-task settings, find a near-linear boundary 1-beta2 = C(1-beta1), and show a one-dimensional loss proportional to |x|^n reproduces it. They argue confident cross-entropy gives a narrow quadratic core followed by a steep wall, i.e. effective superquadratic behavior at the scale of an update.
6FU81Yj3wT.key_idea: Loss spikes arise when momentum timescales mismatch finite-scale superquadratic loss geometry (a quadratic core plus steep wall), which sets a linear boundary in (1-beta1, 1-beta2).
6FU81Yj3wT.evidence: Empirical phase diagrams across six model-task settings (at most 9.7M parameters per a review), a one-dimensional toy analysis contrasting quadratic and superquadratic losses, and measured core-wall loss slices.
6FU81Yj3wT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the systematic mapping of the phase boundary across settings is a useful empirical finding and the core-wall picture is an intuitive, testable explanation beyond the Hessian.
6FU81Yj3wT.main_concern: The link between core-wall geometry and the neural-network boundary is empirically fitted rather than derived, and rests on one-dimensional slices and small models far from LLM-scale spikes.

H3kLkMylT8.one_liner: Shows fixed stable score filters, including momentum, keep the Polyak-Ruppert sandwich covariance, enabling one-pass online inference for nonsmooth scores.
H3kLkMylT8.problem: It is unclear when momentum, which changes transient SGD behavior, preserves the first-order statistical inference of averaged stochastic approximation, especially for nonsmooth or discontinuous scores.
H3kLkMylT8.method: A framework for fixed stable score filters (SGD, fixed preconditioning, scalar and coordinate momentum, higher-order filters) shows the filter gain cancels from the first-order influence function under local and trajectory conditions. It builds one-pass sandwich intervals, including an online Jacobian estimator for quantile regression, and path-based self-normalization.
H3kLkMylT8.key_idea: Under local and trajectory conditions, an exact change of variables makes the filter gain cancel from the influence function, so averaged estimators share the usual sandwich covariance.
H3kLkMylT8.evidence: Asymptotic theory assuming differentiable population means and local quadratic-mean continuity, with simulations in a least-squares setting (d=100) and online quantile regression coverage.
H3kLkMylT8.claimed_gains: Simulations show lower error for momentum in one least-squares setting with d=100, and online quantile coverage near the nominal level across the reported regular settings (no further numbers).
H3kLkMylT8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper gives a clean, unified mechanism (gain cancellation) and a coherent inference argument covering nonsmooth scores, including a feasible quantile-Jacobian construction.
H3kLkMylT8.main_concern: The key assumption (localization, mean-square rate, bounded filter-state moment, negligible nonlinear bias) is assumed rather than proved beyond scalar momentum, and the advance over prior online-inference results is seen as incremental.

IZ7SgoAgyI.one_liner: Latent reasoning that compresses only predictable reasoning spans via confidence gating, keeping precision-critical steps as explicit chain-of-thought.
IZ7SgoAgyI.problem: Existing latent reasoning methods treat all reasoning steps as equally compressible, over-compressing precision-critical steps and losing accuracy.
IZ7SgoAgyI.method: SLT uses a lightweight decoder to anticipate a short upcoming span and confidence-based gating to pick the longest span that can be compressed reliably, leaving the rest explicit. The compression policy is further optimized with trajectory-level RL balancing correctness against reasoning cost.
IZ7SgoAgyI.key_idea: A lightweight decoder predicts upcoming spans and a confidence gate compresses the longest reliable prefix into latents, with numerical and critical tokens kept explicit within one trajectory.
IZ7SgoAgyI.evidence: Four mathematical reasoning benchmarks across model sizes (including Qwen3-4B and Llama-3.2-1B), with ablations of span selection and the gate added to an existing latent reasoning model.
IZ7SgoAgyI.claimed_gains: Compressing arbitrary spans drops Qwen3-4B GSM-Hard accuracy from 54.7% to 17.3% while keeping numerical tokens explicit retains 51.8%; SLT reduces explicit reasoning length by 58.4% with a 2.8-point drop (abstract truncated).
IZ7SgoAgyI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that which spans are compressed matters, the selective-compression idea is intuitive and supported by ablations, and the gate also helps existing latent reasoning models.
IZ7SgoAgyI.main_concern: Closely related methods that mix latent and explicit reasoning are largely uncited or not compared, and some baselines are taken from prior work without multi-seed variance.

KF0hOh0YJU.one_liner: Single-stage pixel-space diffusion for radar nowcasting using masked asynchronous noising and a scoring-rule objective that enables few-step sampling.
KF0hOh0YJU.problem: Diffusion precipitation nowcasters depend on separately trained compression or deterministic components and are costly at inference because of iterative denoising.
KF0hOh0YJU.method: JWS forecasts directly in radar space with a hierarchical transformer, using Masked Asynchronous Diffusion (timestep sampling that keeps clean context) and a simple scoring-rule objective (a timestep-dependent interpolation of pixelwise CRPS and MSE) for few-step generation.
KF0hOh0YJU.key_idea: Train a radar-space diffusion model with clean-context asynchronous noise levels and a CRPS/MSE scoring-rule loss so few-step sampling yields calibrated probabilistic forecasts.
KF0hOh0YJU.evidence: SEVIR and MeteoNet benchmarks, with CRPS and SSIM results across model sizes, latency and FLOP analyses, and component ablations.
KF0hOh0YJU.claimed_gains: Reports leading probabilistic forecasting performance on SEVIR and MeteoNet at reduced training and inference cost; the smallest model stays competitive with substantially fewer parameters and more than 17x faster inference.
KF0hOh0YJU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the single-stage radar-space design is simple and well motivated, removes compression-induced uncertainty, and gives strong CRPS and SSIM with a good accuracy-latency trade-off.
KF0hOh0YJU.main_concern: The pixelwise CRPS/MSE objective does not constrain spatiotemporal dependence, so ensemble coherence is not established, and several components build on prior work including a concurrent anonymous submission.

OeGIbgwoJw.one_liner: Post-hoc topological abstraction of concept recoverability and interaction scores, edited to perform concept erasure, disentanglement and transfer.
OeGIbgwoJw.problem: Concept-editing methods are specialized to single interventions and offer no common, editable representation of how concepts in a learned representation are organized.
OeGIbgwoJw.method: Topological Concept Representations build an intermediate concept space from concept recoverability and interaction scores and encode its organization topologically (persistence diagram). Interventions edit this abstraction and are propagated back to the representation through a shared optimization framework.
OeGIbgwoJw.key_idea: Encode concept organization as a persistence diagram over recoverability and interaction scores, and implement interventions as edits to that diagram propagated back to the representation.
OeGIbgwoJw.evidence: Stability and reparameterization-invariance properties, disentanglement as preprocessing for seven erasure methods on four datasets, and teacher-to-student concept transfer.
OeGIbgwoJw.claimed_gains: Improves worst-group accuracy by 21.89 on average at comparable concept leakage when used before existing erasure methods, and improves concept recoverability by up to 5.54 in concept transfer.
OeGIbgwoJw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that a unified abstraction for concept-level interventions is well motivated and that worst-group accuracy gains over concept-erasure baselines are clear.
OeGIbgwoJw.main_concern: Clarity and justification are lacking: the problem is never formalized, the added value of the topological component is not isolated (for example no ablation without persistence), and concept transfer shows no clear advantage.

2rDXHBYR9W.one_liner: A lightweight selector decides which candidate step-label edits to apply to process reward model outputs, leaving the LM unchanged.
2rDXHBYR9W.problem: Process reward models miss errors or reject valid steps, and it is hard to decide which alternative judgments from other PRMs or critics improve a verifier's current predictions.
2rDXHBYR9W.method: Proposed error locations are converted into candidate step-label edits, and a lightweight selector trained on annotated reasoning traces decides which edits to apply, without changing the reasoning text or language-model weights.
2rDXHBYR9W.key_idea: Train the selector on an edit's effect on the verification metric, rather than on first-error correctness, to learn which candidate label edits to apply.
2rDXHBYR9W.evidence: PRMBench and an adapted DeltaBench task across multiple PRMs, comparing candidate sources (PRM scores versus critics) and selector targets.
2rDXHBYR9W.claimed_gains: Shows gains across multiple PRMs on PRMBench and an adapted DeltaBench task; no numbers in the abstract.
2rDXHBYR9W.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the experiments are carefully controlled and clear, and that first-error correctness alone can miss whether an edit improves step-level verification.
2rDXHBYR9W.main_concern: Most gains seem to come from a stronger reference PRM rather than the critics (simple baselines such as ensembling are missing), and the advantage of metric-aware selection is small and unclear on DeltaBench.

wc1mFO47j4.one_liner: Trains a coding agent with asynchronous PPO to use shell file operations as memory across four long-horizon environments.
wc1mFO47j4.problem: Memory control learned through predefined memory tools in short-horizon, domain-specific environments ties behavior to interfaces outside the base model's pretraining, so agents still struggle with memory on long-horizon tasks.
wc1mFO47j4.method: They introduce Coding Agent Memory Gym (CAMG), four long-horizon environments (Shop, Coding, DeepResearch, AutoResearch) with executable shell access and an episode-persistent workspace. CAMG-RL trains one policy jointly across them with fully asynchronous PPO from downstream task reward.
wc1mFO47j4.key_idea: Let the agent create, revise, search, and reuse files in a persistent workspace as memory, learning this behavior from task reward alone on top of pretrained file-operation skills.
wc1mFO47j4.evidence: CAMG-RL-4B and CAMG-RL-9B (from Qwen3.5) evaluated on SWE-bench Verified and MLE-bench Lite; reviewers cite memory-content interventions and paired confidence intervals.
wc1mFO47j4.claimed_gains: CAMG-RL-4B and CAMG-RL-9B are competitive with Qwen3.5-35B-A3B and Qwen3.5-122B-A10B, respectively, on SWE-bench Verified and MLE-bench Lite.
wc1mFO47j4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that eliciting memory behavior from pretrained file operations is interesting, the paper is clearly written, and the long-horizon environments are useful.
wc1mFO47j4.main_concern: The gains are not shown to come from learned memory: there is no same-environment RL baseline without a memory workspace, fairness against training-free memory baselines is questioned, and the environments supply heavy scaffolding.

EuZnUZZZra.one_liner: A VLM runs in parallel with an embodied policy, screens for failures, and intervenes with corrections only when needed.
EuZnUZZZra.problem: Embodied models trained on successful demonstrations do not recover from their own failures, and VLM-led systems that plan every step put the VLM on the critical path.
EuZnUZZZra.method: In Spotter the embodied model leads and executes continuously while a VLM runs in parallel, monitors through a lightweight local screener, intervenes only when an error is detected, reflects on and corrects it, and returns control.
EuZnUZZZra.key_idea: Reverse the usual roles: keep the embodied policy in control and have an asynchronous VLM monitor, reflect on detected failures, and issue corrective actions.
EuZnUZZZra.evidence: Experiments across multiple embodied policies and benchmarks, including beyond-simulator tests, with Qwen-based VLMs.
EuZnUZZZra.claimed_gains: Raises success at a fraction of the latency of LLM-led systems (per the TLDR); no numbers in the visible abstract.
EuZnUZZZra.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the parallel supervision design is sound and training-free, with a strong failure-recovery analysis and success-rate gains across several policies without large overhead.
EuZnUZZZra.main_concern: Ablations do not isolate each component (reflection versus longer history, synchronous versus asynchronous), and it is unclear how much the strong VLM rather than the embodied policy does the correcting, with no failure-detection recall or false-alarm rates.

ug4hB1le11.one_liner: Pixel-space diffusion with an implicit transformer denoiser that raises resolution along the sampling trajectory.
ug4hB1le11.problem: Pixel-space diffusion and flow models run every denoising step at full resolution even though early steps mainly establish coarse structure.
ug4hB1le11.method: CINDI trains an end-to-end implicit transformer denoiser with a next-scale bridge loss for in-scale and cross-scale prediction, paired with a coarse-to-fine sampler that needs no multi-model cascade or latent compression.
ug4hB1le11.key_idea: Schedule spatial resolution along the sampling trajectory, using coarse-grid evaluations early and one shared implicit denoiser trained to predict both the current and next resolution.
ug4hB1le11.evidence: Matched-budget comparison with the single-scale JiT baseline on ImageNet (model size, training epochs, and sampling steps held equal), a loss ablation on ImageNet 64, and a PixelFlow system comparison.
ug4hB1le11.claimed_gains: Competitive FID scores with up to a 3x speedup in inference throughput over the JiT baseline.
ug4hB1le11.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation is clear, the implicit denoiser avoids a pretrained autoencoder or cascaded models, and the efficiency gains under matched settings are practically useful.
ug4hB1le11.main_concern: The independent contribution of the implicit renderer is unclear, and positioning against related work (Pyramid Flow, Scale Space Diffusion, prior INR-diffusion work) is insufficient.

ftTPJquDN7.one_liner: Training-free correction of frozen DETR detections using horizontal-flip matching and nearest-center ownership slicing.
ftTPJquDN7.problem: Small objects occupy few visual tokens, so their localization is unstable under changes in view or spatial context.
ftTPJquDN7.method: FSCI matches same-class boxes between an image and its horizontal reflection to expose localization discrepancies and applies confidence-weighted box correction. It also slices the image and assigns each candidate to a unique slice by nearest-center ownership.
ftTPJquDN7.key_idea: Treat localization disagreement between an image and its flip as a correction signal, and assign sliced candidates by nearest-center ownership to avoid duplicates.
ftTPJquDN7.evidence: Seven frozen DETR-based detectors on COCO, TinyPerson, and VisDrone2019, plus controlled experiments on correction direction and spatial ownership.
ftTPJquDN7.claimed_gains: Improves overall and small-object AP in all 21 detector-dataset settings without updating model weights.
ftTPJquDN7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the training-free frozen-detector setting is practical and that AP improves consistently across detector and dataset settings with shared hyperparameters.
ftTPJquDN7.main_concern: Novelty is not established against SAHI, flip-based test-time augmentation, and Weighted Boxes Fusion because matched baselines are not run, and evaluation covers only older DETR variants with ResNet-50 and no APm or APl.

dY41knza1s.one_liner: Confidence sequences for federated M-estimation with Local SGD from a schedule-aware strong Gaussian approximation.
dY41knza1s.problem: Federated models are inspected or released repeatedly during training, so uncertainty quantification at a single fixed horizon is insufficient.
dY41knza1s.method: For the Polyak-Ruppert average of synchronized Local SGD iterates they prove an almost-sure Gaussian approximation that keeps the exact finite-schedule normalization and controls local drift and noise-freezing errors. They combine it with Gaussian time-uniform boundaries and a strongly consistent covariance estimator.
dY41knza1s.key_idea: An almost-sure Gaussian approximation that reflects total local computation and the communication-round variance clock, which yields time-uniform confidence sequences.
dY41knza1s.evidence: Theory (Gaussian approximation, a coverage corollary, fresh-sample sandwich estimator consistency) plus experiments on generalized linear models and a public-health dataset examining coverage, precision, and sensitivity to communication schedules.
dY41knza1s.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that valid inference under repeated monitoring matters and that the analysis, which keeps exact schedule normalization and controls local drift errors, is a useful contribution.
dY41knza1s.main_concern: The evaluated procedure does not match the theory: experiments use zero inflation (the theorem needs a positive value) and reuse training data for the covariance (the proof uses fresh samples), and one setting shows 11% pathwise failure against a nominal 5%.

AnSVg6D6pK.one_liner: Localizes RTL edits for natural-language change requests via semantic seeds and intent-conditioned propagation over typed dependency graphs.
AnSVg6D6pK.problem: Natural-language hardware change requests often touch multiple locations coupled by hardware dependencies, which independent request-to-code matching cannot recover.
AnSVg6D6pK.method: RTLocating fuses textual semantics, functional behavior, and architectural context into selective semantic seeds, then propagates intent-conditioned impact over directed, typed RTL dependencies with adaptive channel and scope selection, trained with counterfactual decision supervision. The authors also introduce EvoRTL-Bench from real RTL revisions.
AnSVg6D6pK.key_idea: Seed with fused semantic evidence, then spread impact along typed RTL dependency edges, with propagation choices supervised by the support-recovery utility of counterfactual alternatives.
AnSVg6D6pK.evidence: EvoRTL-Bench built from real RTL revisions (OpenTitan per reviewers) with an IP-disjoint split, plus an end-to-end RTL editing study.
AnSVg6D6pK.claimed_gains: Improves mean average precision by 17.3% relative to the strongest retriever baseline on EvoRTL-Bench, and its localization guidance improves downstream RTL editing.
