AnSVg6D6pK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark addresses a useful maintenance task with traceable labels from real revisions, and that ablations and editing results show the method helps.
AnSVg6D6pK.main_concern: Evidence is narrow: all data come from OpenTitan with one split (110 test queries), labels follow a single reference commit, and the editing study covers only 30 requests with best-of-up-to-four attempts.

W0wu5gEfrC.one_liner: Returns zero-variance GRPO query groups to a mutable pool for later resampling when training search agents.
W0wu5gEfrC.problem: In GRPO-style search-agent training, all-correct and all-incorrect groups are zero-variance and waste rollouts, and existing approaches discard or pre-filter them as if the property were static.
W0wu5gEfrC.method: Query recycling puts zero-variance groups back into a mutable pool for future resampling, so the effective training distribution co-evolves with the policy.
W0wu5gEfrC.key_idea: Zero-variance status changes as the policy evolves, so queries from zero-variance groups are recycled for later resampling instead of discarded, while queries that already contributed gradients are removed.
W0wu5gEfrC.evidence: A 4B model trained only on synthetic data and evaluated on seven multi-hop QA benchmarks, with analysis of recycling patterns; reviewers cite four model configurations over three backbone families against Bounded-DAPO.
W0wu5gEfrC.claimed_gains: A 4B model trained exclusively on synthetic data achieves 71.3 average Pass@1 across seven multi-hop QA benchmarks, and recycled queries supply roughly three quarters of the effective batch by the end of training.
W0wu5gEfrC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation is clear and the method is simple, with consistent gains over Bounded-DAPO under matched rollout budgets.
W0wu5gEfrC.main_concern: Novelty looks incremental (prior DAVID-GRPO already assumes failed groups can become solvable) and baselines are incomplete, with the outperforming claim omitting a same-backbone comparison row.

e7PAlA4pjo.one_liner: Structured pruning plus adaptive fine-tuning that confines PPG foundation models to a compact task-relevant parameter space.
e7PAlA4pjo.problem: PPG foundation models struggle to adapt to sparse, low-quality real-world data and do not consistently beat general-purpose time-series models even after full fine-tuning.
e7PAlA4pjo.method: SPAFT prunes using parameter importance and structural redundancy, then fine-tunes within the resulting compact, task-relevant parameter space. Reviewers add that filter importance is re-estimated after pruning.
e7PAlA4pjo.key_idea: Prune filters by combining task importance with structural redundancy, then fine-tune only the retained compact subnetwork, with importance re-estimated after pruning.
e7PAlA4pjo.evidence: Four PPG foundation models, five benchmark datasets, and ten downstream tasks, compared against multiple fine-tuning baselines.
e7PAlA4pjo.claimed_gains: SPAFT achieves win rates of 82.8% and a second figure that is cut off in the available abstract text.
e7PAlA4pjo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the study is thorough, with comparisons across four PPG foundation models and many fine-tuning paradigms, and find pruning before fine-tuning well motivated for redundant PPG data.
e7PAlA4pjo.main_concern: Novelty is limited because the core components are domain-agnostic and close to Less-is-More for general time series, and win rates over single-run, closely spaced results lack statistical tests.

eDLhiRu3Y2.one_liner: Training-free Quotient Attention shares key-value and query computation among similar-profile tokens in VGGT, keeping dense token representations.
eDLhiRu3Y2.problem: VGGT's global attention over all tokens makes compute and memory grow rapidly with the number of views, and existing acceleration reduces or merges tokens, which can alter token-specific interactions.
eDLhiRu3Y2.method: QuadVGGT selects original token representatives from sparse operator-induced profiles so that tokens with similar attention interactions share key-value and query computation without merging their representations. It adds scene-adaptive anchor construction and hierarchical feature offloading for long sequences.
eDLhiRu3Y2.key_idea: Separate representational redundancy from computational redundancy: share attention computation among tokens with similar operator-induced profiles via representatives, without merging their representations.
eDLhiRu3Y2.evidence: Applied to pretrained VGGT without training; reviewers cite experiments up to 1000 frames, several reconstruction tasks, and application to other geometric foundation models such as DA3 and pi3.
eDLhiRu3Y2.claimed_gains: No numbers in the available abstract text; a reviewer reports up to 14.8x faster inference than VGGT in the 1000 frames setting with competitive accuracy.
eDLhiRu3Y2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is well motivated, training-free, and effective, with jointly reduced key-value and query computation, preserved dense tokens, and extensive experiments.
eDLhiRu3Y2.main_concern: The novelty of the anchor construction and feature offloading is questioned, and the long-sequence tests use mostly densely sampled sequences with small inter-frame motion, while Delta-Walking is inefficient on shuffled inputs.

VW2Yt9hNvc.one_liner: Learns gated per-factor position, size, and orientation corrections on a scene graph, injected into diffusion denoising for indoor layouts.
VW2Yt9hNvc.problem: Diffusion-generated indoor scenes still contain collisions, boundary violations, scale inconsistencies, and obstructed paths, and predefined physics guidance adapts poorly to evolving scene states while joint attribute updates interfere with each other.
VW2Yt9hNvc.method: The framework builds a multi-relational semantic-geometric scene graph, fuses semantic and direction-aware geometric context, and predicts gated corrections for position, size, and orientation through factor-aware branches. Counterfactual perturbations supervise the predictor, and its corrections are injected into diffusion posterior updates during denoising.
VW2Yt9hNvc.key_idea: Replace predefined physical guidance with a learned, state-dependent correction predictor that has separate gated branches per attribute and is trained to undo counterfactual perturbations.
VW2Yt9hNvc.evidence: Experiments reported on 3D-FRONT across three room types (per reviewers), with encoder and factor-aware correction ablations and comparisons to PhyScene.
VW2Yt9hNvc.claimed_gains: Reports leading layout fidelity and collision reduction; no numbers in the abstract.
VW2Yt9hNvc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that replacing hand-crafted guidance with a learned, factor-aware correction applied during denoising is sensible and that the paper is detailed and reproducible, with consistent but modest FID gains.
VW2Yt9hNvc.main_concern: Physical gains are small (collision rates improve over PhyScene by only 1 to 3 points, boundary results are mixed), no seeds or variance are reported, and baselines such as backbone-only or post-hoc optimization are missing.

omUhn1v0bs.one_liner: Cost-aware prover: symbolic goal selection over two-level proof graphs, plus an agentic router that prices specialist invocations.
omUhn1v0bs.problem: Existing provers chase pass rates at any sampling or search budget and ignore the success-versus-cost frontier, although real software has hundreds of interdependent proof obligations.
omUhn1v0bs.method: CoCo-Prover joins an AND/OR proof hypergraph within each declaration to a lemma-dependency graph across declarations. Goal selection is a symbolic topological pass, and an agentic router treats each bounded specialist invocation as a separately priced computation, matching specialists and configurations under routing rules that evolve with evidence.
omUhn1v0bs.key_idea: Frame proving as metalevel decision-making under cost: symbolic goal selection on two-level proof graphs, and routing among priced specialist agents with rules that evolve as evidence accumulates.
omUhn1v0bs.evidence: Five program verification benchmarks per the abstract (text cut off); reviewers cite the Vero benchmark and ablations on adaptive routing and lemma reuse.
omUhn1v0bs.claimed_gains: No numbers in the available abstract text; a reviewer cites Gemini solving 26 of 43 Vero tasks compared with 3 for a coding agent.
omUhn1v0bs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that cost efficiency is an important, underexplored goal and that persistent proof state, lemma reuse, and adaptive routing form a coherent pipeline with supporting ablations.
omUhn1v0bs.main_concern: Cost evidence and baselines are incomplete: cost is compared only on commonly solved problems, the router ablation uses one fixed specialist order, and relevant provers such as Goedel-Code-Prover are missing.

sQHRHjOQ7m.one_liner: Discovers fMRI activity patterns via unsupervised decomposition and explains each with automatically scored descriptions of top-eliciting images.
sQHRHjOQ7m.problem: Studies of visual representation in the human brain are mostly small-scale, rely on manual inspection, focus on specific regions and concepts, and rarely validate systematically.
sQHRHjOQ7m.method: BrainExplore first discovers candidate patterns in fMRI activity with unsupervised, data-driven decomposition. It then explains each pattern by finding the natural images that most strongly elicit it and generating a language description, using an automated pipeline that tests multiple candidate explanations and assigns reliability scores.
sQHRHjOQ7m.key_idea: Decompose fMRI into candidate patterns, then choose each pattern's description by scoring several candidate natural-language explanations of its top-activating images.
sQHRHjOQ7m.evidence: fMRI visual responses (NSD per reviewers) with several decomposition methods, sparse autoencoders among them, plus appendix validation including cross-subject and cross-dataset checks and ablations.
sQHRHjOQ7m.claimed_gains: Reveals thousands of interpretable patterns spanning many distinct visual concepts, including fine-grained representations beyond well-established categories.
sQHRHjOQ7m.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is valuable for AI-for-neuroscience and credit the scale, the systematic comparison of decomposition methods, and the extensive appendix.
sQHRHjOQ7m.main_concern: The difference from prior automated fMRI explanation work (BrainSCUBA, LaVCa, BrainDIVE) is not clearly stated, and validity lacks closed-loop stimulus experiments and rests on 16 images per concept and predicted fMRI.

y5WiK71CrM.one_liner: Query-agnostic KV eviction scoring cached keys by approximating reconstruction attention in a single prefill, without extra passes.
y5WiK71CrM.problem: KV caches grow with context length, and estimating which KV pairs preserve answer quality for unknown future queries is expensive for long contexts.
y5WiK71CrM.method: RECAP-KV applies the model's existing Q/K projections and normalization to attention-input states captured during prefill, with rotary embeddings at virtual positions, to approximate the attention cached keys would receive during context reconstruction. It allocates the budget across layers, heads, and context blocks and refines token selection with Lookback Reranking.
y5WiK71CrM.key_idea: Approximate reconstruction-attention importance from prefill states using existing Q/K projections and virtual RoPE positions, avoiding an extra transformer pass or a learned importance predictor.
y5WiK71CrM.evidence: 12 tasks and 6 models from the Qwen, Llama, and GPT-OSS families at multiple retention levels, plus a vLLM prototype and component ablations.
y5WiK71CrM.claimed_gains: Best or near-best mean task scores among query-agnostic methods at 15% and 30% KV (the rest of the sentence is cut off in the available abstract).
y5WiK71CrM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it avoids a trained importance predictor, spans many tasks and model types, and takes less prefill time than KVZip at the same compression.
y5WiK71CrM.main_concern: The cost-benefit is not fully shown: there is no end-to-end serving evaluation, scoring adds overhead (22.7 s versus 9.8 s for ordinary prefill at 128K), and ablations do not separate the estimator from budget allocation.

dMqt8eh5Ch.one_liner: Derives Gaussian, Gaussian-Laplace, and Laplace limits for private rank-based quantiles and a Gaussianizing one-step correction.
dMqt8eh5Ch.problem: Valid private quantile inference needs the joint distribution of sampling error and privacy noise, which was not characterized for the rank exponential mechanism.
dMqt8eh5Ch.method: They characterize the rank exponential mechanism's error distribution as the privacy level shrinks and build feasible intervals using neighboring private quantiles to estimate the local scale. A one-step correction adds Gaussian noise to a bounded quantile score to give a Gaussian pivot under approximate differential privacy.
dMqt8eh5Ch.key_idea: Add Gaussian noise to a bounded quantile score in a one-step correction so the privacy-noise error becomes Gaussian at every relative noise level.
dMqt8eh5Ch.evidence: Asymptotic theorems for the phase laws and pivots, plus simulations of the phase laws, public range, and budget allocation; reviewers note comparisons of interval width to prior methods.
dMqt8eh5Ch.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the phase-transition characterization of sampling versus privacy error is informative and the Gaussianization correction is interesting, with simulations supporting the theory.
dMqt8eh5Ch.main_concern: The empirical evaluation is thin: no direct comparison with prior methods (for example Drechsler et al. and Lalanne et al.), little on compute cost or small-sample behavior, and sensitivity to the assumed public range.

xdEmJQtBKQ.one_liner: Benchmarks LLM agents using packaged embodied skills on LIBERO-Pro tasks across native, skill-only, and agent-directed reuse modes.
xdEmJQtBKQ.problem: VLA policies, perception models, and procedural know-how differ in interfaces, embodiment assumptions, and conditions of use, so agents struggle to reuse them and their benefit on physical tasks is unmeasured.
xdEmJQtBKQ.method: They package such modules as embodied skills with explicit embodiment assumptions and conditions of use, and build a repository of 250 skills from 1,052 existing resources. Agents run in a closed observation-action loop under native control, skill-only execution, or Agent-Directed Reuse (ADR), where the agent decides per skill whether to invoke, modify, or ignore it.
xdEmJQtBKQ.key_idea: Agent-Directed Reuse: the agent keeps its native controls and decides per skill whether to invoke, modify, or ignore it, while success, actions, tokens, and time are recorded.
xdEmJQtBKQ.evidence: Four agents on 100 perturbed LIBERO-Pro tasks in three modes, recording success, actions, tokens, and wall-clock time.
xdEmJQtBKQ.claimed_gains: Skill-only execution lifts GPT-5.6-Sol from 11% to 63% and Kimi-K3 and Claude-Opus-5 by about 20 points while cutting token usage by 58% to 85%, yet all four agents end between 61% and 64%.
xdEmJQtBKQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark gives a useful common setting for comparing skill reuse across agents, and find it interesting that skills help weaker agents but can constrain stronger ones.
xdEmJQtBKQ.main_concern: Novelty and rigor are questioned: the skill concept and extraction appear in prior work, results come from one simulator, embodiment, and seed without uncertainty estimates, and the skill abstraction's own value is not isolated.

YL5oma2FkD.one_liner: Builds an orthogonal atom dictionary from knowledge-induced gradients and uses sparse addressing to edit or unlearn knowledge.
YL5oma2FkD.problem: In knowledge editing and unlearning, different knowledge items share overlapping parameters or representational directions, causing unintended interference.
YL5oma2FkD.method: KEY builds an orthogonal atom dictionary from knowledge-induced gradients by decomposing their input- and output-side directions. It then performs sparse addressing to pick a compact set of atoms and coefficients for each update, with global and local proximity bounds as theory.
YL5oma2FkD.key_idea: Decompose gradients into an orthogonal dictionary of input and output atoms, and update knowledge through sparse coefficients over a few atoms so items are separated in weight space.
YL5oma2FkD.evidence: Knowledge editing and unlearning experiments on multiple backbones and benchmarks (reviewers cite CounterFact and TOFU), plus proximity-bound theory and coefficient analysis.
YL5oma2FkD.claimed_gains: Consistently competitive performance against recent baselines with more interpretable and disentangled updating; no numbers in the abstract.
YL5oma2FkD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that casting editing and unlearning as sparse addressing over a shared dictionary is a well-motivated, interpretable framing with competitive results on locality and retention.
YL5oma2FkD.main_concern: Practicality and fairness are questioned: baseline numbers are copied from original papers, the method depends on a global knowledge pool and retained set (the ablation shows large drops without them), and sequential or batch editing is not evaluated.

fxBZQywtau.one_liner: Multimodal model merging that traces cross-layer expert influence on graphs and jointly selects regional merging weights.
fxBZQywtau.problem: Layer-wise merging ignores that merging one layer changes downstream representations and visual-textual interaction, making expert influence across depth hard to trace and merging weights hard to select jointly.
fxBZQywtau.method: TAC-Merge's multimodal influence mapping builds graphs that trace expert influence across depth and separate responses to image and instruction changes, using a shared objective of Ricci curvature matching plus prediction agreement. Coupled merge control then finds a compact subspace and fits a local quadratic model of weight interactions to select regional weights jointly.
fxBZQywtau.key_idea: Select merge weights jointly across regions with a local quadratic interaction model, guided by a curvature-matching objective on influence graphs built from image and instruction perturbations.
fxBZQywtau.evidence: Diverse multimodal tasks on two backbones (Qwen3.5-4B and Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct per reviewers), including unseen tasks, with ablations of the curvature objective, graph structure, response basis, and quadratic coupling.
fxBZQywtau.claimed_gains: Demonstrates effectiveness across diverse multimodal tasks and generalization to unseen tasks; no numbers in the abstract.
fxBZQywtau.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is practical and that consistent improvements over merging baselines, together with ablations, support the cross-layer influence modeling and joint weight optimization.
fxBZQywtau.main_concern: Computational cost is unreported (wall-clock time, memory), the benefit of Ricci curvature matching and coupled optimization is modest or unexplained, and baseline coverage (Expert Merging) and implementation details are insufficient.

nWsa8VDtls.one_liner: One-pass multiplier bootstrap for Polyak-Ruppert averaged stochastic approximation with fixed momentum or dynamic preconditioning.
nWsa8VDtls.problem: Online inference for averaged stochastic approximation with momentum or evolving preconditioners lacks a one-pass method that avoids explicit covariance estimation and handles nonsmooth problems.
nWsa8VDtls.method: Weighted replicas are updated alongside the original recursion. With fixed momentum and preconditioning the first-order influence function is unchanged, and with dynamic preconditioning replicas can reuse the original preconditioner sequence or keep their own curvature states.
nWsa8VDtls.key_idea: Run multiplier-weighted replicas of the recursion in one pass, and show momentum and an evolving preconditioner are first-order negligible so replicas can share the original preconditioner.
nWsa8VDtls.evidence: Theory under mean and score regularity and rate conditions, plus experiments with momentum, dynamic preconditioning, and correlated Gaussian settings; reviewers mention logistic and quantile regression examples.
nWsa8VDtls.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the theory is careful and extends online bootstrap inference to momentum and dynamic preconditioning, with the useful result that replicas can reuse the original preconditioner to cut storage and computation.
nWsa8VDtls.main_concern: Key conditions, such as mean-square rate assumptions for the original and weighted recursions, are assumed rather than verified for the logistic and quantile regression examples, and the paper is hard to read.

KPtLLFIZcs.one_liner: Jointly trains instance-specific rubric generation and rubric-conditioned scoring in one policy with RL and distributional rewards.
KPtLLFIZcs.problem: Judge-training methods leave per-instance evaluation criteria implicit, while rubric-guided approaches optimize rubric generation separately from downstream judging.
KPtLLFIZcs.method: RubricRL uses downstream judging performance to optimize instance-specific rubrics and uses the learned rubrics to guide score prediction within a shared policy model. It adds a distributional second-moment reward for absolute scoring and a distributional pairwise score-gap reward for relative scoring.
KPtLLFIZcs.key_idea: Alternately optimize rubric generation and rubric-conditioned judging in one shared policy, rewarding rubrics by the downstream judge's scoring accuracy.
KPtLLFIZcs.evidence: Experiments across diverse backbones and benchmarks, including a cumulative ablation and a fixed-judge experiment that isolates the value of learned rubrics.
KPtLLFIZcs.claimed_gains: Consistently improves LLM judging, is competitive with strong closed-source LLMs, and yields rubrics whose judging performance is comparable to human-validated criteria; no numbers in the abstract.
KPtLLFIZcs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the coupled rubric-and-judge design is well motivated and that the cumulative ablation and fixed-judge experiment show learned rubrics add value.
KPtLLFIZcs.main_concern: Supervision comes from GPT-4-derived scores rather than direct human ratings, so annotator errors may be inherited, and reward hacking through the shared rubric and judge policy is not ruled out.

0CH2ORSgBt.one_liner: Offline safe RL with a budget-conditioned flow policy trained on constraint-reweighted action targets and an adaptive budget guide.
0CH2ORSgBt.problem: Offline safe RL datasets may contain no complete trajectory within the deployment cost budget, and bootstrapped cost estimates can miss delayed costs visible only in recorded subtrajectories.
0CH2ORSgBt.method: FIBA-Flow scores each candidate action by combining a cost-to-go estimate with a short-horizon cumulative-cost prediction, optimizes target action probabilities for entropy-regularized return under a remaining-budget constraint, and trains a budget-conditioned flow to match them in one step. A guide learns to adjust the flow's internal budget input.
0CH2ORSgBt.key_idea: Combine cost-to-go with short-horizon cumulative-cost prediction to score actions, reweight targets under the remaining budget, and learn a guide that adjusts the flow's internal budget input.
0CH2ORSgBt.evidence: 38 DSRL tasks, with reviewers highlighting results on MetaDrive.
0CH2ORSgBt.claimed_gains: Satisfies the cost constraint on every one of 38 DSRL tasks and achieves the highest normalized return on 25 tasks among budget-compliant methods.
0CH2ORSgBt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that learning without budget-compliant trajectories is practically relevant and that the method is sound with comprehensive experiments.
0CH2ORSgBt.main_concern: Setting realism and fairness are questioned: the dataset without compliant trajectories is constructed artificially, model selection and tuning for baselines are unclear, and C2IQL and BCRL are omitted from the comparison.

gDRLZbhBji.one_liner: Online covariance estimators and Wald regions for Polyak-Ruppert averages of inexact Riemannian Newton iterates.
gDRLZbhBji.problem: Statistical inference for inexact Newton iterates on Riemannian manifolds must account for observation noise, solver randomization, and accumulated implementation bias.
gDRLZbhBji.method: A local asymptotic representation separates observation noise, solver randomization, and implementation bias, giving one-pass covariance estimators and asymptotically valid Wald regions. Independent fresh solves add a positive semidefinite term to the score-sandwich covariance, and averaging solver replicas shrinks it in inverse proportion to their number.
gDRLZbhBji.key_idea: Keep solver randomness in the covariance: fresh solves add a positive semidefinite term that shrinks with replica count, while slowly varying predictable gains cancel at first order.
gDRLZbhBji.evidence: Theory plus product-torus simulations and intrinsic-mean and principal-subspace applications with a streaming illustration (a WDBC application per reviewers).
gDRLZbhBji.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the covariance decomposition is a coherent inferential theory that does not require solver randomness to vanish and tells practitioners which covariance to report.
gDRLZbhBji.main_concern: The theory depends on strong local assumptions (an invariant basin, rate and averaging conditions) that are hard to verify, and validation is narrow, covering a product torus and one WDBC application.

aRusjdsuZg.one_liner: Bilingual benchmark of 12,207 multi-image financial document samples for evaluating large multimodal model reasoning.
aRusjdsuZg.problem: Existing financial multimodal benchmarks focus on isolated charts and overlook integrating data from text, tables, and images across financial documents.
aRusjdsuZg.method: A semi-automated pipeline combining Visual-Centric Generation with Expert Verification builds 12,207 samples from 2,878 financial reports across twelve domains and five task types, to test multi-image processing and document-level understanding.
aRusjdsuZg.key_idea: Generate questions that need visual evidence from multi-page reports and verify them with experts, to minimize text bias and test document-level, cross-page grounding.
aRusjdsuZg.evidence: Eleven LMMs evaluated on the benchmark, with human-expert comparison and error analysis.
aRusjdsuZg.claimed_gains: No model among the eleven LMMs surpasses an overall score of 65.
aRusjdsuZg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark is a useful, carefully verified resource that tests full financial documents rather than isolated charts, with a broad model evaluation.
aRusjdsuZg.main_concern: Evaluation reliability is questioned: numerical-estimation references come from Gemini then expert verification with a 5% tolerance while human experts reach only about 63%, and the error analysis is generic.

FCqFtIK9JY.one_liner: Maintains typed execution-state nodes with links to raw observations as agent memory, updated incrementally and revealed on demand.
FCqFtIK9JY.problem: Long-horizon LLM agents either pay for full-history context or lose details needed later when compressing, and the relevance of past information often appears only as the task progresses.
FCqFtIK9JY.method: FlowState preserves semantically typed state nodes, their relations, and references to raw tool observations, separating persistent retention from on-demand access. Incremental State Update maintains the current state from new inputs and feedback, and Progressive State Access reveals historical states and supporting evidence as needed.
FCqFtIK9JY.key_idea: Treat execution state as memory: retain everything persistently but expose an index, letting the agent progressively expand historical states and evidence during reasoning.
FCqFtIK9JY.evidence: MemoryArena and tau^3-Bench with DeepSeek-V4-Flash against a full-context baseline, plus other memory baselines and three models for the full-context comparison per reviewers.
FCqFtIK9JY.claimed_gains: Versus a full-context baseline with DeepSeek-V4-Flash, improves average success rate on MemoryArena by 7.26 and average pass rate on tau^3-Bench by 15.91 percentage points while reducing total token consumption (amount cut off in the abstract text).
FCqFtIK9JY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the typed-state design with on-demand access is clear and well motivated, and that it improves accuracy and token cost together over relevant baselines.
FCqFtIK9JY.main_concern: Reliability and attribution are unclear: some success-rate gains rest on a few extra tasks without repeated runs, FlowState uses a longer engineered prompt than baselines, and ablations and scalability beyond one model are limited.

KdC9nAuT5q.one_liner: Martingale MMD two-sample tests on compact manifolds with diffusion kernels and chi-square calibration for singular covariance.
KdC9nAuT5q.problem: Two-sample testing on manifolds needs geometry-respecting kernels that are sensitive at unknown scales, but diffusion smoothing attenuates signal and noise and neighboring scales give redundant tests.
KdC9nAuT5q.method: Within martingale MMD testing, an exact spectral criterion shows extra diffusion helps when the average null-noise frequency exceeds the average signal frequency. For a fixed grid of scales, thresholding the covariance pseudoinverse gives an asymptotic chi-square null limit with estimated positive rank.
KdC9nAuT5q.key_idea: Compare average null-noise and signal frequencies to decide when more diffusion helps, and threshold the covariance pseudoinverse to calibrate a multiscale statistic without resampling.
KdC9nAuT5q.evidence: Theory plus simulations on the circle, torus, and sphere, a matched torus runtime comparison (MMD-FUSE with 199 permutations per a reviewer), and a pigeon example.
KdC9nAuT5q.claimed_gains: Simulations support the predicted frequency dependence and conservative-to-near-nominal size, and the resampling-free calculation can improve detection by processing more observations in similar time; no numbers in the abstract.
KdC9nAuT5q.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the spectral efficiency criterion clearly explains when smoothing helps and the singular-covariance treatment is carefully formulated, with experiments reporting both advantages and limitations.
KdC9nAuT5q.main_concern: The advance is narrower than a new framework (Chatterjee and Ramdas already give multi-kernel mMMD with chi-square calibration), practical comparisons are limited, and results are sensitive to threshold and kernel scaling.

2rFN9LiyVH.one_liner: Shows KV-cache reuse evaluations overstate accuracy and proposes a cleaner evaluation methodology plus the Boxoffice dataset generator.
2rFN9LiyVH.problem: Evaluations of position-independent KV cache reuse use measurements that fail to capture the accuracy loss caused by reuse, and existing datasets lack the reuse dynamics needed for thorough evaluation.
2rFN9LiyVH.method: They propose an evaluation methodology that measures the accuracy loss attributable to reuse without ambiguity, and introduce Boxoffice, a tool that programmatically generates datasets exercising challenging KV cache reuse patterns.
2rFN9LiyVH.key_idea: Measure accuracy loss attributable to reuse against full prefill, and generate datasets programmatically with controlled chunk-reuse patterns such as cache staleness.
2rFN9LiyVH.evidence: Re-examination of existing reuse techniques on MuSiQue, HotpotQA, and 2WikiMQA, plus datasets generated with Boxoffice.
2rFN9LiyVH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it identifies real limitations of current KV-cache reuse benchmarks and is well motivated, clearly written, and insightful.
2rFN9LiyVH.main_concern: Related benchmarks (for example SCBench and KV-Repurpose) are not discussed, the 'inflation' framing and the modified CacheCraft variant are questioned, and generality beyond three multi-hop QA datasets is unclear.

ua3BJXLihb.one_liner: Neural operators that learn local symmetries and inter-region frame alignment, with a soft projection onto a cross-region weight-sharing space.
ua3BJXLihb.problem: Equivariant networks assume a known, globally consistent group action, but in heterogeneous materials and around defects symmetries and frames vary by region and loops can have nontrivial holonomy.
ua3BJXLihb.method: From multiple input-output observations of one operator, SDNO learns feature transformations shared within each local region and the alignment between neighboring regions. These constraints define a cross-region weight-sharing space onto which trainable weights are softly projected, with curvature and holonomy representing local defects and global topology.
ua3BJXLihb.key_idea: Treat local symmetries and frame alignment as episode-conditioned structure learned from operator observations, and softly project weights onto the cross-region sharing space they define.
ua3BJXLihb.evidence: Theory on global compatibility, approximate descent, and local-symmetry recovery under a spectral gap, plus experiments with local transport under U(1) and a noncommutative special unitary group.
ua3BJXLihb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem of local-to-global consistency of equivariance is significant and that the framework, with its theoretical guarantees, is interesting.
ua3BJXLihb.main_concern: The paper is hard to follow and depends on many assumptions (multiple observations per operator, Jacobians, a spectral gap), with comparisons to related methods such as AtlasD missing.

i8EYk6MFyR.one_liner: Benchmark for generating runnable multi-route web apps from screenshots, scoring executability, visual fidelity, and inferred interactions.
i8EYk6MFyR.problem: Screenshot-to-code benchmarks measure visual fidelity but not whether models infer interactive behavior from screenshots alone.
i8EYk6MFyR.method: UI2App has 600 screenshots grouped into 95 state-coherent sets for multi-route web applications, and an end-to-end pipeline scoring executability, visual fidelity, and interaction inference. The interaction metric (IIS) credits any valid implementation by functional correctness and state-management complexity.
i8EYk6MFyR.key_idea: Score inferred interactions against a reference interaction inventory in an implementation-agnostic way, crediting any valid implementation rather than matching a single reference.
i8EYk6MFyR.evidence: Six frontier vision-language models evaluated on 600 screenshots in 95 sets, with human validation of the automated IIS (81.8% outcome agreement per a reviewer).
i8EYk6MFyR.claimed_gains: Reports a marked capability mismatch between visual reconstruction and interaction realization across six models; no numbers in the visible abstract text.
i8EYk6MFyR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark fills a real gap by evaluating interaction inference across routes, and note the large gap between visual similarity and working interactions.
i8EYk6MFyR.main_concern: The IIS metric is judged by an LLM reading code and static screenshots rather than executing interactions, with only 81.8% agreement with humans, and expected interactions are underdetermined by screenshots.

cMvo0h2gku.one_liner: Octree flow model that generates 3D molecules coarse-to-fine, resolving sparse occupancy, then atom types and in-cell offsets.
cMvo0h2gku.problem: Atom-based diffusion and flow models generate largely at a single scale and dense spatial fields become costly at high resolution, while molecules need both global shape and fine local precision.
cMvo0h2gku.method: A hierarchical occupancy flow progressively resolves sparse molecular support from coarse to fine on an octree, and a joint atom flow assigns atom types and continuous in-cell offsets to occupied leaves. Cell corruption improves robustness to generated support.
cMvo0h2gku.key_idea: Decompose generation into a coarse-to-fine octree occupancy flow and a joint atom flow for type and subcell offset, exposing intermediate occupancy states for spatial conditioning.
cMvo0h2gku.evidence: QM9 and GEOM-DRUG against baselines including Uni-3DAR, a dense-versus-octree efficiency comparison, and conditioning tasks such as shape conditioning, regional editing, linker generation, and interpolation.
cMvo0h2gku.claimed_gains: Strong chemical, distributional, and geometric quality on QM9 and GEOM-DRUG, with particularly clear gains over Uni-3DAR on GEOM-DRUG and substantial efficiency gains over dense 3D generation; no numbers in the abstract.
cMvo0h2gku.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the octree decomposition is intuitive and clearly presented, and that the gain over Uni-3DAR on GEOM-DRUG is substantial.
cMvo0h2gku.main_concern: Baselines are insufficient (SemlaFlow and TABASCO are discussed but not compared) and the ablations do not isolate whether gains come from flow matching, the octree, or the decoder.

sMkVNn6BAg.one_liner: CLT and Wald inference for full-participation Riemannian federated averaging with growing communication intervals.
sMkVNn6BAg.problem: Inference under infrequent communication in Riemannian federated averaging requires client drift and geometric error to be controlled at the scale of all local observations.
sMkVNn6BAg.method: A moment-sensitive synchronized-state bound makes drift and geometric errors negligible and gives a CLT for a computable fixed-anchor average in a regular local basin. Fresh pooled scores and exact or sample-based Hessians consistently estimate the covariance, giving feasible Wald regions.
sMkVNn6BAg.key_idea: A refined synchronized-state error bound lets communication intervals grow slowly while preserving first-order precision, so the CLT covariance separates the Hessian, client noise, and communication schedule.
sMkVNn6BAg.evidence: Theory plus Gaussian and sphere experiments at matched total oracle budgets against a fixed-interval baseline, and a four-site principal-subspace application.
sMkVNn6BAg.claimed_gains: A prespecified half-tail schedule attains near-nominal coverage with substantially lower communication cost than a fixed-interval baseline, at the cost of a larger uncertainty scale; no numbers in the abstract.
sMkVNn6BAg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the refined state-error bound, which permits growing communication intervals and controls drift at the total-observation scale, is a meaningful technical contribution with feasible inference.
sMkVNn6BAg.main_concern: The guarantees assume iterates stay in a small neighborhood after burn-in, which is not established for the unmodified recursion with unbounded noise, and the communication comparison changes several settings at once.

uh426x3DWx.one_liner: Single-codebook universal audio codec built by quantizing intermediate Qwen3-Omni AuT encoder representations at 13 to 52 Hz.
uh426x3DWx.problem: Multi-codebook neural audio codecs raise token rates or need specialized prediction or multi-stage decoding, and existing single-codebook codecs have largely focused on speech.
uh426x3DWx.method: UFC quantizes intermediate representations of the Qwen3-Omni Audio Transformer encoder into one discrete token stream for 16 kHz speech, music, and sound. Variants run at frame rates from 13 to 52 Hz, corresponding to 0.195 to 0.780 kbps.
uh426x3DWx.key_idea: Reuse an audio language model's own encoder (early AuT layers) as the codec encoder and quantize it into a single codebook, following the FocalCodec design.
uh426x3DWx.evidence: Evaluations across speech, music, and sound with multiple metrics against universal codecs, plus ablations of encoder layers, temporal resolutions, quantizers, perceptual losses, and speech-only versus universal training.
uh426x3DWx.claimed_gains: UFC-13 achieves the strongest overall performance among universal codecs operating around 0.195 kbps, leading on most metrics and outperforming several higher-bitrate systems; variants span 0.195 to 0.780 kbps.
uh426x3DWx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the codec is competitive at very low token rates across speech, music, and environmental sound, with informative ablations and clear presentation.
uh426x3DWx.main_concern: Methodological novelty over FocalCodec is limited, and there are no listening tests or downstream probing to validate perceptual fidelity and the claim of capturing both semantic and acoustic information.

eEjowGbcWu.one_liner: Self-evolving agent that stores experience as hierarchical text memory and crystallizes recurring plans into callable code tools.
eEjowGbcWu.problem: Self-evolving agents store experience as either text or code, chosen a priori at the system level, and the trade-offs between the two representations are poorly understood.
eEjowGbcWu.method: A controlled study compares text memory and code memory under an identical task stream. Metis then organizes textual experience into execution plans, environment facts, and common pitfalls, and selectively turns recurring plans into callable code tools.
eEjowGbcWu.key_idea: Keep general guidance as text and promote recurring plans to code tools only when repeated reuse justifies the tool-generation cost.
eEjowGbcWu.evidence: A controlled text-versus-code memory study on one task stream and an evaluation on three challenging benchmarks for interactive agents against a no-memory agent and other baselines.
eEjowGbcWu.claimed_gains: Improves over a no-memory agent and baselines on three benchmarks per the abstract (comparison text cut off), and reviewers note reduced token usage; no numbers stated.
eEjowGbcWu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that keeping guidance as text while materializing recurring routines as code tools is a sensible design, with improvements over a no-memory agent across three environments.
eEjowGbcWu.main_concern: The contribution over existing skill-learning systems (ASI, SkillX) looks incremental, the representation study does not establish a general principle, and reuse statistics and upfront cost versus gains are missing.

9SlV59TAcV.one_liner: SFT of deep research agents on 2,000 synthetic Wikidata-based trajectories filtered by per-turn reasoning length to drop looping.
9SlV59TAcV.problem: It is unclear whether a small set of high-quality trajectories can elicit deep research ability through supervised fine-tuning alone, and teacher trajectories contain loop-prone reasoning that revisits hypotheses without progress.
9SlV59TAcV.method: A Wikidata-based pipeline builds verifiable multi-entity questions with obfuscated entities and cross-entity constraints. Loop-aware trajectory filtering uses maximum per-turn reasoning length as a proxy for looping to select trajectories without requiring correct final answers.
9SlV59TAcV.key_idea: Drop teacher trajectories whose longest assistant turn is excessively long, using per-turn reasoning length as a proxy for repetitive looping, regardless of answer correctness.
9SlV59TAcV.evidence: 4B and 35B students trained by SFT on 2,000 trajectories and evaluated on six research benchmarks including BrowseComp and BrowseComp-zh, with external judge evaluations.
9SlV59TAcV.claimed_gains: The 35B agent achieves 66.4% on BrowseComp, 60.8% on BrowseComp-zh, and a 62.8% macro average across six research benchmarks, with no consistent gains from scaling beyond 2,000 trajectories.
9SlV59TAcV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the performance is strong from only about 2,000 trajectories and that the analyses of filtering, answer correctness, and data size are informative.
9SlV59TAcV.main_concern: Attribution is unclear: length filtering changes data size and tool-call distribution at once, length is a coarse proxy for looping, and much of the performance may come from the inference-time discard-all context management.

b37m1YoFSI.one_liner: 4B tutor trained with Bloom-taxonomy diagnosis data, a multi-head reward model, and GRPO with a cognitive-advancement reward.
b37m1YoFSI.problem: Existing LLM tutors emphasize observable pedagogical behaviors with limited explicit modeling of learner cognition.
b37m1YoFSI.method: CogRaise builds a dataset on the 19 cognitive processes of Anderson's revised Bloom taxonomy for SFT initialization and reward learning, and trains a multi-head reward model that scores cognition-related criteria separately from general quality. GRPO then adds a cognitive-advancement reward conditioned on the learner's current cognitive level.
b37m1YoFSI.key_idea: Reward interventions that advance the learner from the diagnosed cognitive level toward the next, using a reward model that scores cognition-related tutoring criteria separately from general quality.
b37m1YoFSI.evidence: CogEdu-Bench (849 instances) for diagnosis, pedagogical decisions, and tutoring quality, plus MathTutorBench and general reasoning checks on GSM8K and MATH500.
b37m1YoFSI.claimed_gains: Improves fine-grained diagnosis QWK by 37.6% relative to its SFT initialization and enhances scaffolding on MathTutorBench, while general reasoning stays within 0.3 percentage points of that initialization.
b37m1YoFSI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation is clear and the pipeline from theory-driven data through reward modeling and RL to a benchmark is complete and carefully evaluated.
b37m1YoFSI.main_concern: The core assumption that the 19 Bloom processes form a fixed one-step learner progression is not supported by the taxonomy, and conditional Minor QWK is computed on a subset (191 of 849 instances).

y0v4LDeZkG.one_liner: End-to-end computer-use agent unifying GUI actions and code execution, trained with SFT then RL using step-balanced GSPO.
y0v4LDeZkG.problem: Naively adding a code tool degrades a GUI agent, so routing between GUI and code must be learned from high-quality hybrid data rather than obtained by prompt-level tool composition.
y0v4LDeZkG.method: OS-Helix puts GUI actions and code in one action space and builds tasks by pairing desktop applications with authentic file artifacts and generating verifiable instructions and evaluators. It cold-starts with SFT on filtered hybrid data, then runs online RL with Step-balanced GSPO.
y0v4LDeZkG.key_idea: Step-balanced GSPO aggregates importance weights per action step rather than per assistant token, so long code actions do not dominate optimization across heterogeneous actions.
y0v4LDeZkG.evidence: OSWorld-Verified with 27B and 35B-A3B models plus transfer to Windows; reviewers cite matched-backbone comparisons, teacher and training ablations, and paired bootstrap confidence intervals.
y0v4LDeZkG.claimed_gains: OS-Helix-27B and OS-Helix-35B-A3B achieve relative improvements of 35.0% and 33.7% on OSWorld-Verified over their reference models (the reference is cut off in the abstract text).
y0v4LDeZkG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the controlled experiments show hybrid GUI and code coordination must be learned and that the recipe yields gains across base models and on Windows.
y0v4LDeZkG.main_concern: The pipeline relies heavily on one proprietary teacher (Claude-Sonnet-4.6) for data, filtering, and evaluators, and synthetic evaluators used for filtering and as RL reward have no reported human agreement check.

Fl0nktsRdu.one_liner: Neural operator evolving Kuramoto-style relation states through Dirac operator components, decoding harmonic and non-harmonic parts via Hodge decomposition.
Fl0nktsRdu.problem: Neural operators handle irregular geometries but overlook the distinct field supports on vertices, edges, and faces, their condition-dependent coupling, and topology-shaped global responses.
Fl0nktsRdu.method: DKHO encodes conditions on their native cochain supports, evolves Kuramoto-inspired relation states with the boundary and coboundary operators that compose the Dirac operator, and decodes non-harmonic and harmonic responses in orthogonal Hodge subspaces.
Fl0nktsRdu.key_idea: Topology fixes where information can flow through Dirac operator structure, while learned Kuramoto-style dynamics adapt how it is exchanged per PDE instance, with Hodge-orthogonal outputs.
Fl0nktsRdu.evidence: Porous-medium Darcy flow, torus transport-diffusion, and cavity magnetostatics against leading baselines.
Fl0nktsRdu.claimed_gains: DKHO-large reduces prediction error by approximately 61% on average over leading baselines, while DKHO-small remains competitive using only 11.5-24.3% as many parameters.
Fl0nktsRdu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that PDE operators on complex geometries are an important problem and that combining discrete exterior calculus, adaptive relation dynamics, and Hodge decomposition is well motivated.
Fl0nktsRdu.main_concern: Novelty and attribution are unclear: related work (TNO, HSD, KNO, Dirac-Bianconi GNNs) overlaps, the benefit of Kuramoto dynamics is not isolated, and DKHO trained for up to 300 epochs versus 200 for baselines.

9LkzX6u4pB.one_liner: Patches the final prompt-side hidden state to show a late assistant-generation boundary band controls jailbreak behavior.
9LkzX6u4pB.problem: Safety-aligned LLMs refuse direct harmful requests but comply when the same intent is wrapped in jailbreak prompts, and the internal point where this switch is established is unclear.
9LkzX6u4pB.method: Using matched pairs of direct and jailbreak-wrapped prompts, they predict a direct-like state counterfactually, patch a single wrapped state at the assistant-generation boundary, and evaluate full generations across three open-weight models.
9LkzX6u4pB.key_idea: Replace the jailbreak-wrapped prompt's final prompt-side state with a predicted direct-like state; the late boundary band then changes refusal behavior through the early generated trajectory.
9LkzX6u4pB.evidence: Three open-weight models with query-group-disjoint counterfactual prediction, one-state patching, reverse and random controls, specificity tests, and prefix counterfactuals under greedy decoding.
9LkzX6u4pB.claimed_gains: Replacing a single wrapped state with a predicted direct-like state reduces ASR from 60.7% to 23.6%, and prefix counterfactuals recover 83.9-100.0% of the full-generation effect within eight tokens.
9LkzX6u4pB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the single-state intervention with reverse and random controls is a strong causal design with full-generation evidence across three models.
9LkzX6u4pB.main_concern: Generalizability and practical value are limited: only three open-weight models under greedy decoding, interventions can raise benign refusals, and the causal interpretation and implementation details (hook point, KV-cache handling) are unclear.

HMqNisP7QV.one_liner: Builds a cross-domain foundation world model for digital agents from a 7-domain corpus, benchmark, and RL training.
HMqNisP7QV.problem: Current world models for digital agents are fragmented: they lack a unified data pipeline, are tied to specific domains, and are treated as passive, isolated simulators.
HMqNisP7QV.method: The authors build WIA-Corpus (5M continual pre-training examples, 9k SFT trajectories, 134.6k RL prompts) and WIA-Bench (1.8k in-domain and 1.7k out-of-domain items over seven digital domains), then train the WIA-WM family (4B / 9B / 27B / 35B-A3B). Reviews describe Dual-Perspective Inversion (action and observation prediction) and a CSPO reinforcement-learning stage.
HMqNisP7QV.key_idea: Train one model on both action prediction and observation prediction (Dual-Perspective Inversion) over unified action-observation trajectories from seven digital domains, then refine with CSPO RL.
HMqNisP7QV.evidence: In-domain and out-of-domain evaluation on WIA-Bench across seven digital domains against other models including GPT-5.6-sol and Claude-Opus-4.8, plus downstream agent use via simulation SFT, simulation RL, and inference.
HMqNisP7QV.claimed_gains: WIA-WM surpasses GPT-5.6-sol and Claude-Opus-4.8 by +3.99% and +4.34% on the seven-domain OOD suite.
HMqNisP7QV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the large multi-domain corpus and benchmark with paired in-domain and out-of-domain splits, and the extensive experiments across model scales and downstream tasks.
HMqNisP7QV.main_concern: Scores and rewards rely heavily on LLM-as-a-judge without human calibration, and there is no comparison with domain-specific world models to justify the foundation-model claim.

LXOpqqaISQ.one_liner: Trains geometry-to-field surrogates on two inverse-density point views with a prediction-disagreement penalty to resist remeshing.
LXOpqqaISQ.problem: Surrogates that predict physical fields from meshes or point clouds change their predictions when remeshing redistributes sampling density, even though the physical case is unchanged (sampling-distribution sensitivity).
LXOpqqaISQ.method: For each case, DeAL draws two fixed-budget views from a continuous inverse-density family, supervises both predictions at common physical queries, and penalizes their disagreement. It is a training principle that leaves the backbone and single-view inference unchanged.
LXOpqqaISQ.key_idea: Supervise two inverse-density views of the same physical case against the target and add a consistency penalty on their predictions at shared query points.
LXOpqqaISQ.evidence: Nine surrogate architectures and four physical systems, evaluated under held-out spatial redistributions and independently generated remeshes; reviews also cite remesh geometry audits, ablations, and seed replication.
LXOpqqaISQ.claimed_gains: DeAL reduces error and inconsistency among predictions by roughly half on average over a large number of matched comparisons.
LXOpqqaISQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree DeAL gives consistent accuracy and stability gains across architectures and tasks, drops into existing models without changes, and is backed by ablations and geometry audits.
LXOpqqaISQ.main_concern: The methodological contribution is seen as incremental (data augmentation plus consistency regularization), and remeshing tests use the original field as ground truth rather than a re-simulated one.

TlO7NHkqAg.one_liner: Converts LLMs to spiking networks in two stages: activity-constrained multi-threshold neurons, then pipelined symmetric integrate-and-fire neurons.
TlO7NHkqAg.problem: Existing LLM-to-SNN conversion reaches high fidelity but needs high spike activity (more energy), and layer-wise temporal accumulation causes serial inference latency.
TlO7NHkqAg.method: Stage one, BA-MTN, jointly learns basis transformations and channel-wise thresholds under an explicit activity constraint. Stage two, BA-SIF, gives an equivalent temporal realization with causal step-by-step spike propagation for pipelined cross-layer execution, with relaxation steps and differential operators handling delays and nonlinear operations.
TlO7NHkqAg.key_idea: Optimize reconstruction under an explicit spike-activity constraint, then realize it with causal symmetric integrate-and-fire neurons so layers execute in a pipeline instead of accumulating per layer.
TlO7NHkqAg.evidence: LLaMA-2, LLaMA-3, and Qwen2.5 models from 7B to 70B parameters under full-precision and 4-bit weight settings; reviews note energy and latency are evaluated theoretically, not on neuromorphic hardware.
TlO7NHkqAg.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract claims a strong accuracy-energy trade-off without figures).
TlO7NHkqAg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the direction meaningful and the large-scale conversion of modern LLMs with explicit spike-activity control practically interesting, with extensive model coverage.
TlO7NHkqAg.main_concern: Energy and latency are estimated theoretically with assumptions (4-bit MAC/AC, omitted transformation and nonlinear-operator costs) and not validated on hardware, and novelty over FlatQuant-style quantization plus an activity regularizer is questioned.

MzwXs40tne.one_liner: Rewards exploration by temporal-contrastive distance to future states in a learned Hamiltonian phase space.
MzwXs40tne.problem: Curiosity signals, including Hamiltonian-based ones, are local in time and do not show whether an action reaches an informative future over longer horizons.
MzwXs40tne.method: HTC^2 trains a horizon-conditioned contrastive critic on same-episode future pairs and uses the positive-pair representation distance as the intrinsic reward. Multi-step Hamiltonian variation adds a bounded structural modulation to this signal.
MzwXs40tne.key_idea: Use the representation distance of a horizon-conditioned contrastive critic on same-episode future pairs as curiosity, modulated by bounded multi-step Hamiltonian variation.
MzwXs40tne.evidence: Experiments with SAC and PPO, supplemented by coverage, robustness to physical changes, and ablation studies; specific environments are not named in the visible text.
MzwXs40tne.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the method reasonable and clearly written, with evaluation from several angles (return, state coverage, robustness to physical changes, ablations).
MzwXs40tne.main_concern: Gains over baselines are modest with high variance, baselines are mostly pre-2022 and omit close methods such as C-TeC, and the RND warm start strongly affects performance.

1A2seNVDZG.one_liner: Adapts sample selection in zeroth-order LLM fine-tuning using gradient-norm estimates from existing directional differences.
1A2seNVDZG.problem: Zeroth-order methods sample training examples uniformly, ignoring their evolving importance and leaving avoidable estimation variance.
1A2seNVDZG.method: SAZO estimates sample importance from gradient-norm information in the directional differences ZO already computes, and keeps per-example exponential moving averages to track importance from sparse minibatch feedback. It needs no extra model evaluations and only O(N) additional scalar state compared with MeZO.
1A2seNVDZG.key_idea: Importance-sample training examples in ZO fine-tuning, using per-example moving averages of gradient-norm estimates derived from directional differences without true gradients.
1A2seNVDZG.evidence: A proof that SAZO asymptotically matches the leading convergence term of the minimum-variance sampling oracle, and experiments across four model families (reviews: classification, NLI, and QA against MeZO and HiZOO).
1A2seNVDZG.claimed_gains: Improved average downstream performance and up to 6x faster convergence to the same training loss in terms of query count.
1A2seNVDZG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like that the method is simple and lightweight, adds no extra evaluations, and adapts in sample space, which complements parameter-space ZO methods.
1A2seNVDZG.main_concern: The evaluation is narrow (classification, NLI, QA; mainly MeZO and HiZOO baselines) and lacks ablations such as a loss-based reweighting baseline or a check that tracked importance recovers useful rankings.

EaBNBOUY4i.one_liner: Samples the exact same token as full-scan sampling while refining output-projection precision only for rows that can still win.
EaBNBOUY4i.problem: Output projection reads every vocabulary weight at fixed precision even though sampling only needs to identify one winning token.
EaBNBOUY4i.method: A low-bit scan bounds token scores under fixed Gumbel perturbations, an exact evaluation raises the threshold, and only rows that can still win receive more precision. Each exclusion is certified by bounds, with screening accumulated exactly in integer arithmetic.
EaBNBOUY4i.key_idea: Treat Gumbel-max sampling as a race and use certified low-bit score bounds plus an exact incumbent to exclude contenders, refining precision only for the survivors.
EaBNBOUY4i.evidence: Three large-vocabulary language models at small decoding batches on an RTX 5090 D and an H800, against three full-scan samplers including FlashSampling, with matched INT8 controls and a worst-case analysis.
EaBNBOUY4i.claimed_gains: Sampling-head speedups up to 2.89x and lower complete GPU decode-step latency during natural generation.
EaBNBOUY4i.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit a principled adaptive-precision formulation with certified bounds that preserves the exact sampled token while cutting memory traffic.
EaBNBOUY4i.main_concern: The end-to-end advantage is small (decode-step gains of about 1.45-4.42% on RTX 5090 D, little on H800), the exactness guarantee depends on numerical assumptions for the Tensor Core path, and both precisions must be kept in memory.

aRbNfEDnMX.one_liner: Allocates image tokens by content complexity using a predicted importance heatmap and a hybrid 1D-2D tokenizer.
aRbNfEDnMX.problem: Image tokenizers use a fixed number of tokens at fixed spatial locations, ignoring variation in visual complexity across and within images.
aRbNfEDnMX.method: DynamicTok predicts a heatmap of regional importance and assigns more tokens to informative regions. A hybrid 1D-2D tokenizer lets latent tokens capture global context while receiving localized cues from image tokens, and a two-stage generator predicts the heatmap before synthesis to support different token budgets.
aRbNfEDnMX.key_idea: Predict a regional-importance heatmap to set both token count and token locations, then encode with latent tokens that take localized cues from image tokens.
aRbNfEDnMX.evidence: ImageNet-256 reconstruction and class-conditional generation, with ablations on token range, heatmap type, partitioning strategy, and encoder/decoder fusion.
aRbNfEDnMX.claimed_gains: ImageNet-256 reconstruction rFID of 0.57 with 64 tokens and 0.39 with 128 tokens, and generation gFID of 1.40 with 64 tokens.
aRbNfEDnMX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see a meaningful problem and strong reconstruction and one-stage generation results at low token counts, with ablations supporting the hybrid design.
aRbNfEDnMX.main_concern: The best generation result (gFID 1.40) is one-stage with a fixed grid while two-stage dynamic generation is worse (1.63), token budgets ignore layout side information, and training details are missing.

MNZOx2SRbM.one_liner: Targeted adversarial attack on expressive human pose and shape estimators that steers outputs to attacker-specified articulations.
MNZOx2SRbM.problem: Existing attacks on expressive human pose and shape estimation are mostly untargeted, so it is unknown whether an adversary can steer reconstructions toward a prescribed state.
MNZOx2SRbM.method: CtrlRecon builds an image-specific target by combining attacker-specified articulations with the clean predictions and holds it fixed during optimization. A representation-aware objective steers the output toward the target while limiting changes to untargeted pose, expression, and camera translation, and a two-stage optimization pairs continuous perturbation with discrete 8-bit refinement.
MNZOx2SRbM.key_idea: Fix a target built from attacker-specified articulations plus clean predictions, then optimize a representation-aware loss with continuous perturbation followed by discrete 8-bit refinement to survive quantization.
MNZOx2SRbM.evidence: Experiments across three EHPS estimators; reviews cite comparisons with PGD and C&W baselines, MPVPE metrics, and evaluation on exported and reloaded images.
MNZOx2SRbM.claimed_gains: not stated (the visible abstract reports effectiveness across three estimators without figures).
MNZOx2SRbM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see targeted manipulation as a meaningful, security-relevant step beyond untargeted degradation and value the evaluation on exported and reloaded images.
MNZOx2SRbM.main_concern: The PGD and C&W baselines use an unweighted raw-parameter loss and unmatched computation, and the ablations do not isolate where CtrlRecon's gains come from.

38SDKqRg3g.one_liner: Jointly schedules a training curriculum and routes human experts by cost in interactive imitation learning using bandits.
38SDKqRg3g.problem: Interactive imitation learning is costly in human supervision, and prior adaptive-curriculum and teacher-selection work ignores their coupled non-stationarity as scenario value and supervision needs evolve with the learner.
38SDKqRg3g.method: COACH treats the setting as a coupled non-stationary decision problem. It tracks scenario-specific learning dynamics to choose what to train next and routes episode-level supervision by scenario, learner proficiency, and expert cost, using a factorized but context-coupled architecture with Lazy Re-evaluation to refresh curriculum estimates.
38SDKqRg3g.key_idea: A curriculum bandit picks the next scenario by learning progress while a context-coupled supervision bandit assigns an expert by cost, with lazy refresh of non-stationary estimates.
38SDKqRg3g.evidence: MetaDrive and MetaWorld experiments with baselines, ablations, scalability analysis, and validation with human participants, plus a skill-to-task matching demonstration.
38SDKqRg3g.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract claims better task performance and lower cost than baselines without figures).
38SDKqRg3g.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem practical and the evaluation broad (two environments, many baselines, ablations, human participants), with a favorable performance-versus-supervision-cost trade-off.
38SDKqRg3g.main_concern: The method mostly combines known parts (Exp3, NeuralUCB, a learning-progress signal), with unclear gains over simple rule baselines and a gap between the stated joint objective and the separate bandit objectives.

fvjdMEVlzl.one_liner: Refines frozen VLA policy actions by jointly learning residual corrections and how long to execute each before re-observing.
fvjdMEVlzl.problem: Small execution errors keep strong vision-language-action policies from completing manipulation reliably, and the right correction depends on the intended correction horizon.
fvjdMEVlzl.method: AHR represents each refinement decision as a correction unit: a horizon-conditioned residual sequence paired with its execution length. A lightweight actor proposes bounded residual candidates and selects a unit, trained with an off-policy actor-critic using unit-level values, duration-aware semi-Markov targets, and mixed demonstration and online replay.
fvjdMEVlzl.key_idea: Pair each horizon-conditioned residual action sequence with its execution length as one correction unit, and learn both jointly with a duration-aware semi-Markov critic.
fvjdMEVlzl.evidence: A frozen GR00T N1.6 base policy on RoboMimic-Pixel and DexMimicGen plus two real-world tasks; reviews mention pi0.5 results in the appendix.
fvjdMEVlzl.claimed_gains: Average success rates of 96.1% on RoboMimic-Pixel and 96.8% on DexMimicGen, outperforming the compared methods, and a 95.6% result on two real-world tasks (abstract truncated).
fvjdMEVlzl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers regard jointly optimizing correction amplitude and execution horizon as a practical, well-motivated approach with strong simulation and real-world results supported by ablations.
fvjdMEVlzl.main_concern: Generalization evidence is limited: mostly one VLA backbone (GR00T N1.6), key ablations on one task, unvalidated critic estimates across horizons, and a contribution viewed as incremental.

kuklVEfgRW.one_liner: Splits region features into CLS-aligned and orthogonal-residual parts and fuses them across frozen VLM layers with a learned selector.
kuklVEfgRW.problem: Global image-text pre-training limits the local discriminability of VLMs for dense open-vocabulary perception, and the best feature depth varies across tasks and regions.
kuklVEfgRW.method: ReGDec decomposes region features into CLS-aligned components and orthogonal residuals. A compact selector learns separate region-conditioned weights to combine the two components across layers while the VLM encoders stay frozen.
kuklVEfgRW.key_idea: Decompose region features into a CLS-aligned part and an orthogonal residual, then weight each across layers with a region-conditioned selector on frozen encoders.
kuklVEfgRW.evidence: Multiple VLM backbones and dense perception benchmarks; reviews cite dense recognition, open-vocabulary detection and segmentation, and supervised training on labeled COCO regions.
kuklVEfgRW.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says gains vary across backbones and tasks without figures).
kuklVEfgRW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the motivation clear and the method simple, interpretable, and consistently effective across broad experiments.
kuklVEfgRW.main_concern: Novelty is seen as incremental over multi-layer feature fusion, comparisons use baselines no newer than 2023, and some design gains are small (0.2%-0.3%).

dxLO4bR7B9.one_liner: Compresses visual tokens for text image translation, keeping target-text regions, and distills from a privileged full-context teacher.
dxLO4bR7B9.problem: Text image machine translation needs visual context to resolve ambiguity, but it is unclear which visual evidence supports translation decisions and how much context is necessary.
dxLO4bR7B9.method: Translation Context Lens (TCL) diagnoses context with controlled visual interventions. ConServe samples background tokens with spatially balanced selection while keeping all tokens in target text regions, and PC-OPSD trains the student on its own prefixes with a teacher that sees full visual context, correct interpretations, and explanations of wrong alternatives. The authors also introduce the SC-TIMT benchmark.
dxLO4bR7B9.key_idea: Keep all target-text tokens and sample background tokens spatially, then use on-policy self-distillation from a teacher with privileged full context to correct compression-induced preference shifts.
dxLO4bR7B9.evidence: A 9B model evaluated on the new SC-TIMT screen-translation benchmark and on MCiT, with ablations and an intervention analysis run on a single model.
dxLO4bR7B9.claimed_gains: The 9B model outperforms larger multimodal models on SC-TIMT and remains competitive on MCiT with substantially fewer visual tokens.
dxLO4bR7B9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see a practical, coherent design for perception, context disambiguation, and efficiency, with an informative intervention-based diagnostic and demonstrated token and latency savings.
dxLO4bR7B9.main_concern: Dataset coverage is limited (SC-TIMT is foreign-to-Chinese and dominated by mobile screenshots), and the gains from fine-tuning, privileged supervision, and compression-aware distillation are not fully disentangled.

y8WZArNEYm.one_liner: Derives one-sided directional derivatives of the robust value under Wasserstein uncertainty and builds an actor-critic that learns them.
y8WZArNEYm.problem: In finite-horizon MDPs with Wasserstein transition uncertainty, the worst-case kernel depends on the policy, so the classical policy gradient misses the sensitivity of the robust objective.
y8WZArNEYm.method: The Lagrangian dual of the inner robust problem yields one-sided directional derivatives of the robust value with respect to policy parameters, and a robust dynamic programming principle covers the value and its sensitivity. The actor-critic uses three networks: policy, robust value, and a vector-valued sensitivity that provides the policy gradient.
y8WZArNEYm.key_idea: Replace the classical policy gradient with one-sided directional derivatives of the robust value, obtained from the inner problem's Lagrangian dual and learned by a critic through backward recursions.
y8WZArNEYm.evidence: Proofs under regularity conditions, finite-state benchmarks, and a linear-quadratic control task (abstract truncated); reviews also mention ablation studies.
y8WZArNEYm.claimed_gains: On finite-state benchmarks the method recovers the exact robust dynamic programming solution.
y8WZArNEYm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the theory rigorous and non-trivial, with new results on one-sided derivatives and clearly stated limitations.
y8WZArNEYm.main_concern: The practical algorithm lacks guarantees, may need an exponentially large branch set with high compute overhead, and prior robust actor-critic work with Wasserstein uncertainty is not discussed.

N7Q7Lhbywj.one_liner: Probes frozen multilingual text embeddings to predict human colour-naming centroids of held-out languages across 14 languages.
N7Q7Lhbywj.problem: Translation-based alignment cannot show whether multilingual representations capture the colours speakers associate with colour terms, and existing evaluations do not test transfer to naming in new languages.
N7Q7Lhbywj.method: A human-referenced cross-lingual probe maps frozen text representations to language-specific human naming centroids for 1,160 colour terms in 14 languages. Each of ten non-English languages is predicted from the others, with the target excluded from probe fitting and model selection.
N7Q7Lhbywj.key_idea: Fit a readout from frozen text embeddings to human colour-naming centroids on other languages, test on a fully held-out language, and vary colour-region coverage in the supervision.
N7Q7Lhbywj.evidence: 1,160 colour terms in 14 languages, six language models compared with character, subword-token, and frequency baselines, plus a coverage analysis that removes colour regions or random terms.
N7Q7Lhbywj.claimed_gains: In five of six language models the probe predicts held-out centroids better than character, subword-token, and frequency baselines, and transfer persists without English or same-family training examples.
N7Q7Lhbywj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the human-referenced evaluation is well motivated and rigorous, with carefully designed controls and thorough supplementary analyses.
N7Q7Lhbywj.main_concern: Baselines are weak (no multilingual-embedding or translation-based comparisons), centroid targets drop category extent and boundaries, and the significance beyond formalizing an intuitive result is unclear.

eoGzZttUQr.one_liner: Decouples on-policy distillation KL into forward KL on matched tokens and self-weighted reverse KL on mismatched tokens.
eoGzZttUQr.problem: In on-policy distillation, forward KL concentrates loss and gradient on tokens where teacher probability far exceeds student probability, causing length inflation, truncation, and accuracy collapse, while reverse KL can under-cover teacher modes.
eoGzZttUQr.method: DKLD splits the KL into Matched Region and Mismatched Region contributors, using forward KL in the first and reverse KL with p_S self-weighting in the second. An advantage-weighted distillation module then balances OPD with GRPO in a single objective, since the student rollouts supply both signals.
eoGzZttUQr.key_idea: Apply forward KL on tokens where student and teacher agree and p_S-weighted reverse KL on high-disparity tokens, and weight distillation by GRPO advantage to reduce gradient conflict.
eoGzZttUQr.evidence: Math reasoning with 0.6B, 1.7B, and 4B students over three training seeds with validation-selected checkpoints, compared with FKL, RKL, AKL, and ToDi, plus component ablations (details from reviews).
eoGzZttUQr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit a clear motivation and a loss derived from an exact decomposition, with consistent gains across student sizes and ablations supporting the design.
eoGzZttUQr.main_concern: The motivating forward-KL collapse does not match the healthy FKL baseline in the main table, and the advantage-weighted GRPO module is confounded with reduced distillation strength and loosely tied to the stated motivation.

Uy9ma9gr8m.one_liner: Proves a one-step gradient GCN estimator attains information-theoretic limits on stochastic block models with non-informative Gaussian features.
Uy9ma9gr8m.problem: It is unclear how GCNs exploit graph structure and a few revealed labels when node features carry no signal, a setting that existing CSBM-based analyses do not cover.
Uy9ma9gr8m.method: The authors analyze a single-layer one-step gradient GCN estimator fit by regularized least squares on a symmetric SBM with n nodes and K communities, an eta fraction of revealed labels, and i.i.d. Gaussian features in R^d. They prove upper bounds on exact recovery and misclassification and matching information-theoretic lower bounds.
Uy9ma9gr8m.key_idea: A single-layer one-step gradient GCN fit by regularized least squares uses large-dimension random Gaussian features to exploit graph structure and revealed labels, matching information-theoretic lower bounds.
Uy9ma9gr8m.evidence: Theorems for exact recovery in the logarithmic-degree regime and for misclassification rates in the broader regime, matching lower bounds, plus a multi-layer analysis and synthetic experiments (from reviews).
Uy9ma9gr8m.claimed_gains: Exact recovery when (sqrt p - sqrt q)^2 > K log n / n using a vanishing fraction eta = o(1) of labels, with a matching lower bound showing this threshold is sharp.
Uy9ma9gr8m.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the setting meaningful and the theory deep, with sharp upper bounds, matching information-theoretic lower bounds, and useful multi-layer insight.
Uy9ma9gr8m.main_concern: Several conditions are loose or mismatched: the dimension condition depends on a random margin, the misclassification upper bound does not match the lower bound in the log-degree regime, and experiments do not satisfy the theorem assumptions.

VD0cSkkIxc.one_liner: Diagnoses text-trigger dominance in dual-key MLLM backdoors and builds low-amplitude UAP triggers with a necessity penalty.
VD0cSkkIxc.problem: Low-amplitude visual triggers often fail to establish dual-key backdoors in MLLMs because activation becomes dominated by the text trigger.
VD0cSkkIxc.method: Gradient analysis and visual-state replacement reveal a representation-influence mismatch: the UAP changes hidden states substantially but barely affects the target response, which a path-integral decomposition explains. The method builds UAPs from normalized projector residuals and, under training control, adds a necessity penalty so activation depends on both triggers.
VD0cSkkIxc.key_idea: Construct universal adversarial perturbations from normalized projector residuals and add a necessity penalty so the backdoor fires only when both image and text triggers are present.
VD0cSkkIxc.evidence: Several datasets, model architectures, and fine-tuning settings (full fine-tuning and LoRA per reviews), with ablations and visual-state interventions.
VD0cSkkIxc.claimed_gains: High attack success when both triggers are present, low activation with either trigger alone, and clean-task performance comparable to clean fine-tuning (no figures in the abstract).
VD0cSkkIxc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the analysis explaining why text triggers dominate (gradient analysis and hidden-state interventions) and the testing across datasets, architectures, and fine-tuning regimes.
VD0cSkkIxc.main_concern: Novelty over prior dual-key and text-dominance work is unclear because the residual objective and necessity penalty are simple extensions, and the method generalizes unevenly across datasets.

DgqCqFLpTr.one_liner: Post-trains flow-matching restorers with rewards by perturbing the source state in opposite directions and following the reward-weighted restoration difference.
DgqCqFLpTr.problem: Flow-matching restorers are trained to match paired ground truth rather than human preferences or task rewards, and policy-gradient post-training needs stochastic exploration and action likelihoods that deterministic samplers lack.
DgqCqFLpTr.method: Given a degraded input, APD-Flow perturbs the source state in two opposite directions, restores both with the same deterministic sampler, and weights the difference of the two restorations by their reward difference to form an Antithetic Preference Direction. The restorer is optimized along this direction, with fidelity-aware reward adaptation keeping a composite fidelity score at or above a target relative to the pretrained restorer.
