DgqCqFLpTr.key_idea: Explore at the source state with antithetic perturbation pairs under one deterministic sampler, and update the restorer along the reward-weighted difference of their outputs.
DgqCqFLpTr.evidence: Blind face restoration, blind image super-resolution, and scene-text restoration across several backbones, with comparisons to alternative post-training methods and ablations.
DgqCqFLpTr.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says targeted perceptual or task-specific metrics improve consistently while fidelity is kept, without figures).
DgqCqFLpTr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like that it leaves the deterministic sampler unchanged, supports non-differentiable rewards and one-step models, and is evaluated across backbones and tasks.
DgqCqFLpTr.main_concern: Novelty is limited relative to FDFO, FPO, Neighbor GRPO, and DiffusionNFT (mainly source-state antithetic coupling), and fidelity is only partly preserved (for example LPIPS rises on PMRF).

xScAoz6sUF.one_liner: Detects AI-generated text from how ablating attention and MLP branches in a frozen LLM shifts next-token distributions.
xScAoz6sUF.problem: Existing AI-text detectors struggle under distribution shifts, limited text lengths, and paraphrasing.
xScAoz6sUF.method: LesionProbe ablates attention and MLP branches, individually and jointly, at each layer of a frozen proxy LLM and measures changes in next-token distributions with normalized Jensen-Shannon divergence. The resulting module contribution patterns across layers and token positions feed a lightweight classifier, and Shapley analysis shows layer-wise differences between human and LLM text.
xScAoz6sUF.key_idea: Human and LLM text differ in how a proxy LLM's predictions depend on its attention and MLP modules, so layer-wise ablation responses serve as detection features.
xScAoz6sUF.evidence: DetectRL experiments across generation-source configurations and leave-one-domain-out evaluation, with several proxy models.
xScAoz6sUF.claimed_gains: Average AUROC of 98.74% and a true-positive rate of 87.80% at a false-positive rate of 0.1% across generation-source configurations.
xScAoz6sUF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find it an interesting, interpretable way to extract features from a frozen LLM, with competitive, fairly complete experiments that stay stable across proxy models.
xScAoz6sUF.main_concern: DetectRL is nearly saturated and related work on simple probing detectors is thin, and the heavy compute (97 runs per input at 32 layers) is not compared with baseline costs.

rq0YmhI2gJ.one_liner: Merges models by applying graph wavelets to weights viewed as bipartite graphs, damping high-frequency conflicts and aggregating low-frequency components.
rq0YmhI2gJ.problem: Model merging suffers destructive interference from conflicting parameter updates, and it is unclear which parameter components cause interference and which can be safely shared.
rq0YmhI2gJ.method: Spectral Graph Merging views weight matrices as bipartite neuron-interaction graphs and uses graph wavelets to split task vectors into low-frequency components (shared structure) and higher-frequency components (task-specific conflicts). It reduces interference in the high-frequency components while aggregating the low-frequency ones.
rq0YmhI2gJ.key_idea: Decompose task vectors with graph wavelets over the neuron-interaction bipartite graph, aggregating low-frequency bands and suppressing interference in high-frequency bands.
rq0YmhI2gJ.evidence: MergeBench and OptMerge benchmarks, including highly conflicting task combinations; reviews cite Gemma-2-2B and Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct and ablations on graph construction and band decomposition.
rq0YmhI2gJ.claimed_gains: SGM outperforms existing merging methods on both MergeBench and OptMerge while maintaining reasoning and safety under highly conflicting task combinations (no figures in the abstract).
rq0YmhI2gJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like the clear spectral framing, the deployable static merged model, the informative ablations, and the improvements in the evaluated settings.
rq0YmhI2gJ.main_concern: Closeness to SVD-based shared-subspace methods is unresolved, the data-free claim conflicts with tuning on calibration data, and the paper and supplied code differ in the Laplacian definition and band conventions.

GN1UmNqUCR.one_liner: Proves balanced splitting is optimal for recursive long-step gradient-descent schedules and derives a log-periodic convergence rate.
GN1UmNqUCR.problem: The convergence of optimized recursive predetermined-stepsize schedules for gradient descent on smooth convex functions was not fully characterized, and optimality of balanced splitting was a conjecture of Zhang and Jiang.
GN1UmNqUCR.method: The paper proves balanced splitting is optimal at every horizon for the ConPP/OBS-S schedules, giving a bound with a positive, Lipschitz, nonconstant 1-periodic function Phi(log2 N). For the asymmetric ConPD/OBS-F schedules, optimal splits need not be balanced, but the same Silver exponent persists with a distinct modulation.
GN1UmNqUCR.key_idea: A four-point rearrangement inequality shows balanced splits are optimal in the recursive composition, yielding a convergence bound with a log-periodic factor.
GN1UmNqUCR.evidence: Theoretical proofs only, covering the symmetric and asymmetric schedule families; no experiments are stated.
GN1UmNqUCR.claimed_gains: For every N >= 1 the bound f(x_{N-1}) - f_* <= [1/(2 N^p Phi(log2 N) - 1)] (L/2)||x_0 - x_*||^2 holds with p = log2(1+sqrt2) for the optimized ConPP/OBS-S schedules.
GN1UmNqUCR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper resolves an explicit conjecture with clean proofs that balanced splitting is optimal for the symmetric family.
GN1UmNqUCR.main_concern: The log-periodic phase effect changes the leading constant by under 1%, the exponent was already known, optimality is limited to the ConPP/OBS-S family, and the schedules are not formally defined.

DYFfmOhBcV.one_liner: Terminates KV-cache block traversal inside attention kernels once accumulated attention outputs stop changing.
DYFfmOhBcV.problem: Long-context decoding is limited by KV-cache access cost, and most KV management methods prune using keys only because including values is costly.
DYFfmOhBcV.method: ART is a run-time kernel mechanism that tracks accumulated attention outputs and stops reading further KV blocks when successive output updates stay small. It runs on top of existing dense or sparse attention policies, using a stability criterion on magnitude and directional change with a theoretical truncation-error characterization.
DYFfmOhBcV.key_idea: Monitor the magnitude and direction of the running attention output inside the kernel and stop visiting the remaining KV blocks once updates are small.
DYFfmOhBcV.evidence: LongBench and RULER NIAH experiments across multiple models, context lengths, and KV-cache methods, with an end-to-end vLLM integration (from reviews).
DYFfmOhBcV.claimed_gains: Up to 20% higher generation throughput for existing KV-cache methods on LongBench with marginal quality loss.
DYFfmOhBcV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like the training-free, kernel-level, composable design that uses value information without a separate importance predictor, with measured low overhead and vLLM integration.
DYFfmOhBcV.main_concern: The benefit of adaptive termination is not isolated from simply processing fewer blocks (no fixed-truncation control), and early stopping can miss late evidence, as RULER accuracy at 32K falls from 99.34% to 78.65% on Qwen3-8B.

X14Hkjb4Ud.one_liner: Pretrains on healthy 6-DoF knee gait via discrete codebook tokens and masked code prediction, then fine-tunes for disease recognition.
X14Hkjb4Ud.problem: Learning-based knee disease recognition depends on disease-specific annotations that are hard to obtain at scale, and it is unexplored whether healthy-only pretraining supports label-efficient recognition across centers.
X14Hkjb4Ud.method: GaitReader splits recordings into cycle-level gait units and learns a gait vocabulary of six DoF-specific codebooks. The frozen tokenizer provides discrete targets for contextual pretraining that combines masked code prediction, attribute prediction, and waveform reconstruction without disease labels, followed by supervised fine-tuning; the authors also release the KineGait multicenter dataset with 4,168 healthy participants plus Healthy, ACLD, and KOA cohorts.
X14Hkjb4Ud.key_idea: Tokenize gait cycles into six DoF-specific codebooks, then pretrain a contextual model on healthy data only to predict masked codes, attributes, and waveforms.
X14Hkjb4Ud.evidence: KineGait with fixed internal and external test sets across five training-validation folds, plus label-efficiency experiments and comparisons with existing methods.
X14Hkjb4Ud.claimed_gains: Mean accuracies of 93.04% and 89.87% on the fixed internal and external test sets across five training-validation folds.
X14Hkjb4Ud.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the large multicenter KineGait dataset, the clear motivation of reducing disease-label needs, and same-architecture comparisons with external testing that support pretraining.
X14Hkjb4Ud.main_concern: Disease classification is confounded by age, sex, and recruitment-source differences between cohorts, and the method largely combines existing components (VQShape- and HeartLang-like tokenization and masking).

GpCGeMWN0w.one_liner: Labels gates in synthesized netlists with a GNN, then accepts each arithmetic-core label only if simulation matches a reference function.
GpCGeMWN0w.problem: Logic synthesis shares gates across operations, so neighborhood aggregation in GNNs mixes operation cues at shared gates and leaves gate classes ambiguous for functional subgraph matching.
GpCGeMWN0w.method: A GNN assigns each gate one of five classes (adder, multiplier, subtractor, comparator, control) and proposes candidate regions. Verification-driven refinement simulates each candidate and a fixed reference function on the same random input patterns and gives the class only if outputs agree on every pattern; a shared gate keeps one label and lies in every core that uses it.
GpCGeMWN0w.key_idea: The learned classifier only proposes; a simulation conformance check against a reference function is the sole mechanism that can change a gate label, and accepted regions are locked.
GpCGeMWN0w.evidence: 21 netlists with embedded arithmetic cores from EPFL, ISCAS-85, and ITC-99, compared with nine baselines at four logic-injection levels (from reviews).
GpCGeMWN0w.claimed_gains: not stated (the visible abstract is cut off before results; a review reports 92.34% accuracy versus 76.80% for the strongest baseline at the highest injection level).
GpCGeMWN0w.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see a relevant circuit-analysis problem and a sound propose-then-verify design that could anchor work combining learning with formal verification, with consistent gains over nine baselines.
GpCGeMWN0w.main_concern: The logic-sharing sweep adds label-free neighbor gates rather than varying real sharing, the speed and certification comparison is against an author-built post-processor, and the problem formulation is unclear.

NMvPfKRsJ6.one_liner: Defines document structure as elements, a forest, and reference edges; releases DocVine data and a 2B VLM pipeline.
NMvPfKRsJ6.problem: Document structure recovery targets the heading hierarchy alone, which under-determines real documents with non-title parents, long-range reference links, and units split across page breaks.
NMvPfKRsJ6.method: The paper defines structure G=(V,E_h,E_r): semantic elements that persist across pages with a participation flag, a forest whose internal nodes need not be titles (groups may be virtual nodes), and directed reference edges. It builds DocVine (1,217 documents, 12,736 pages, human-annotated), the staged VinePipe, and VineVLM-2B, a 2B vision language model fine-tuned to drive every stage.
NMvPfKRsJ6.key_idea: Annotate and predict elements, hierarchy, and reference links jointly over the same cross-page elements, with one fine-tuned VLM driving each pipeline stage.
NMvPfKRsJ6.evidence: The DocVine benchmark of 1,217 documents and 12,736 pages compared against task-specific hierarchy parsers and frontier vision language models, plus an external evaluation (from reviews).
NMvPfKRsJ6.claimed_gains: VinePipe with VineVLM-2B beats task-specific hierarchy parsers and frontier vision language models on DocVine (the visible abstract is cut off after this).
NMvPfKRsJ6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see a useful formulation capturing non-heading parents, virtual groups, cross-page continuity, and references, plus a substantial jointly annotated dataset with detailed guidelines.
NMvPfKRsJ6.main_concern: Conceptual novelty over GraphDoc, DocGenome, DocParser, and DSG is insufficiently distinguished, and the benefit of the extra structure for downstream tasks is not shown.

GNklCDCxuG.one_liner: Extends a frozen VGGT to any central camera by injecting a distortion token from a canonical-plus-distortion camera decomposition.
GNklCDCxuG.problem: 3D foundation models such as VGGT do not generalize to non-perspective cameras like fisheye and panoramic ones.
GNklCDCxuG.method: VGGT-Any decomposes camera geometry into a canonical space following the perspective-camera formulation and a distortion space expressing each camera's projection, and injects a distortion token into the frozen foundation model. The authors also build LensZoo, a synthetic indoor dataset where any central camera model can be rendered at shared poses.
GNklCDCxuG.key_idea: Split camera geometry into a pinhole-compatible canonical component and a distortion component, and feed the latter as a token to a frozen VGGT so pinhole behavior is exactly preserved.
GNklCDCxuG.evidence: Real fisheye and panoramic benchmarks plus heterogeneous-camera and single-view settings, against camera-specific and fine-tuned baselines, with the LensZoo dataset.
GNklCDCxuG.claimed_gains: VGGT-Any is competitive with camera-specific and fine-tuned baselines on real fisheye and panoramic benchmarks and exactly retains the base model's pinhole reconstruction ability (no figures given).
GNklCDCxuG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the camera decomposition principled and the evaluation broad across fisheye, panoramic, heterogeneous, and single-view settings, with preserved pinhole capability as a practical advantage.
GNklCDCxuG.main_concern: The 'any central camera' claim is untested on unseen camera families (all thirteen are in training), calibration is assumed known with no robustness check, and ablations do not isolate the decomposition.

prZtrNlhZM.one_liner: Training-free caching for structured 3D latent diffusion using per-cell drift to choose step reuse, block fallback, or refresh.
prZtrNlhZM.problem: Existing caching strategies are unreliable for structured latent 3D generation: global change estimates hide spatially concentrated latent evolution, and token-output reuse mixes stale predictions with outputs recomputed under an altered attention context.
prZtrNlhZM.method: Cache3D groups sparse tokens into cells of the latent 3D grid, averages anchor-relative token drift within each cell, and takes the maximum cell response as a localized spatial risk metric. This signal selects among denoising-step reuse, transformer-block fallback, and full denoiser refresh.
prZtrNlhZM.key_idea: Measure cache reliability as the maximum per-cell anchor-relative drift on the latent 3D grid, while executing reuse at coarser step or block granularity.
prZtrNlhZM.evidence: The TRELLIS 2.0 example-image benchmark compared with EasyCache (and TeaCache per reviews), with ablations on block fallback and aggregation rules.
prZtrNlhZM.claimed_gains: 1.633x end-to-end speedup and 16.0% lower shape latent relative RMSE than EasyCache, with comparable geometric fidelity.
prZtrNlhZM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find separating local risk measurement from coarse-grained reuse a sensible response to sparse 3D latents, with useful partial block fallback.
prZtrNlhZM.main_concern: The increment over EasyCache and similar methods is unclear, comparisons omit stronger methods such as TaylorSeer, and metric differences from EasyCache and TeaCache are tiny.

QpzyPpdfH3.one_liner: Compresses ColBERT-style multi-vector document embeddings with per-document eigendirections and derives an equivalent single-vector representation.
QpzyPpdfH3.problem: Late-interaction models like ColBERT store many token vectors per document, causing large indexing cost, storage footprint, and expensive MaxSim scoring.
QpzyPpdfH3.method: EigenLI finds the dominant eigendirections of each document's token embeddings, which lie in a low-dimensional subspace, and builds reduced interaction representations without training. EigenLI-SV derives an ANN-compatible single-vector representation from the second-order summary of the reduced structure.
QpzyPpdfH3.key_idea: Project each document's token embeddings onto its top eigendirections for compression, and use the second-order summary of that subspace as a single vector.
QpzyPpdfH3.evidence: ColBERTv2, AnswerAI-ColBERT-small, and GTE-ModernColBERT across multiple datasets, against k-means and Ward clustering pooling and against MUVERA.
QpzyPpdfH3.claimed_gains: k-EigenLI with k <= 32 outperforms k-means and Ward clustering pooling on ColBERTv2 and AnswerAI-ColBERT-small (but clustering is better on GTE-ModernColBERT at k=32), and EigenLI-SV consistently outperforms single-vector surrogates such as MUVERA.
QpzyPpdfH3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the method simple, training-free, and mathematically coherent, with a query-compression error bound and strong gains over pooling baselines on some models.
QpzyPpdfH3.main_concern: Effectiveness varies by model (it underperforms Ward on GTE-ModernColBERT), and its closeness to the document-subspace work of Piwowarski et al. (2010) is not clearly distinguished.

29Nu9jOmDL.one_liner: Decomposes a graph once into cached edge-disjoint subgraphs and recombines them per epoch into exact-budget GNN training graphs.
29Nu9jOmDL.problem: Reusing one sparse graph locks GNN training to a fixed topology, while varying the graph across epochs needs costly repeated sampling or recomputation.
29Nu9jOmDL.method: EDiS decomposes the graph once into cacheable edge-disjoint subgraphs (by default using feature-based scores and successive maximum-score covering forests), then composes per-epoch training graphs under edge-budget constraints and retention ratios without re-extracting structure. A combinatorial analysis shows the stored decomposition preserves cut structure and that composed graphs keep a guaranteed share of it.
29Nu9jOmDL.key_idea: Separate one-time structural extraction into edge-disjoint covering-forest subgraphs from per-epoch composition, so each epoch draws an exact-budget graph from the cached decomposition.
29Nu9jOmDL.evidence: 19 homophilic, heterophilic, and large-scale node-classification benchmarks against 17 baselines under the same edge budget, plus ablations and a combinatorial analysis.
29Nu9jOmDL.claimed_gains: EDiS ranks first in aggregate accuracy, average rank, and gap to the best method across 19 benchmarks against 17 baselines under the same edge budget.
29Nu9jOmDL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like the clear decomposition-composition framing, the reusable cached structure across budgets, the structural guarantees, and the broad benchmark coverage.
29Nu9jOmDL.main_concern: Novelty over the closest predecessor (AGS-GS-Disjoint) is overstated, and comparisons with DropEdge or GraphSAINT/LADIES-style sampling under the same exact budget are missing.

xtqWywawQ6.one_liner: Trains one LLM as Organizer and Navigator via alternating RL to build a memory tree and retrieve along its paths.
xtqWywawQ6.problem: External LLM memory is an opaque black box, so without prior awareness of how contents are organized the LLM relies on exploratory queries and repeated retrieval (lack of memory priors).
xtqWywawQ6.method: The Organizer generates Semantic Paths that place atomic facts into a memory tree, and the Navigator follows these paths to retrieve evidence for downstream questions. Multi-round alternating RL uses retrieval performance as feedback to improve organization, and the resulting structures support later navigation training.
xtqWywawQ6.key_idea: Alternate RL updates between a memory Organizer that writes semantic paths and a Navigator that retrieves along them, so organization adapts to the model's own retrieval behavior.
xtqWywawQ6.evidence: Multiple benchmarks and backbones, including LoCoMo, LongMemEval, and NarrativeQA with Qwen3-4B and Qwen2.5-7B (from reviews), compared with baselines such as GAM.
xtqWywawQ6.claimed_gains: MEM-SONAR outperforms the compared baselines across multiple benchmarks and backbones (no figures in the abstract).
xtqWywawQ6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find trainable memory organization with question-driven navigation a promising, interpretable idea with consistent gains on LoCoMo, LongMemEval, and NarrativeQA.
xtqWywawQ6.main_concern: Experiments do not isolate alternating optimization from ordinary RL training or from simpler variants (Organizer-only, Navigator-only, joint, sequential) at matched compute, and cost and model-family coverage are limited.

k3GtChyDOV.one_liner: Derives scaling laws for label-corruption memorization in KANs and mitigates it by perturbing curvature-sensitive basis directions.
k3GtChyDOV.problem: Malign memorization under corrupted labels limits Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks, and it is unexplained how grid size G and spline degree p govern the resulting population damage.
k3GtChyDOV.method: Memorization is decomposed as M_c(t) = alpha_c(t)^2 V_c(t), corruption fitting times population footprint. In the localized regime of a two-layer B-spline KAN, grid refinement speeds fitting but contracts the footprint while higher degree slows fitting and widens it; CURB then perturbs curvature-sensitive basis directions during training to provably slow corruption fitting.
k3GtChyDOV.key_idea: Split memorization into corruption fitting and population footprint, then slow fitting by perturbing curvature-sensitive spline basis directions during training (CURB).
k3GtChyDOV.evidence: NTK-style theory for two-layer B-spline KANs, and experiments on function regression, Darcy-flow operator learning, and classification benchmarks (MNIST per reviews).
k3GtChyDOV.claimed_gains: Matched-fit memorization scales as M_c = Theta(alpha_c^2 sqrt(p) / G), and CURB reduces label-corruption fitting with competitive or superior accuracy (abstract truncated).
k3GtChyDOV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value separating fitting speed from population footprint, the clean NTK-based dependence on (G, p), and the fixed-time versus matched-fit distinction.
k3GtChyDOV.main_concern: The theory holds only in a localized, frozen-NTK two-layer regime that the experiments do not meet, and CURB lacks controlled comparisons with other perturbations, trails SAM and ASAM on smooth regression, and relies on single-run results.

LHMokpKYAC.one_liner: Proves that hard hidden computation in Transformers must leak information into chain-of-thought, though it can be encrypted.
LHMokpKYAC.problem: It is unknown whether reasoning models can perform hidden computation without revealing it in their thinking traces and thereby evade chain-of-thought monitors.
LHMokpKYAC.method: An information-theoretic analysis shows that beyond a task-difficulty threshold depending on model size, solving a covert task necessarily leaks a near-linear amount of information about the covert input into the CoT. A cryptographic construction shows that, under plausible assumptions, a one-layer Transformer can encrypt its reasoning online so no polynomial-time monitor extracts it.
LHMokpKYAC.key_idea: Lower-bound the input-to-trace information needed for computation beyond model capacity, and show under cryptographic assumptions that the leaked information can be made unreadable.
LHMokpKYAC.evidence: Theory (an information-theoretic lower bound and an encryption construction) plus prompting and finetuning experiments on covert tasks across model families (from reviews).
LHMokpKYAC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find a clean unifying framework (No CoT, Agnostic CoT, Informative CoT) with a substantive leakage lower bound and an encryption result that sharpens what CoT monitoring can guarantee.
LHMokpKYAC.main_concern: The bounds assume fixed-precision Transformers, uniform inputs, and exact computation, and experiments do not test whether a realistic monitor can detect or recover the leaked information.

0qsTfF8zdK.one_liner: Defends open-weight LLMs against refusal-direction ablation by editing MLP weights to inject decoy signals that corrupt the attacker's estimator.
0qsTfF8zdK.problem: Refusal Feature Ablation easily bypasses safety guardrails in open-weight LLMs, and defending against it usually requires expensive safety finetuning for every new checkpoint.
0qsTfF8zdK.method: DDO is a post-hoc weight-editing defense that needs no base-model finetuning: it injects a high-magnitude nonlinear decoy signal into MLP neurons so contrastive estimators of the refusal direction pick a harmless orthogonal feature, leaving the real safety mechanism intact. The authors prove a spectral bound formalizing the effect.
0qsTfF8zdK.key_idea: Instead of hiding the refusal circuitry, inject a nonlinear decoy signal into MLP neurons that corrupts contrastive refusal-direction estimates so the attacker ablates a harmless feature.
0qsTfF8zdK.evidence: Six model families under standard RFA, plus adaptive multi-phase attacks and Heretic weight-level attacks on Llama-3-8B-Instruct, with ablations and utility measurements.
0qsTfF8zdK.claimed_gains: Under 10% ASR under standard RFA across six model families; on Llama-3-8B-Instruct 65% vs. 58% worst-case ASR against trained defenses under adaptive attacks, and Heretic ASR reduced from 88.7% to 18%, at 30-450x lower optimization cost per configuration.
0qsTfF8zdK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see an intuitive, lightweight, low-compute defense with formal and empirical support, evaluated across model families and attack settings with limitations stated openly.
0qsTfF8zdK.main_concern: Defense-aware evaluation leaves attack routes untested (such as extracting directions from the edited weights), higher-rank and adaptive attacks still succeed, and reported ASR figures differ across tables.

vPMVN8B8IB.one_liner: Audits motion-caption metrics with one-fact-edit pairs, then proposes an attribute-wise judge and a motion VLM trained on the rubric.
vPMVN8B8IB.problem: Motion-caption metrics have not been tested attribute by attribute for noticing a single wrong motion fact such as acting side or direction, so weak models cannot be told apart from insensitive metrics.
vPMVN8B8IB.method: The authors build MotionADV, a Chinese-English set of caption pairs differing in exactly one fact from 494 artist-corrected clips, define the MotionFact rubric over a typed action schema, and build MotionJudge, which checks each attribute against a reference with its own questions. They also train Motion-VLM, which reads multi-view renders and motion tokens and states MotionFact facts.
vPMVN8B8IB.key_idea: Evaluate captions by decomposing them into typed motion attributes checked one by one against a reference, instead of scoring the whole caption with n-gram, embedding, or LLM-judge metrics.
vPMVN8B8IB.evidence: A minimal-pair audit on 494 artist-corrected clips, MotionJudge ablations with Qwen3.5-27B, and cross-dataset transfer of Motion-VLM.
vPMVN8B8IB.claimed_gains: Under one wrong fact, n-gram and embedding metrics move less than a fifth of the way to an unrelated caption, and with Qwen3.5-27B MotionJudge reaches a detection rate of at least 0.90 and a pass rate of at least 0.89 on every attribute.
vPMVN8B8IB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the controlled-edit audit exposing metric blind spots and the attribute-level feedback of MotionJudge, with clear presentation and ablations.
vPMVN8B8IB.main_concern: MotionJudge is not validated against human judgments and its edits, labels, and judge all rely on one model family, and the technical contribution is seen as modest with no single-call baseline.

uGFEvS0OXh.one_liner: Continuously maintained platform evaluating LLMs on olympiad, research-level, and formal-proof mathematics, including a false-claim benchmark.
uGFEvS0OXh.problem: Static benchmarks are narrow, quickly saturated, and rarely updated, which makes it hard to compare models reliably and track progress in mathematics.
uGFEvS0OXh.method: They extend MathArena into a platform that regularly evaluates new models, reviews their execution, and publishes analyses, with three research benchmarks: ArXivMath (final-answer questions), BrokenArXiv (responses to false claims), and ArXivLean (Lean proof generation).
uGFEvS0OXh.key_idea: Build benchmarks from recent arXiv research and update them as models are released, so evaluations stay current and contamination is reduced.
uGFEvS0OXh.evidence: Regular evaluations of new models on ArXivMath, BrokenArXiv, and ArXivLean, with released questions, prompts, model outputs, and code, and documented under-elicitation bugs per reviews.
uGFEvS0OXh.claimed_gains: The best-performing model, GPT-6 Astra, achieves 88% expected performance on the non-deprecated benchmarks.
uGFEvS0OXh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the live, regularly updated platform and the BrokenArXiv false-claim benchmark are useful and that the question-generation and validation pipeline is thorough.
uGFEvS0OXh.main_concern: Because the benchmark draws on public arXiv papers, answers or clues may be reachable by closed API models, and BrokenArXiv scoring cannot separate reliability from abstention (an always-false answerer would score 100%).

x0afYwOC12.one_liner: Boltzmann generator that reweights each denoising step using a conditional normalizing flow's exact likelihood within stochastic flow maps.
x0afYwOC12.problem: Generating independent equilibrium samples of molecular systems at scale is hard, and existing Boltzmann generators correct the generative model only at the end or rely on approximate or expensive likelihoods.
x0afYwOC12.method: NF2M parametrizes stochastic flow maps with conditional normalizing flows that propose clean configurations given the current noisy state, and uses their exact likelihood to correct each proposal toward the target's true denoising transition via self-normalized importance sampling. The paper proves consistency of the corrected transitions and bounds how errors propagate through the chain.
x0afYwOC12.key_idea: Each denoising transition is importance-weighted with the conditional normalizing flow's exact proposal density, so errors are corrected during generation instead of only at the end.
x0afYwOC12.evidence: Theory (consistency of corrected transitions, error-propagation bounds) and evaluation on peptide systems (including Chignolin per a reviewer) against flow-map baselines and SBG.
x0afYwOC12.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the corrected transition kernel with exact proposal densities is sound and well positioned against SBG and stochastic flow maps, giving consistent estimators with error guarantees.
x0afYwOC12.main_concern: The experiments are weak: strong recent Boltzmann generators (ArBG, Prose) are not compared, no simple setting shows the theoretical benefits, MIS is no better than IS on Chignolin, and the theory rests on unverified assumptions.

jts6KTjtAX.one_liner: Composes local diffusion constraint experts by running loopy belief propagation over clean assignments at each reverse diffusion step.
jts6KTjtAX.problem: Compositional diffusion has two unresolved issues: composing independently noised experts does not match noising a clean-space composition, and variables shared across constraints must resolve conflicting expert preferences.
jts6KTjtAX.method: At each diffusion step, CompDiff-BP builds a constraint-based factor graph for the posterior over clean assignments given the noisy state, uses belief propagation to approximate variable marginals, and uses their means to parameterize the next reverse step, without retraining the local experts.
jts6KTjtAX.key_idea: Do inference over clean assignments with loopy belief propagation on a constraint factor graph, then use the marginal means to drive each reverse step.
jts6KTjtAX.evidence: Boolean SAT, graph coloring, queen placement, and word-matching tasks, with a BP-depth ablation and comparisons against published compositional and neural baselines.
jts6KTjtAX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the factor-graph-plus-BP approach is well motivated, clearly presented, and general across problem structures, with the BP-depth ablation giving the clearest evidence.
jts6KTjtAX.main_concern: The contribution of BP is not fully separated from learned potentials and restricted answer spaces, with no convergence guarantees and no comparison to hard-coded potentials or established inference such as min-sum BP.

laRqPQDJnD.one_liner: Replaces the patch-independence prior of vision SAEs with a Markov spatial prior via smooth and innovation fields.
laRqPQDJnD.problem: Standard SAE objectives implicitly treat patch concepts as independent, which natural images and their activations violate, fragmenting visual concepts.
laRqPQDJnD.method: They state the Markov-Field Linear Representation Hypothesis (MFLRH), which adds spatial dependencies to the LRH, and propose Spatial-SAE as an amortized MAP estimator under it, using an MRF over patch codes.
laRqPQDJnD.key_idea: Estimate patch codes as an amortized MAP under a Markov random field prior over neighboring patches instead of an independent per-patch sparse code.
laRqPQDJnD.evidence: Synthetic concept recovery across four variants and interpretability evaluation on DINOv2 activations.
laRqPQDJnD.claimed_gains: Achieves a 96% average win rate on synthetic concept recovery across four variants and improves interpretability on DINOv2 activations, at a reconstruction cost concentrated in high spatial frequencies.
laRqPQDJnD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the implicit patch-independence prior is a well-motivated problem and that replacing it with a spatial model is intuitive, with evidence on synthetic ground truth and real DINOv2 activations.
laRqPQDJnD.main_concern: The metrics reward spatially smooth maps and may reflect smoothing rather than better concepts, the synthetic comparison may give the model oracle smooth and innovation streams, and the reconstruction drop is substantial.

0ROurBdGUk.one_liner: Parameterizes discrete diffusion by predicting a clean-token posterior mean mapped linearly to scores, enforcing Bayes realizability in SEDD.
0ROurBdGUk.problem: SEDD's unconstrained positive score ratios need not come from any valid clean-token posterior, and violations can create negative pre-normalization weights in the finite-step sampler.
0ROurBdGUk.method: In M2S the network predicts a clean-token posterior mean and converts it to the score through an exact kernel-dependent linear map, so scores are Bayes-realizable by construction rather than projected post hoc.
0ROurBdGUk.key_idea: Output a posterior mean over clean tokens and apply an exact kernel-dependent linear map to obtain the score, so every score lies in the realizable set.
0ROurBdGUk.evidence: Diagnostics on a trained pure-uniform SEDD checkpoint (about a quarter of score vectors violate the coordinate box) and a projection experiment; per reviews, M2S is evaluated on OpenWebText against baselines including GIDD-uniform.
0ROurBdGUk.claimed_gains: Projecting the checkpoint's raw scores onto the bridge polytope lowers external generative PPL from 203.6 to 175.1 without changing the sampler; M2S gains are not stated in the visible abstract.
0ROurBdGUk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the Bayes-realizability diagnosis of SEDD is a concrete, measurable, clearly presented insight that helps explain its underperformance.
0ROurBdGUk.main_concern: M2S changes the score set, output head, and sampler at once so gains cannot be attributed to Bayes realizability alone, and posterior parameterizations and key baselines (duo, cross-entropy training) are missing or not new.

tNw5IlVNpD.one_liner: Flow-matching nowcaster whose supervised hurdle-gated mixture-of-experts velocity field separates precipitation occurrence from conditional severity.
tNw5IlVNpD.problem: Generative nowcasting models handle light-to-moderate precipitation but struggle with rare high-intensity extremes because training optimizes an average loss with one shared set of generative dynamics.
tNw5IlVNpD.method: HurdleCast decomposes precipitation prediction into occurrence and conditional severity inside latent conditional flow matching. Two probabilistic gates route the latent flow dynamics among experts specialized for dry, moderate, and heavy precipitation.
tNw5IlVNpD.key_idea: Two supervised probabilistic gates route latent flow-matching velocity among dry, moderate, and heavy experts, following a hurdle model of occurrence then severity.
tNw5IlVNpD.evidence: Experiments on SEVIR and MeteoNet with competitive baselines, a single-head ablation, and CRPS evaluation on 60-minute forecasts.
tNw5IlVNpD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the hurdle decomposition is simple and well motivated for zero-inflated, heavy-tailed precipitation, adds fewer than 0.1% of backbone parameters, and helps at the highest intensity thresholds.
tNw5IlVNpD.main_concern: Reviewers question the probabilistic evaluation (CRPS from a fitted Gaussian), the high training cost and short horizon, and the missing comparison to prior mixture-of-experts precipitation work.

2pWNraq7cA.one_liner: Training-free flow-matching sampler that skips steps and corrects accumulated velocity error from a later residual, with adaptive skip scheduling.
2pWNraq7cA.problem: Step skipping in flow matching reuses cached velocities, and the resulting errors accumulate through the solver.
2pWNraq7cA.method: SnapCache keeps the original integration grid; at the next retained step a velocity residual reveals the error accumulated over the skipped interval without an extra model evaluation. Optimal Brain Trajectory Compensation (OBTC) estimates it and applies a minimum-change correction to the refreshed velocity or multistep history, while a causal scheduler picks the next skip interval by comparing predicted residual error with the solver's truncation-error scale.
2pWNraq7cA.key_idea: Treats step skipping like model-compression compensation: estimates skipped-interval error from the next retained step's residual and applies a minimum-norm correction.
2pWNraq7cA.evidence: Euler and UniPC solvers on FLUX.1-dev, Krea-2-Raw, and Wan2.2 (image and video), a few-step distilled model, and a qualitative LIBERO action-sampling rollout, with compensation ablations.
2pWNraq7cA.claimed_gains: Improves sample-fidelity trade-offs over the compared caching baselines at approximately 2x-4x fewer network forward passes.
2pWNraq7cA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like treating step skipping as retrospective error compensation that needs no extra model evaluation, and the coverage of image, video, and robot-action sampling.
2pWNraq7cA.main_concern: No measured wall-clock latency is reported (only forward-pass counts), and the linear-error estimator is unvalidated and inconsistent with Algorithm 1 as written.

u5k5jqCTHU.one_liner: Monocular drone navigation policy trained with forward and inverse latent-dynamics losses; the predictor is dropped at deployment.
u5k5jqCTHU.problem: World models for navigation feed predictions back into action generation at every control step, which is costly, while a policy mainly needs the representation required to produce the prediction.
u5k5jqCTHU.method: Skytopia trains an action-conditioned latent world model with a forward objective (predict the next observation's representation from intended motion) and an inverse objective (recover motion from the predicted transition), on a new 3D Gaussian Splatting platform. The predictor is discarded at deployment, so one policy serves point-goal, image-goal, and goal-free navigation.
u5k5jqCTHU.key_idea: Uses forward and inverse latent dynamics losses only as training supervision for the policy representation, so the predictor never reaches action generation and is removed at inference.
u5k5jqCTHU.evidence: Simulation under point-goal, image-goal, and goal-free navigation on a 3DGS platform (94 reconstructed scenes, 32.5 million rendered frames per reviews), plus zero-shot real-drone flights in three unseen sites reported by reviewers.
u5k5jqCTHU.claimed_gains: Success rates of 57.8%, 66.0%, and 49.0% under the three goal specifications, outperforming all evaluated baselines, while discarding the predictor removes 59.4% of the inference cost.
u5k5jqCTHU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the large 3DGS training platform, the zero-shot sim-to-real flights, and the inference savings from dropping the predictor.
u5k5jqCTHU.main_concern: Possible goal leakage through the 13-dimensional proprioceptive state, which contains the relative goal vector and may inflate the image-goal and goal-free results.

JLbPhgsExJ.one_liner: Sparse occupancy world model sharing one kinematic state per anchor across history sampling and future horizons, with hierarchical point refinement.
JLbPhgsExJ.problem: Recent sparse occupancy models do not couple historical evidence alignment and future prediction through a shared motion state, so moving content misaligns image feature sampling and horizons lack a common motion reference.
JLbPhgsExJ.method: KIO-World equips each query anchor with a horizon-shared kinematic state that compensates scene dynamics during historical feature sampling and provides references for future anchor evolution. A hierarchical residual point refinement module lets query points inherit parent geometry and decouples anchor-wise pose updates from point-wise shape refinement.
JLbPhgsExJ.key_idea: One horizon-shared kinematic state per anchor both motion-compensates historical feature sampling and anchors future query evolution, with parent-inherited hierarchical point refinement.
JLbPhgsExJ.evidence: Occupancy forecasting experiments across model sizes and evaluation settings, with ablations on motion-state sharing, soft versus hard rollout, and regularizers (mIoU and IoU reported in reviewer-cited tables).
JLbPhgsExJ.claimed_gains: not stated (the visible abstract claims top results but is cut off before giving figures).
JLbPhgsExJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that sharing a motion state between historical alignment and future prediction is a sensible design supported by state-sharing and soft-versus-hard rollout ablations.
JLbPhgsExJ.main_concern: The benefit of future-center regularization is unclear (about 0.2 IoU alone, larger only with the static-scene prior) and novelty over SparseBEV-style compensation and SnowflakeNet-style refinement is limited.

VNjcy5xYcF.one_liner: Iteratively adds task-vector increments for under-recovered domains during multi-teacher on-policy distillation, starting from a uniform merge.
VNjcy5xYcF.problem: Multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) can fail to recover some teacher capabilities, is sensitive to student initialization, and initial benchmark performance does not predict a good initialization.
VNjcy5xYcF.method: IM-MOPD starts from a uniform merge of teachers that share a reference model and, during distillation, progressively adds task-vector increments for domains that are under-recovered. It builds on the finding that effective merging depends on teacher contributions and overall merge scale, with some strong configurations outside the simplex of convex averaging.
VNjcy5xYcF.key_idea: Start MOPD from a uniform merge and progressively add task-vector increments for under-recovered domains during distillation instead of searching merge coefficients once.
VNjcy5xYcF.evidence: A 5-domain setting with mixed SFT and RLVR teachers on two small models (reviewers note 1.7B and 4B of one family), compared with uniform-merge and SFT warm-up initializations.
VNjcy5xYcF.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says IM-MOPD achieves higher average normalized recovery than MOPD with uniform merge initialization or SFT warm-up, without figures).
VNjcy5xYcF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the finding that initial performance does not predict post-MOPD quality is useful and well demonstrated, and that the method is simple with large headline gains.
VNjcy5xYcF.main_concern: Novelty and controls are limited: two same-family small models, single runs with test-set hyperparameter selection, and much of the gain may come from better final coefficients rather than iterating.

IkJDyUWfVA.one_liner: Clipped federated and gradient-tracking methods for hierarchical networks under generalized smoothness, with clipping at client and hub levels.
IkJDyUWfVA.problem: Hierarchical learning combines federated aggregation within client groups and decentralized communication across hubs, and under (H0,H1)-smoothness the descent inequality holds only for sufficiently small displacements.
IkJDyUWfVA.method: Clients clip gradients before aggregation, while hubs clip the optimization step and leave the gradient tracker unchanged. They prove nonconvex convergence for the federated, decentralized, and hierarchical methods, with accelerated dependence on the network spectral gap, and two-phase rates for convex objectives.
IkJDyUWfVA.key_idea: Two-level clipping (client gradients and hub steps) controls locality under (H0,H1)-smoothness, which is preserved under averaging with heterogeneity entering as an additive interpolation defect.
IkJDyUWfVA.evidence: Theoretical guarantees for nonconvex, convex (linear then O(1/K)), and strongly convex (linear) cases, with numerical simulations noted by reviewers.
IkJDyUWfVA.claimed_gains: not stated (theory paper: accelerated dependence on the network spectral gap and linear-then-sublinear convex convergence).
IkJDyUWfVA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is well structured with clearly formulated assumptions and strong convergence results, and that the hierarchical setting is clearly motivated.
IkJDyUWfVA.main_concern: The main technical contribution is hard to separate from established clipping, gradient tracking, and gossip techniques, and the practical motivation (no local steps, common-minimizer assumption) is thin.

iBUoTe3i4L.one_liner: OR-Space benchmarks LLM agents on building, revising, and explaining optimization models inside executable industrial workspaces.
iBUoTe3i4L.problem: Existing OR benchmarks test model construction from a self-contained problem statement, while industrial optimization also needs connecting requirements to data and code, revising models, and explaining solver results.
iBUoTe3i4L.method: A benchmark of executable workspaces containing business documents, structured data, code, solver outputs, and task-specific evaluators, with three separately scored tasks: BUILD, REVISE, and EXPLAIN.
iBUoTe3i4L.key_idea: Evaluate model construction, revision under changed requirements while preserving prior logic, and evidence-grounded explanation separately inside executable workspaces of heterogeneous artifacts.
iBUoTe3i4L.evidence: 16 language models on 100 base problems instantiated as 300 task instances, with controlled studies of workspace interface, revision context, and solver backend.
iBUoTe3i4L.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark addresses a relevant gap by separating build, revise, and explain capabilities and provides broad, informative experiments.
iBUoTe3i4L.main_concern: Success is judged by execution plus an objective value close to the reference, which does not verify that the submitted model's constraints and feasible region are correct.

HYggbHw3tq.one_liner: SHARE reuses a small set of high-rank trainable parameter banks across layers and modules, grouped by update shape.
HYggbHw3tq.problem: High-rank PEFT methods keep separate trainable parameters per target weight matrix, leaving open whether high-rank adaptation can share parameters across layers and modules.
HYggbHw3tq.method: SHARE organizes target weight matrices by update shape and assigns them to banks of trainable parameters, so matrices in the same bank reuse one high-rank update that is constructed once during training. A first-order analysis shows fixed sharing is a reparameterization of the weight updates.
HYggbHw3tq.key_idea: Assign weight matrices of the same update shape to a shared parameter bank so one high-rank update is built once and reused by all of them.
HYggbHw3tq.evidence: Commonsense reasoning, mathematical reasoning, and code generation across multiple backbones against PEFT baselines at matched trainable-parameter budgets, plus training throughput.
HYggbHw3tq.claimed_gains: Consistently outperforms strong PEFT baselines while achieving competitive training throughput; no numbers stated.
HYggbHw3tq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree high-rank adaptation with sharing is a natural extension supported by a simple first-order analysis and consistently strong results across three backbones and task families.
HYggbHw3tq.main_concern: Baselines look insufficiently tuned or limited (VeRA and ShareLoRA are not compared), SHARE has lower throughput than LoRA and needs extra caching memory, and the gains over close competitors are small.

yUy3ObMwyf.one_liner: Grounds multi-agent traffic simulation in a self-supervised LiDAR-occupancy world model with DPP-guided diverse sampling.
yUy3ObMwyf.problem: Data-driven simulators learn from lossy abstractions such as 3D boxes and polylines that discard the sensory context shaping agent behavior, limiting distributional realism.
yUy3ObMwyf.method: AutoWorld trains a self-supervised world model on LiDAR occupancy and builds a coarse-to-fine predictive scene context for a multi-agent motion generation model, with a motion-aware latent supervision objective. A cascaded Determinantal Point Process framework guides sampling in both the world model and the motion model to promote diversity.
yUy3ObMwyf.key_idea: Condition motion generation on sampled LiDAR-occupancy world-model futures with motion-aware latent supervision, and apply cascaded DPP guidance to diversify both stages.
yUy3ObMwyf.evidence: Experiments on nuPlan and Waymo with ablations, covering realism, physical plausibility, reactiveness, and controllability, with larger gains in partially observed scenarios.
yUy3ObMwyf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that grounding behavior in sensor-derived scene representations is well motivated and that the two-benchmark evaluation and ablations show consistent improvements.
yUy3ObMwyf.main_concern: Contributions are incremental and not cleanly attributed (most gain comes from adding LiDAR features), the DPP component is heavy for its gain, and grounding is LiDAR-only.

PGEbfIPX7h.one_liner: Lifetime-aware memory with separate identity, active-event, and completed-event stores for streaming sports commentary.
PGEbfIPX7h.problem: Streaming commentary must track identities, unfolding actions, and when to speak using only the video observed so far, but these semantic states have different useful lifetimes.
PGEbfIPX7h.method: GroundedPlay keeps identity evidence across events, updates active event states, and retains completed outputs as episodic context. It learns reciprocal interactions between identity and action representations, while a completion predictor guides evidence accumulation and updated event states help predict whether the current event has ended.
PGEbfIPX7h.key_idea: Maintain entity, event, and episodic memories with different retention policies, couple identity and action representations bidirectionally, and use event-completion prediction to gate evidence accumulation.
PGEbfIPX7h.evidence: Experiments on NBA_Streaming and MatchTime-SID measuring event response timing, commentary quality, and throughput against baselines, with lifetime ablations described in reviews.
PGEbfIPX7h.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating persistent identity, evolving action, and completed-event memory matches the structure of live commentary, supported by lifetime ablations.
PGEbfIPX7h.main_concern: Methodological novelty is limited and the central notion of lifetime is predefined and not clearly defined or isolated by ablations, with weak cross-domain evidence on MatchTime-SID.

XgYh8jfypi.one_liner: Replaces fully satisfied rubric criteria per sample with checks targeting remaining quality differences during rubric-based RL for open-ended generation.
XgYh8jfypi.problem: In rubric-based RL, criteria become fully satisfied and lose discrimination as the policy improves, and dynamic methods that revise rubrics may also change useful criteria.
XgYh8jfypi.method: RARE uses current policy feedback to choose which criteria change and what their replacements assess: sample-level updates replace criteria fully satisfied across current outputs with checks of remaining quality differences, keeping all other criteria and scores. It compares rewarding desired qualities with penalizing observed flaws, tested on video script generation.
XgYh8jfypi.key_idea: Detect saturated criteria from current-output scores and swap only those for flaw-targeting checks generated from observed output differences, leaving other criteria and scores untouched.
XgYh8jfypi.evidence: Video script generation, with comparisons against fixed-rubric and dynamic-rubric baselines, replacement-strategy analyses, and model and human preference judgments.
XgYh8jfypi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method addresses a concrete limitation of static rubrics with a simple mechanism, and that blinded human assessment and baseline comparisons support the improvements.
XgYh8jfypi.main_concern: Experiments do not isolate saturation-based selective replacement from other changes, novelty is limited, and GPT-5.4 acting as both rubric reviser and judge raises circularity concerns.

Z4wVtY7PrV.one_liner: Hallucination detector: shared MLP over token features, feature-wise max pooling, linear head, motivated by margin analysis of HaMI.
Z4wVtY7PrV.problem: Hybrid hallucination detectors like HaMI combine semantic consistency with internal states via multiple instance learning but need repeated sampling and semantic comparisons that add substantial compute.
Z4wVtY7PrV.method: The authors analyze HaMI's decision margins to identify when semantic-probability scaling enlarges the average logit margin, then propose a detector in which a shared MLP extracts token-level features, feature-wise max pooling aggregates them, and a linear head scores the response, with no extra sampling or semantic consistency computation.
Z4wVtY7PrV.key_idea: Aggregate token-level MLP features with feature-wise max pooling so a single response's hidden states suffice, replacing HaMI's semantic-probability weighting.
Z4wVtY7PrV.evidence: Four QA benchmarks and three LLMs, plus LongFact++ with web-verified entity labels on two LLMs.
Z4wVtY7PrV.claimed_gains: Competitive with semantically weighted HaMI in detection AUC while adding a median of 0.5% to end-to-end response time, whereas semantically weighted HaMI takes 7-34 times as long.
Z4wVtY7PrV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method gives a relevant accuracy-cost trade-off, with competitive detection without extra sampling and well-controlled mean versus max pooling and architecture ablations.
Z4wVtY7PrV.main_concern: The theory has limited explanatory power for the empirical gains, novelty over existing max-pooling aggregation is unclear, and long-form labels come from an automated judge.

UKDjPeyA5i.one_liner: Predicts per-location Gabor atom parameters with a network and builds dual frames for exact reconstruction in self-supervised image restoration.
UKDjPeyA5i.problem: Image restoration benefits from representations that adapt to local structure while keeping explicit reconstruction guarantees, which fixed or purely implicit representations lack.
UKDjPeyA5i.method: A neural network predicts the scales, orientations, and frequencies of Gabor atoms aligned with edges and textures, and corresponding dual frames give perfect reconstruction under suitable conditions. Coefficient sparsity is used in self-supervised denoising, inpainting, and super-resolution trained without ground-truth images.
UKDjPeyA5i.key_idea: Image-conditioned local Gabor parameters define a spatially varying frame whose dual frame gives an explicit analysis-synthesis formula for coefficient-based processing.
UKDjPeyA5i.evidence: Denoising on Kodak24, McMaster18, SIDD, and FMD and super-resolution and inpainting on Set14 per reviews, with ablations on spatial adaptation and Gaussian atoms and theorems on frame preservation and dual construction.
UKDjPeyA5i.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says competitive performance on denoising, inpainting, and super-resolution without numbers)
UKDjPeyA5i.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it gives an interpretable representation with an exact reconstruction identity, competitive ground-truth-free denoising, and ablations that support spatial adaptation.
UKDjPeyA5i.main_concern: Novelty is limited relative to non-stationary Gabor frames, GDLNet, and learned dictionaries, and comparisons with closely related learnable dictionaries are insufficient.

eDSegdbDwP.one_liner: Online multiplier bootstrap runs weighted parallel Riemannian SGD paths to give confidence regions for averaged manifold estimates without covariance estimation.
eDSegdbDwP.problem: Uncertainty assessment for manifold-valued estimates from averaged Riemannian stochastic approximation normally needs a plug-in asymptotic covariance estimator.
eDSegdbDwP.method: Weighted iterations run alongside the original algorithm on the same observations, each path updating its own state and intrinsic average. A fixed number of paths gives Student intervals and intrinsic confidence regions, and the theory covers samplewise nonsmooth scores.
eDSegdbDwP.key_idea: Perturb each observation with random multipliers in parallel Riemannian SGD runs and use the spread of their intrinsic averages as the sampling distribution of the estimate.
eDSegdbDwP.evidence: Theory under local stability and regularity conditions (bootstrap consistency and an oracle-bias regime), applications to spherical means, positive-definite matrix means and medians, and principal-subspace estimation, simulations, and North Atlantic storm locations.
eDSegdbDwP.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says simulations show coverage close to nominal in regular settings, without numbers)
eDSegdbDwP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it offers a unified, rigorous framework across several manifold problems with clearly stated theorems under general assumptions and a clear computational motivation.
eDSegdbDwP.main_concern: Novelty is seen as limited because the algorithm and Student calibration are inherited from the Euclidean cheap online bootstrap and related work, with the extension being geometric.

dgdMUb281p.one_liner: Trains LVLMs with GRPO to substitute entropy-trough-layer tokens for final-layer tokens when an evidence verifier judges the shift unsupported.
dgdMUb281p.problem: Overthinking in large vision-language models is mostly controlled at the token-sequence level, ignoring that entropy can reach a trough at intermediate layers and rebound with depth, causing unnecessary extra reasoning.
dgdMUb281p.method: An entropy trigger finds the layer where entropy rebounds from its trough, and an evidence verifier judges whether the resulting token preference shift is supported; unsupported final-layer tokens are replaced by the trough-layer token. The GRPO reward uses changes in reasoning length and final-answer correctness under trough-token substitution, with verifier supervision from token-shift outcomes.
dgdMUb281p.key_idea: Detect cross-layer entropy rebounds and, when a learned verifier finds the final-layer token shift unsupported, replace it with the entropy-trough-layer token during reasoning rollouts.
dgdMUb281p.evidence: Experiments across seven reasoning benchmarks; reviews add 3B, 7B, and 32B models, ablations, and comparison with GRPO and FAST-GRPO.
dgdMUb281p.claimed_gains: not stated; the visible abstract is cut off after 'Experiments across seven reasoning benchmarks demonstrate'.
dgdMUb281p.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the layer-wise entropy view of overthinking a fresh, intuitive complement to sequence-level length control, with experiments across model sizes and benchmarks supporting the components.
dgdMUb281p.main_concern: Gains may come mainly from inference-time trough-token substitution rather than GRPO training, and controls such as baselines with the same substitution, DoLa-style layer selection, or a length penalty are missing.

rP59823YbY.one_liner: Scores crystal generators separately for distribution matching and discovery using a multi-probe stability panel and set-level kernels.
rP59823YbY.problem: Classical generative metrics evaluate only distribution reproduction, while S.U.N.-style metrics are reported as discovery progress without declaring the aim, even though the two aims prescribe different optimal output distributions.
rP59823YbY.method: GEMBench scores GEM-match and GEM-disc separately under explicit stability-probe and crystal-similarity choices, using a shared stability panel (energy above hull, phonon, and finite-temperature checks) and excluding near-duplicates of training crystals.
rP59823YbY.key_idea: Evaluate matching and discovery as separate scores on a shared multi-probe stability panel: GEM-match rewards dataset-like distribution shape, GEM-disc rewards a large, diverse set of stable structures.
rP59823YbY.evidence: Evaluation on public generative models (the abstract text is cut off); reviews mention MACE-MP embedding kernels and ML-potential-based stability checks.
rP59823YbY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating matching from discovery and replacing the single energy-above-hull bit with multi-probe stability is a well-organized, mathematically grounded evaluation protocol.
rP59823YbY.main_concern: Reliance on machine-learned interatomic potentials without DFT validation, which are imprecise near small hull energies, plus MACE-MP embedding kernels.

rdOZJvrUnF.one_liner: GeoAct nudges a world action model's action toward the arm pose read from its generated video, using forward kinematics.
rdOZJvrUnF.problem: World action models generate video and action jointly, but the training loss does not tie them to robot kinematics, so the two outputs can describe different arm motions.
rdOZJvrUnF.method: At selected denoising steps, a frozen geometric backbone and trained joint readout estimate arm configurations from the clean video prediction; forward kinematics places this estimate and the predicted action in the base frame, a bounded proximal step moves the action toward the visual estimate, and the corrected action is reinjected at the current noise level and the model re-evaluated.
rdOZJvrUnF.key_idea: Bounded proximal correction of the clean action toward a kinematics-based estimate read from the predicted video, reinjected mid-sampling so later video generation responds.
rdOZJvrUnF.evidence: LIBERO and RoboTwin 2.0 on a shared backbone, compared with post-hoc correction using the same readout and budget, with ablations on fresh readout and update bound, and a latency measurement.
rdOZJvrUnF.claimed_gains: Task success rises from 94.5% to 97.5% on LIBERO and from 81.8% to 89.0% on RoboTwin 2.0 (post-hoc correction reaches 95.6% and 83.9%), at 1.22x base latency for two interventions per action chunk.
rdOZJvrUnF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the kinematics-grounded comparison of video and action is meaningful and that correcting during generation, rather than post-hoc, gives measured gains on LIBERO and RoboTwin 2.0.
rdOZJvrUnF.main_concern: It is unclear when the video should be trusted over the action, since both come from the same generator and may share the same error, and generalization beyond the chosen backbone and readout accuracy on generated videos are unverified.

isaVxUY5zV.one_liner: Module-specific norms and calibrated perturbation scales guide gradient-free sampling of language-model ensembles.
isaVxUY5zV.problem: RandOpt uses a global perturbation scale that ignores differences in module geometry.
isaVxUY5zV.method: Modular Norm RandOpt assigns natural norms to modules and calibrates their perturbation scales using module allocation and sensitivity corrections. It retains candidate selection and plurality voting.
isaVxUY5zV.key_idea: Sample weight perturbations with module-specific natural norms and sensitivity-calibrated scales, then select candidates and ensemble their votes.
isaVxUY5zV.evidence: Experiments cover seven tasks and three Qwen scales, with additional Countdown and GSM8K evaluations on Llama 3.2 3B and Gemma 3 4B.
isaVxUY5zV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize that changing the perturbation distribution produces measurable ensemble accuracy improvements.
isaVxUY5zV.main_concern: The ablations do not cleanly isolate modular geometry from perturbation magnitude and other components.

jhgGm1zUuG.one_liner: Multi-scale target supervision and clean-prediction regularization inject backdoors into visual autoregressive image generators.
jhgGm1zUuG.problem: Backdoor vulnerabilities in visual autoregressive text-to-image models remain poorly characterized.
jhgGm1zUuG.method: ScaleTrojan combines multi-scale target learning with regularization against a frozen pretrained model and studies adaptation subspaces. A detector checks cross-scale prediction consistency under textual perturbations.
jhgGm1zUuG.key_idea: Fit triggered targets across visual scales while regularizing clean predictions against the frozen pretrained model.
jhgGm1zUuG.evidence: Experiments on Infinity 2B and STAR include supervision and regularization ablations, injection-subspace comparisons, and fixed-image, style, and patch objectives.
jhgGm1zUuG.claimed_gains: ScaleTrojan achieves nearly 100% attack success rate (ASR) while largely preserving clean generation quality.
jhgGm1zUuG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the effective backdoor attack and informative analyses of injection choices.
jhgGm1zUuG.main_concern: Apparently similar target-fitting baselines and ablations produce substantially different results without clear explanations of their training differences.

vSVMNpdWJB.one_liner: Posterior approximation and concentration theory characterize causal discovery models under pretraining misspecification and identifiability limits.
vSVMNpdWJB.problem: It is unclear what pretrained causal discovery models recover when causal graphs are non-identifiable or data fall outside their simulator family.
vSVMNpdWJB.method: The framework characterizes convergence toward the graph posterior induced by the pretraining prior and its large-sample recovery targets. A concrete model uses discrete diffusion over topological-order permutations to represent order uncertainty while ensuring acyclic graphs.
vSVMNpdWJB.key_idea: Separate learning the simulator-induced graph posterior from its concentration on KL-best-fitting graphs, equivalence classes, or identifiable DAGs.
vSVMNpdWJB.evidence: Theoretical guarantees address misspecification and identifiability, while graph-recovery experiments include smaller and larger graphs and a LiNGAM setting.
vSVMNpdWJB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the statistical account of what pretraining learns and what observational data can identify.
vSVMNpdWJB.main_concern: The posterior-learning theory is disconnected from the proposed model's training objective and lacks direct posterior-quality validation.

BM2J0wXm7r.one_liner: A learned cut-position head redirects frozen reasoners by inserting a user turn and regenerating the failed suffix.
BM2J0wXm7r.problem: LLMs struggle to locate and correct errors in their own reasoning without expensive model fine-tuning.
BM2J0wXm7r.method: UPTURN trains a 130K-parameter MLP on a frozen encoder using final-answer correctness to choose intervention positions. It preserves the selected prefix, inserts a fixed instruction as a new user turn, and regenerates the suffix.
BM2J0wXm7r.key_idea: Learn where to truncate failed reasoning and redirect continuation through a new user message instead of an inline instruction.
BM2J0wXm7r.evidence: Experiments cover four reasoners and six math benchmarks, matched-budget correction baselines, intervention ablations, and transfer to GPQA-Diamond.
BM2J0wXm7r.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the lightweight correction design and ablations supporting learned positions and user-turn injection.
BM2J0wXm7r.main_concern: Gains shrink with larger generation budgets, and experiments do not distinguish correcting reasoning from rescuing truncated responses.

doS5M6jeyc.one_liner: Recorded browser workflows define and verify software-repair tasks created by deleting dependent application behaviors.
doS5M6jeyc.problem: Web-development specifications often exist as working reference software rather than explicit issues, instructions, or tests.
doS5M6jeyc.method: ProgramDistill's mine--craft--patch pipeline records browser workflows, removes their implementing code, and verifies repairs by workflow replay. Masking multiple dependent behaviors controls restoration depth while agents inspect a live reference with hidden source.
doS5M6jeyc.key_idea: Use recorded application interactions as both behavioral specifications and executable verifiers after masking the code that implements them.
doS5M6jeyc.evidence: The benchmark contains 4,063 tasks from 26 applications and evaluates nine frontier agents across restoration depths and whole-application rebuilding.
doS5M6jeyc.claimed_gains: GPT-6 Astra drops from 100% at depth 1 to 64.0% at depth 8, the best agent passes 49.2% of whole-application workflows, and 59.2% of unrecovered behaviors were never observed in the reference.
doS5M6jeyc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value executable reference-guided tasks and systematic automated construction with repair checks.
doS5M6jeyc.main_concern: Fixed-workflow replay and missing independent task audits leave unclear whether passing patches restore behavior beyond the recorded traces.

HWKfdKzx9L.one_liner: Pooled binary response agreement trains and recalibrates reasoning-model confidence without correctness labels.
HWKfdKzx9L.problem: Reasoning-model confidence is poorly calibrated when labels are unavailable and repeated sampling is expensive.
HWKfdKzx9L.method: BASC treats agreement between an anchor answer and one independent probe as a Bernoulli observation of latent self-consistency. It pools observations to recalibrate confidence or learn a score before held-out binary isotonic recalibration.
HWKfdKzx9L.key_idea: Use one anchor-probe agreement bit per query as unbiased supervision for latent self-consistency, then apply isotonic recalibration.
HWKfdKzx9L.evidence: Experiments span 5 tasks and 9 reasoning models, and binary-isotonic theory guarantees calibration to latent self-consistency.
HWKfdKzx9L.claimed_gains: BASC uses as few as two responses per calibration query and only one at deployment.
HWKfdKzx9L.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the simple, low-sampling-budget use of agreement supervision without correctness labels.
HWKfdKzx9L.main_concern: The incremental contribution and comparison against existing uncertainty-amortization and calibration methods are insufficiently established.

NjYeGjdE2S.one_liner: Executor-maintained state, token-specific advantages, and capability-calibrated skill planning support long-horizon mobile GUI tasks.
NjYeGjdE2S.problem: End-to-end GUI agents struggle with long tasks, while hierarchical assistance can add substantial inference overhead.
NjYeGjdE2S.method: EASE-UI maintains its own state and uses TAPO to assign separate training advantages to action and history token spans. EASE-Agent adds sparse strong-model planning through skill memory whose subgoal granularity matches executor capabilities.
NjYeGjdE2S.key_idea: Separate action and state-summary training signals and calibrate planned subgoal granularity to the executor's demonstrated capabilities.
NjYeGjdE2S.evidence: GUI-Odyssey evaluates the executor and TAPO against GRPO and GDPO, while MemGUI-Bench tests online task success, costs, and skill-memory ablations.
NjYeGjdE2S.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize practical state and skill-memory mechanisms and useful performance and component evaluations.
NjYeGjdE2S.main_concern: The technical contribution beyond established planner-executor systems and history summarization needs clearer differentiation.

ddLqjwcuU7.one_liner: Hierarchical physical memories supply scene, event, and rule evidence for training-free video plausibility verification.
ddLqjwcuU7.problem: Video-language models remain unreliable at judging physical plausibility despite strong conventional visual question answering.
ddLqjwcuU7.method: PhysMRV builds a reusable memory bank of scene descriptions, event graphs, and physics-rule summaries. At inference, it retrieves relevant memories to guide a VLM's plausibility verification without parameter updates.
ddLqjwcuU7.key_idea: Retrieve physical evidence at scene, interaction, and rule levels and use it to verify a video's physical plausibility.
ddLqjwcuU7.evidence: ImplausiBench, IntPhys2, and GRASP Level 2 evaluations span four VLM backbones and include retrieval and shuffled-memory ablations.
ddLqjwcuU7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the physical-reasoning problem and the training-free reuse of structured memories across backbones.
ddLqjwcuU7.main_concern: Near-chance results and shifts in plausible-versus-implausible answer tendencies leave the claimed improvement in physical discrimination uncertain.

Nmz44oubGz.one_liner: Evidence-linked execution claims and independent tool-based verification trigger diagnosis-guided retries for search agents.
Nmz44oubGz.problem: Search agents can retrieve relevant evidence yet answer incorrectly because they fail to inspect it, verify premises, or stop error propagation.
Nmz44oubGz.method: EAV archives raw observations and maintains a compact evidence chain linking adopted claims to sources and conflicts. An independent verifier seeks fresh evidence for high-risk premises, and rejected answers trigger re-execution that retains evidence memory.
Nmz44oubGz.key_idea: Anchor intermediate claims to archived observations and independently challenge high-risk premises with fresh tool evidence before retrying failed execution.
Nmz44oubGz.evidence: Matched-backbone experiments include GAIA text-only validation, xBench-DeepSearch, and BrowseComp-ZH, with component and efficiency analyses.
Nmz44oubGz.claimed_gains: EAV-Flash attains an average success rate of 82.64\%, 3.69 points above MiroFlow across nine matched-backbone settings.
Nmz44oubGz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the evidence-anchoring design and broad empirical performance across benchmarks and backbones.
Nmz44oubGz.main_concern: Verification is coupled with additional re-execution, so current controls do not isolate its benefit at comparable total compute.

YRt6FnBCWF.one_liner: Step-boundary prefix segmentation and shortest-sufficient-prefix reward amplification compress chain-of-thought reasoning via reinforcement learning.
YRt6FnBCWF.problem: Length-based RL rewards for chain-of-thought efficiency ignore query-specific model capacity, encouraging futile long traces on beyond-capability queries and failing to pinpoint stopping points on near-capability queries.
YRt6FnBCWF.method: RazorReward-RL segments chain-of-thought trajectories at natural reasoning step boundaries into semantically coherent prefixes and probes early-exit answers from each prefix. Its RazorReward function sharply amplifies the reward gap in favor of the shortest prefix that reaches a correct answer.
YRt6FnBCWF.key_idea: Segment chain-of-thought rollouts at natural step boundaries into prefixes and amplify the RL reward gap toward the shortest sufficient prefix.
YRt6FnBCWF.evidence: Experiments span three model scales up to 14B across mathematical, non-math, and Chinese benchmarks, accompanied by prefix-correctness and behavioral trace analyses.
YRt6FnBCWF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that optimizing chain-of-thought token efficiency around the first sufficient prefix is well-motivated, intuitive, and empirically effective across model scales, domains, and languages.
YRt6FnBCWF.main_concern: Reviewers view the method as an incremental refinement over S-GRPO's serial prefix framework and note that negative advantages from short failed prefixes can penalize shared valid early steps.

QC5FvvEe7T.one_liner: Multi-round beam search over line-lifted relation graphs performs multi-hop RAG retrieval without LLM calls.
QC5FvvEe7T.problem: Graph-based retrieval-augmented generation typically relies on per-query LLM calls for query decomposition and traversal, creating deployment latency and cost bottlenecks.
QC5FvvEe7T.method: LiftRAG transforms an extracted knowledge graph into its line graph by representing each relation as a vertex carrying its evidence-sentence embedding. Multi-hop retrieval then runs a training-free multi-round beam search over entity-relation trajectories where query decomposition emerges from frontier expansion without LLM calls.
QC5FvvEe7T.key_idea: Lift extracted knowledge-graph relations into vertices carrying evidence-sentence embeddings and run multi-round beam search over entity-relation trajectories without LLM decomposition.
QC5FvvEe7T.evidence: Evaluations run on entity-grounded test sets of three multi-hop question-answering benchmarks across four metrics against baselines including LightRAG and HippoRAG 2.
QC5FvvEe7T.claimed_gains: LiftRAG leads published baselines on all four metrics across three multi-hop benchmarks, achieving accuracy margins of 5.7–10.0 points over LightRAG and 0.9–3.9 points over HippoRAG 2 at 13–25× lower retrieval latency in API deployment.
QC5FvvEe7T.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that eliminating retrieval-time LLM calls via relation-vertex embeddings and trajectory beam search is a lightweight, training-free, and well-motivated design for multi-hop graph RAG.
QC5FvvEe7T.main_concern: Reviewers note limited algorithmic novelty in combining line-graph lifting with beam search and point out missing comparisons with recent LLM-free graph RAG methods such as LinearRAG, E2GraphRAG, and GFM-RAG.

R8rI4Al23r.one_liner: Basis-SDM learns determinantal distributions over compatible LP bases using certificate-derived targets and conditional-greedy decoding.
R8rI4Al23r.problem: Crossover methods designed for interior-point solutions recover vertices and bases inefficiently from first-order LP solver outputs.
R8rI4Al23r.method: Basis-SDM assigns order-invariant probabilities to complete bases, uses a determinant factor to exclude singular column sets, and derives target families from optimality certificates. Exact KL supervision trains distribution updates before conditional-greedy selection and simplex cleanup.
R8rI4Al23r.key_idea: A determinantal set distribution models column compatibility while certificate-conditioned target families supervise multiple valid optimal bases.
