R8rI4Al23r.evidence: Experiments evaluate 111 unseen LPs with primal–dual hybrid gradient and interior-point inputs against native COPT crossover and LP-GNN.
R8rI4Al23r.claimed_gains: Basis-SDM reduces cleanup iteration sGM from 367.99 to 43.66 for primal–dual hybrid gradient inputs and from 518.52 to 4.74 for interior-point inputs, versus 274.40 for KKT-adapted LP-GNN on the latter, with no cleanup on 64 instances.
R8rI4Al23r.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that set-valued determinantal prediction and certificate-derived target families match the mathematical structure of LP bases.
R8rI4Al23r.main_concern: Reviewers find that the comparisons do not sufficiently isolate the learned distribution updates and joint modeling from initialization, supervision, and decoding.

xHut8bTSrd.one_liner: Embedding differences between rendered words and matched controls reveal lexical semantic organization in image-only DINOv3 models.
xHut8bTSrd.problem: It is unclear whether image-only self-supervision can produce word representations organized by meaning beyond spelling similarity.
xHut8bTSrd.method: The paper extracts word representations by subtracting matched-control embeddings from rendered-word embeddings and tests semantic neighborhoods with spelling controls. It also compares word-object alignment and text or speech representations and applies contrastive fine-tuning.
xHut8bTSrd.key_idea: Subtracting matched visual-control embeddings isolates rendered-word representations for spelling-controlled tests of semantic structure.
xHut8bTSrd.evidence: DINOv3-H and DINOv3-7B evaluations examine brand and noun categories, country-capital relations, word-object alignment, cross-modal representations, and contrastive fine-tuning.
xHut8bTSrd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the emergence of lexical semantic structure under image-only training interesting and value the varied semantic and cross-modal experiments.
xHut8bTSrd.main_concern: Reviewers question whether the tested relationships, especially country-capital offsets, support the breadth of the semantic claims.

LBjoEeJ5oP.one_liner: ControlTrace reconstructs diffusion control fields with a U-Net before asking a VLM to recognize hidden image content.
LBjoEeJ5oP.problem: VLMs miss hidden words and contours in generated images, while transformation-based recovery depends on selected parameters and views.
LBjoEeJ5oP.method: ControlTrace trains an 8.4M-parameter U-Net to recover the grayscale conditioning field from a carrier image, then passes the recovered field to a VLM. FreqBlind benchmarks contours, words, and non-words at different conditioning strengths.
LBjoEeJ5oP.key_idea: Supervised recovery of the generator's grayscale control field exposes embedded content for downstream VLM recognition.
LBjoEeJ5oP.evidence: FreqBlind contains 6,000 images; experiments compare transformation methods across four VLMs and test JPEG compression, Gaussian noise, and downsampling.
LBjoEeJ5oP.claimed_gains: With Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct, ControlTrace achieves 60.2% contour accuracy, exceeds the best evaluated prior method by 26.9 percentage points, and adds 7.4 ms (5.3%) on an A100 GPU.
LBjoEeJ5oP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize substantial contour-recognition gains, especially under weak conditioning, and extensive supporting experiments.
LBjoEeJ5oP.main_concern: Reviewers question generalization beyond the training generator, citing weak cross-generator transfer and limited external validation.

UjqwuBa2K2.one_liner: AudioScape-TTA converts verified soundscape annotations into semantic rubrics scored by an audio-language model and ASR.
UjqwuBa2K2.problem: Global text-audio similarity scores do not reveal which requirements complex audio-generation prompts satisfy or omit.
UjqwuBa2K2.method: AudioScape-TTA annotates scene context, sound effects, music, and speech, then derives fixed event, attribute, and speech-content rubrics. An audio-language model evaluates events and attributes while a separate ASR pathway scores speech coverage.
UjqwuBa2K2.key_idea: Fixed annotation-derived semantic rubrics separate event and attribute judgments from ASR-based speech-content coverage.
UjqwuBa2K2.evidence: The benchmark contains 2,258 audio-text pairs and 25,707 rubrics, evaluates 13 open-source models, and includes a human-study subset.
UjqwuBa2K2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the structured, reusable benchmark and its interpretable evaluation of multiple soundscape components.
UjqwuBa2K2.main_concern: Fine-grained evaluator reliability lacks sufficient rubric-level human validation on generated audio.

3BBdKt267i.one_liner: A permutation-calibrated geometric scan combines diffusion features and distance critics, residualizing distance features to reduce irrelevant variance.
3BBdKt267i.problem: Distributional changes in manifold-valued observations can preserve location summaries and remain difficult to detect despite visible feature contrasts.
3BBdKt267i.method: The scan combines multiscale diffusion features with geodesic distance critics and jointly permutes all channels for null calibration. It projects distance features off a finite diffusion span and analyzes signal retention, variance reduction, and localization.
3BBdKt267i.key_idea: Projecting distance features off a zero-contrast diffusion span preserves the change contrast while reducing variance unrelated to it.
3BBdKt267i.evidence: Finite-sample type-I control, feature-drift and localization theory, and circle, sphere, and torus experiments support the construction.
3BBdKt267i.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the rigorous statistical construction and its explanation of how variance allocation affects geometric change detection.
3BBdKt267i.main_concern: Reviewers find practical relevance insufficiently demonstrated by idealized manifold simulations without evaluation on the motivating application.

Uw2EDUQtIg.one_liner: TRAPE learns continuous axial attention biases and exports compact tables that slice and blend independently across image dimensions.
Uw2EDUQtIg.problem: Vision transformers trained at one resolution often lose accuracy at larger resolutions or different aspect ratios.
Uw2EDUQtIg.method: TRAPE combines continuous log-offset functions with local correction tables and a bounded shared amplitude. Position-only adaptation at square resolutions produces per-axis tables that independently slice and blend for unseen shapes without a positional network.
Uw2EDUQtIg.key_idea: Fixed-reference axial bias functions produce nested tables, while independently blended height and width tapes serve variable image shapes.
Uw2EDUQtIg.evidence: Experiments cover ImageNet-1k resolution extrapolation, position-only adaptation of five frozen ViTs, rectangular inputs, segmentation, and A800 inference efficiency.
Uw2EDUQtIg.claimed_gains: TRAPE-DeiT-S trained at 224² retains 70.2% top-1 at 1024² versus 36.4% and 12.1%, raises five frozen ViTs by 18–56 points with under 0.1 ImageNet epoch, assembles tables in about 0.1 ms, and enables over 10× the dense-attention batch size.
Uw2EDUQtIg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the practical axial-table design and high-resolution and aspect-ratio evaluation.
Uw2EDUQtIg.main_concern: Reviewers question the comparison with prior positional methods, including missing directly relevant resolution-extrapolation baselines.

Qw913dVTOM.one_liner: AsymStego embeds instruction fragments in carrier text that agents decode using runtime information unavailable to content-only auditors.
Qw913dVTOM.problem: Content-only auditors and executing agents can interpret identical material differently because their runtime information states differ.
Qw913dVTOM.method: AsymStego constructs environment-bound steganographic injections whose recovery depends on agent runtime information. The paper tests whether these injections evade auditing in a controlled task-driven stress test.
Qw913dVTOM.key_idea: Runtime-dependent decoding makes concealed instructions recoverable to the agent while withholding the same interpretation from a content-only auditor.
Qw913dVTOM.evidence: Experiments use 62 InjecAgent-derived attack cases on OpenClaw–DeepSeek-V4-Flash, including GPT-5.5 auditing, baselines, and component controls.
Qw913dVTOM.claimed_gains: Auditing reduces baseline attack success from 83.9%--92.5% to 0.5%--19.4%, while AsymStego reaches 52.7% under the permissive audit versus 90.3% without auditing.
Qw913dVTOM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the auditor-agent information gap as a useful attack perspective and appreciate the experimental controls and measurement effort.
Qw913dVTOM.main_concern: Reviewers question realism because permissive audit rules, disabled confirmations, and decoding-oriented tasks may drive attack success.

Ryn0lyyByh.one_liner: RAVEC learns post-selection repair and damage probabilities to choose reasoning prefixes, continuation budgets, and stopping decisions.
Ryn0lyyByh.problem: Improved candidate generation need not improve returned answers when a frozen selector rejects repairs or replaces correct answers with errors.
Ryn0lyyByh.method: RAVEC learns intervention values from randomized same-parent trials with a frozen generator and selector. A finite-horizon controller chooses reopening positions, suffix budgets, and stopping, using parent-centered fitting to sharpen action ordering.
Ryn0lyyByh.key_idea: Estimating post-selection repair and damage for prefix interventions links recomputation choices to the final selected answer.
Ryn0lyyByh.evidence: The paper provides selector-gating and policy-value theory and evaluates 14 models against sampling, verifier, and backtracking methods with controlled ablations.
Ryn0lyyByh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the final-answer-based objective and the controlled experiments separating learning targets from reopening-position selection.
Ryn0lyyByh.main_concern: Reviewers question practical compute efficiency because measured deployment overhead and the cost of offline controller training remain insufficiently established.

xDxFiJogwY.one_liner: Readout-direction overlap and controlled DPO interventions expose differences between evaluator agreement and sensitivity to training-induced changes.
xDxFiJogwY.problem: Evaluators that agree on existing responses may respond differently to policy changes caused by training.
xDxFiJogwY.method: The paper models criteria as linear readouts on a shared representation and computes geometric overlap before training. Matched-KL DPO experiments remove the component of a driver direction shared with a checker and measure changes in detection.
xDxFiJogwY.key_idea: Removing the checker-aligned component of a training direction tests how shared readout geometry controls relative evaluator responsiveness.
xDxFiJogwY.evidence: Qwen2.5-1.5B DPO experiments cover eleven FLASK criteria, five criterion pairs, nine seeds, independent rescoring, and equal-length placebo removals.
xDxFiJogwY.claimed_gains: Readout overlap predicts responsiveness with Spearman ρ = 0.71; across five pairs with 65%–80% ranking agreement, checker detection falls (aggregate +0.063) while the driver retains 79%–99% of its above-chance signal.
xDxFiJogwY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the distinction between static agreement and training responsiveness and the disciplined matched-KL experimental design.
xDxFiJogwY.main_concern: Reviewers question whether reduced checker responsiveness demonstrates a meaningful evaluation failure rather than fewer changes in the checker's preferred direction.

r5wHEaNw0f.one_liner: Ising and Kuramoto dynamics generate image latents through energy relaxation, with class-dependent node biases and a compact decoder.
r5wHEaNw0f.problem: Porting conventional neural networks to alternative hardware underuses native low-energy relaxation as a computational primitive.
r5wHEaNw0f.method: The paper trains Ising-spin and Kuramoto-oscillator generative systems with explicit Lyapunov energies and decodes their final states into images. Local class conditioning changes one bias per node while keeping programmed pairwise interactions fixed.
r5wHEaNw0f.key_idea: Class-dependent node biases reshape fixed-coupling relaxation dynamics, whose final states feed an image decoder.
r5wHEaNw0f.evidence: CIFAR-10 generation experiments, conditioning ablations, noise and quantization studies, and CMOS-compatible circuit simulations support the design.
r5wHEaNw0f.claimed_gains: With 4096 nodes, Ising and Kuramoto models reach clean-FID scores of 6.40 and 5.37 on CIFAR-10, and the dynamical core is projected to cost ~110.6 nJ per image.
r5wHEaNw0f.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value hardware-native relaxation and local conditioning that avoids reprogramming pairwise couplings.
r5wHEaNw0f.main_concern: Reviewers agree that projected hardware-efficiency gains lack consistent end-to-end physical measurements and complete system-overhead accounting.

QYLUiRLODb.one_liner: Intermediate video reassessment, evolving memory, and pairwise quality comparisons guide adaptive restoration-tool sequences.
QYLUiRLODb.problem: Fixed restoration pipelines cannot adapt when tools remove overlapping degradations or introduce new artifacts.
QYLUiRLODb.method: ReVRA repeatedly examines the current video and reselects restoration toolboxes using instance-aware evolving memory. Execution outcomes refine that memory, while relative quality comparisons evaluate candidate restoration results.
QYLUiRLODb.key_idea: Replan restoration stages from intermediate video states and update toolbox-selection memory using verified execution outcomes.
QYLUiRLODb.evidence: Experiments span synthetic and real-world video degradations, including TaoUGC, with replanning, memory, and evaluator comparisons.
QYLUiRLODb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find iterative plan-execute-evaluate restoration well motivated for compound degradations and tool-induced artifacts.
QYLUiRLODb.main_concern: Ablations do not adequately separate the benefits of reflection, memory, and relative comparison from additional evaluator training.

SR6wwmCONp.one_liner: Controlled feature-group comparisons assess which language-model internal statistics contribute most to harmful-prompt detection.
SR6wwmCONp.problem: The relative detection value of gradients, hidden representations, and other internal language-model signals remains unclear.
SR6wwmCONp.method: The study extracts seven groups of internal statistics and compares their distributions, removal effects, feature selection, and dependence on the base LLM. HELM combines the extracted features with existing classifiers.
SR6wwmCONp.key_idea: Compare internal signal groups under a shared extraction and classification procedure, using group removal to measure their contributions.
SR6wwmCONp.evidence: ToxicChat and SafetyPromptCollections experiments include feature-group ablations, classifier comparisons, feature selection, and alternative LLMs.
SR6wwmCONp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the empirical comparison and combination of internal signals for harmful-prompt detection.
SR6wwmCONp.main_concern: Unequal feature-group sizes confound conclusions about the relative importance of different internal signals.

bYuShrqKZz.one_liner: Shared sparse features organize historical keys into overlapping buckets for query-dependent retrieval of original KV entries.
bYuShrqKZz.problem: Sparse attention can preserve quality, but efficiently locating relevant historical tokens across long contexts remains difficult.
bYuShrqKZz.method: A shared query-key sparse autoencoder learns a common feature dictionary, and PrismKV indexes keys by their active features. Compact bucket summaries select candidates without scanning the full history, after which attention uses selected original KV entries.
bYuShrqKZz.key_idea: Index keys in overlapping sparse-feature buckets and use compact bucket summaries to retrieve candidates for attention.
bYuShrqKZz.evidence: RULER and LongBench evaluate the 27B model, while speed measurements include Qwen3-8B at 128K context and a 27B model at 256K.
bYuShrqKZz.claimed_gains: PrismKV retains 99.90% of full-attention performance on average, with attention-path speedups of 3.37x on Qwen3-8B at 128K and 2.78x on the 27B model at 256K.
bYuShrqKZz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find overlapping sparse-feature indexing an interesting connection between representation analysis and practical attention retrieval.
bYuShrqKZz.main_concern: Missing comparisons with closely related indexed and dynamic attention methods weaken the assessment of practical advantage.

hh8P8HvV7U.one_liner: Shifted action-reward feedback modulates attention projections, while a smoothed utility state provides persistent conditioning for sequential decisions.
hh8P8HvV7U.problem: Input-level feedback injection may inadequately distinguish actions when identical observations require different responses depending on prior outcomes.
hh8P8HvV7U.method: Utility-Augmented Transformers modulate queries, keys, and values using shifted action-reward feedback and an exponentially smoothed utility state. Additive and multiplicative pathways use independent base and utility projections, with zero initialization recovering the vanilla backbone.
hh8P8HvV7U.key_idea: Condition attention queries, keys, and values on causally shifted feedback and an accumulated utility state.
hh8P8HvV7U.evidence: Restricted single-layer expressivity analysis accompanies controlled hidden-regime tasks, including DarkRoom and semi-synthetic sepsis, plus D4RL comparisons and feedback-corruption tests.
hh8P8HvV7U.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find feedback-conditioned attention a concrete, well-motivated design for tasks with hidden state changes.
hh8P8HvV7U.main_concern: The restricted single-layer logit separation does not establish an expressivity or policy-performance advantage for the evaluated nonlinear multilayer models.

mo3S2ihVAe.one_liner: A reinforcement-learned local SLM decides when and how to request adaptive feedback from a cloud LLM.
mo3S2ihVAe.problem: Local small language models lack cloud-model capabilities, while cloud assistance introduces privacy and interaction costs.
mo3S2ihVAe.method: The framework treats the SLM and LLM as heterogeneous agents with asymmetric information. Reinforcement learning trains the SLM to choose assistance requests under answer-quality, privacy, and efficiency objectives while the LLM supplies adaptive feedback.
mo3S2ihVAe.key_idea: Train the local model's assistance-seeking decisions and request formulations jointly while a cloud model provides adaptive feedback.
mo3S2ihVAe.evidence: Evaluations vary SLM and LLM capabilities and constraints, test unseen LLMs, and assess transfer to real-world personal tasks without additional training.
mo3S2ihVAe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the learned local-cloud collaboration well motivated and practically useful for balancing task quality with privacy and interaction costs.
mo3S2ihVAe.main_concern: Multi-turn collaboration rarely occurs during evaluation, leaving its contribution unclear without a comparably trained single-turn rewrite-and-forward baseline.

VhLccdYrzX.one_liner: COLA retrieves semantic and structural graph contexts, then selects them using a reinforcement-learned utility estimator.
VhLccdYrzX.problem: Few-shot graph foundation model adaptation underuses source-graph context and conflates retrieval similarity with downstream usefulness.
VhLccdYrzX.method: COLA builds semantic and structural graph databases and retrieves candidates using graph representations and graph kernels. A lightweight reinforcement-learned policy uses pseudo-target calibration to estimate candidate utility and select fine-grained contexts.
VhLccdYrzX.key_idea: Calibrate a context-selection policy on pseudo-target domains to choose retrieved semantic and structural graph contexts by downstream utility.
VhLccdYrzX.evidence: Reviews describe multiple transfer settings, matched-budget calibration comparisons, utility analyses on Cora, and a generalization bound for routing under domain shift.
VhLccdYrzX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the explicit separation of retrieval relevance from prediction utility in few-shot graph adaptation.
VhLccdYrzX.main_concern: Pseudo-target graphs remain in backbone pretraining despite exclusion from retrieval, weakening evidence that utility calibration transfers to unseen domains.

ZPleoh1C9S.one_liner: CryoNet.Density uses Brownian bridge diffusion to correct physically rendered cryo-EM maps toward experimental maps with continuous resolution conditioning.
ZPleoh1C9S.problem: Synthetic cryo-EM maps struggle to reproduce experimental characteristics while retaining explicit resolution control.
ZPleoh1C9S.method: A differentiable renderer converts atomic structures into resolution-matched density maps, and a 3D Brownian bridge diffusion model learns corrections toward paired experimental maps. Fourier features condition resolution, and a one-transition stochastic sampler uses two denoiser evaluations.
ZPleoh1C9S.key_idea: Learn a resolution-conditioned Brownian diffusion bridge between physically rendered density maps and paired experimental reconstructions.
ZPleoh1C9S.evidence: Evaluation uses a held-out 1,923-case set with seven spatial- and Fourier-domain metrics, analytical renderers and Struc2mapGAN, plus downstream structure analysis.
ZPleoh1C9S.claimed_gains: The abstract reports continuous inference from 1.5–10 Å with only two denoiser evaluations.
ZPleoh1C9S.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize strong map-quality results across multiple complementary evaluation metrics.
ZPleoh1C9S.main_concern: Map similarity does not establish that generated samples capture realistic experimental variability or that nominal resolution conditioning has the claimed physical meaning.

4Xafd1RVZm.one_liner: Quantile aggregation over independent data partitions drives bonus-free ensemble exploration in finite-horizon tabular reinforcement learning.
4Xafd1RVZm.problem: Explicit exploration bonuses and posterior uncertainty estimates are difficult to scale, while practical ensemble exploration lacks theoretical justification.
4Xafd1RVZm.method: The method extends quantile-based ensemble exploration from multi-armed bandits to finite-horizon tabular MDPs. It aggregates estimates from independent data partitions to obtain optimism without explicit uncertainty bonuses.
4Xafd1RVZm.key_idea: Use low-quantile aggregation of estimates from independent data partitions to induce exploration without explicit bonuses or posterior distributions.
4Xafd1RVZm.evidence: The paper presents episodic tabular regret analysis and claims minimax-optimal, variance-dependent bounds, whose justification reviewers dispute.
4Xafd1RVZm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find quantile-based ensemble exploration appealing and view its theoretical treatment as a meaningful direction.
4Xafd1RVZm.main_concern: Reviewers question the stated guarantees, citing mismatched variance comparisons, unclear ensemble-size dependence, and a concentration-bound error underlying the regret proofs.

j3ftJl2x0v.one_liner: SimGraph combines asymmetrically scaled pairwise similarity learning with size-conditioned normalization for graph classification under size imbalance.
j3ftJl2x0v.problem: Graph size imbalance under limited supervision distorts similarity estimates and creates performance gaps across graph-size groups.
j3ftJl2x0v.method: Balanced pairwise graph similarity learning formulates pair similarity as binary classification with asymmetric scaling and a learnable decision boundary. Size-adaptive instance normalization modulates size-coupled statistics using graph size.
j3ftJl2x0v.key_idea: Combine an asymmetrically scaled pairwise classification loss with size-conditioned normalization to adjust graph similarity learning under size imbalance.
j3ftJl2x0v.evidence: The abstract describes binary and multiclass molecular, biological, social, and heterogeneous graph benchmarks, alongside false-negative-free pair construction and bounded-gradient properties.
j3ftJl2x0v.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers identify size-induced graph similarity bias as a relevant problem and acknowledge the breadth of the experiments.
j3ftJl2x0v.main_concern: The evidence does not establish that the components remove size-induced semantic bias rather than exploit size-label correlations or incremental loss changes.

9S1a6H8xUR.one_liner: Adaptive Knowledge Inheritance reorganizes response, feature, and class-distribution representations while retaining knowledge during class-incremental semantic segmentation.
9S1a6H8xUR.problem: Constraints inherited from earlier segmentation tasks can prevent representations from adapting to newly introduced classes.
9S1a6H8xUR.method: AKI coordinates knowledge reorganization at response, feature, and distribution levels. Its components use response masking and consistency, preserve discriminative old-class directions while accounting for feature changes, and address class distributions.
9S1a6H8xUR.key_idea: Coordinate response masking, old-class direction preservation, and class-distribution reorganization as incremental segmentation objectives change.
9S1a6H8xUR.evidence: Optimization and controlled-perturbation analyses support the design, while reviews describe nine incremental settings, repeated runs, component ablations, and multiple backbones.
9S1a6H8xUR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize complementary mechanisms for balancing retention and adaptation, supported by extensive empirical evaluation.
9S1a6H8xUR.main_concern: Differences between the reproduced MBS baseline and its original reported results obscure whether AKI's gains reflect comparable training and evaluation conditions.

D1ejxJd15M.one_liner: Extracts cue-induced image affinities from VLM query-key interactions to group images sharing recurring visual cues and describe each group.
D1ejxJd15M.problem: Conventional VLMs trained with standard token-level supervision struggle to discover and describe sparse recurring visual cues across large image collections filled with distractors without predefined queries.
D1ejxJd15M.method: The authors define query-free shared visual cue discovery, build the CUESEL diagnostic benchmark from packed image collections, and propose CUEMEM. CUEMEM converts internal VLM query-key interactions into cue-induced pairwise image affinities to infer supporting image subsets and conditions cue description generation on those inferred supports.
D1ejxJd15M.key_idea: Transforms internal VLM query-key attention interactions into pairwise image affinities to recover supporting image subsets before conditioning textual cue generation on those subsets.
D1ejxJd15M.evidence: Evaluated on the CUESEL benchmark comprising 4k packed collections and 73k human-filtered cue groups against supervised flat VLMs and clustering baselines.
D1ejxJd15M.claimed_gains: CUEMEM achieves 0.747 Pairwise Grouping F1 (PGF1), compared with 0.405 for the strongest supervised flat VLM.
D1ejxJd15M.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the query-free visual cue discovery formulation interesting and appreciate separating support-subset recovery from cue description rather than autoregressively listing hundreds of image IDs.
D1ejxJd15M.main_concern: Reviewers point out that CUESEL packs groups from VIST photo stories into an artificial mutually exclusive partition—allowing story/scene context shortcuts while penalizing valid overlapping cues—and omits relevant image-collection mining literature.

qVZY5UUYHO.one_liner: Projects a tool-center-point coordinate frame into first-person RGB observations so pretrained VLMs can output continuous robot actions directly as text.
qVZY5UUYHO.problem: Existing VLA models require robot trajectories to train new action heads or tokens, while modular zero-shot VLM manipulation pipelines depend on external planners that cannot be fine-tuned end-to-end as a unified policy.
qVZY5UUYHO.method: Explicit Action-Space Grounding (EASG) overlays a 3D tool center point (TCP)-centered coordinate frame onto the VLM's first-person visual input using depth perception and expresses continuous robot actions through the VLM's native text generation interface. This enables zero-shot manipulation from pretrained VLMs while preserving the exact same action interface for downstream fine-tuning.
qVZY5UUYHO.key_idea: Renders a tool-center-point 3D coordinate frame directly onto first-person camera observations so a VLM can generate continuous robot actions as native text coordinates.
qVZY5UUYHO.evidence: Evaluated on six real-world robotic manipulation tasks (zero-shot and fine-tuned, including pose and object randomization) and the LIBERO simulation benchmark.
qVZY5UUYHO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the visual coordinate-frame projection simple and intuitive, and are impressed that a pretrained VLM achieves a 79.4% zero-shot real-world manipulation success rate without robot-action training.
qVZY5UUYHO.main_concern: Reviewers point out that performance collapses from 79.4% to 11.7% without chain-of-thought reasoning—yet inference latency and token costs are unreported—and note limitations to simple grippers, RGB-D depth requirements, and evaluation only on LIBERO in simulation.

M7AkkTXvbZ.one_liner: Maintains ellipsoidal feasible sets across multiple variation scales to achieve minimax-optimal dynamic regret for contextual pricing in non-stationary environments.
M7AkkTXvbZ.problem: In non-stationary contextual dynamic pricing with binary feedback, small temporal shifts in the hidden valuation vector under heterogeneous contexts can leave a single-scale relaxed feasible set narrow yet far from the true parameter.
M7AkkTXvbZ.method: For identical contexts, the paper combines binary-search exploration, lower-envelope pricing, and two restart mechanisms. For heterogeneous contexts, it introduces a multiscale shallow-pricing algorithm that maintains relaxed feasible sets and ellipsoidal approximations across multiple variation scales, using larger scales for localization certificates and the smallest active scale to set exploitation prices.
M7AkkTXvbZ.key_idea: Coordinates nested ellipsoidal feasible sets across multiple variation scales with width checks and rejection-triggered restarts to localize drifting valuation vectors from binary purchase feedback.
M7AkkTXvbZ.evidence: Supported by theoretical dynamic regret upper bounds for identical and heterogeneous contexts and matching minimax lower bounds up to logarithmic factors.
M7AkkTXvbZ.claimed_gains: The identical-context algorithm achieves dynamic regret O((sqrt(TV)+1) log T) and the heterogeneous-context multiscale algorithm achieves dynamic regret O((d^2 + d^{3/2} sqrt(TV)) log^2 T), matching the lower bound Omega(sqrt(TV) + log log T) up to logarithmic factors for fixed dimension.
M7AkkTXvbZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the rigorous theoretical analysis and the multiscale geometric mechanism that overcomes poor feasible-set localization under simultaneous context heterogeneity and parameter drift.
M7AkkTXvbZ.main_concern: Reviewers note the complete absence of empirical or synthetic experiments, the restrictive assumption of noiseless linear valuations, and the requirement that the cumulative variation budget V be known in advance.

axCkvgjF57.one_liner: Predicts per-token retokenization survival reliability from recovery-side features to weight evidence during autoregressive image watermark verification.
axCkvgjF57.problem: Retokenizing autoregressively generated images after visual transformations introduces non-uniform token recovery errors, yet existing watermark detectors weight all recovered symbols equally.
axCkvgjF57.method: Reliability-Aware Verification (RAV) extracts detector-side features during retokenization—including quantization geometry, posterior uncertainty, consistency, and spatial context—to predict each symbol's survival reliability. The predicted reliabilities are converted into watermark-structure-aware weights to aggregate verification evidence without altering watermark embedding.
axCkvgjF57.key_idea: Weights retokenized watermark verification symbols by a learned survival-reliability score predicted from detector-side quantization geometry, posterior uncertainty, and spatial context.
axCkvgjF57.evidence: Evaluated on WMAR and ClusterMark watermarking schemes across RAR-XL, TAMING, and LlamaGen GPT-B generators under diverse image transformations and neural compression.
axCkvgjF57.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that operating purely on the detector side to weight retokenized symbols by recovery reliability is practical, fast, and consistently improves detection over uniform hard aggregation.
axCkvgjF57.main_concern: Reviewers point out that simple training-free heuristics (such as quantization margin or maximum posterior probability) capture most of the gains of the learned reliability predictor, and that RAV still fails under geometric desynchronization like a 15-degree rotation.

0nhj1v2vJ9.one_liner: Evolves a skill-retrieval graph offline from agent execution traces by updating graph topology, edge weights, and node descriptions.
0nhj1v2vJ9.problem: Static skill-retrieval graphs built from text similarity fail to reflect actual execution utility or refine skill connections and descriptions from agent experience.
0nhj1v2vJ9.method: Self-Evolving Graph-of-Skills (SE-GoS) updates a skill-retrieval graph offline using agent execution trajectories while keeping the retrieval algorithm, source skills, and LLM weights fixed. Each evolution round applies three updates: adding execution-supported topology edges, adapting edge weights based on usage and reward, and rewriting skill node descriptions with the agent backbone.
0nhj1v2vJ9.key_idea: Updates a skill-retrieval graph offline from execution trajectories by inducing co-usage edges, reweighting edges by execution outcomes, and rewriting skill node descriptions.
0nhj1v2vJ9.evidence: Evaluated on SkillsBench across multiple LLM backbones (including deepseek-v4-flash-0731) against static GoS and SkillDAG under in-domain and held-out task protocols.
0nhj1v2vJ9.claimed_gains: In the primary deepseek-v4-flash-0731 setting, one evolution round raises mean reward from 50.8% to 59.4% while using 32% fewer input tokens than full-library loading, and on tasks excluded from evolution SE-GoS achieves 58.3% reward versus 54.2% for SkillDAG.
0nhj1v2vJ9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate treating the retrieval graph as an inspectable, training-free state evolved from execution traces and value the held-out transfer evaluation and component ablations.
0nhj1v2vJ9.main_concern: Reviewers point out a mismatch between the motivation of recovering prerequisite dependencies and the implementation (which induces zero dependency edges in trace analysis), alongside small in-domain margins without statistical significance tests and performance degradation by the third evolution round.

9zB8ZjixLi.one_liner: Diagnoses visual shortcut reliance in audio-visual LLMs via factorized modality swapping and repairs it by training on relabeled counterfactual grids.
9zB8ZjixLi.problem: When asked an audio-specific question, omni-modal LLMs frequently answer using correlated visual cues from the image rather than the audio, and this cross-modal shortcut persists through SFT and RL post-training.
9zB8ZjixLi.method: The authors introduce the Factorized Modality Diagnostic, which crosses audio and image inputs across sample pairs in a 2x2 grid to isolate each modality's causal contribution to the model's answer. They then propose DMC-Repair, which fine-tunes models on these cross-modal swapped grids with answer supervision assigned strictly according to the modality designated by the question.
9zB8ZjixLi.key_idea: Constructs 2x2 crossed audio-image counterfactual grids across sample pairs to measure modality reliance and trains the model with labels determined strictly by the queried modality.
9zB8ZjixLi.evidence: Evaluated across two omni-modal LLM families through SFT and RL post-training stages, measuring shortcut reliance, conditional visual effects, IntentBench, and audio-visual matching.
9zB8ZjixLi.claimed_gains: DMC-Repair reduces the image-induced share of the answer effect by 59.9%.
9zB8ZjixLi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the 2x2 factorized swap diagnostic clearly exposes cross-modal visual shortcuts on audio questions and that training on question-designated counterfactual pairs is a simple, effective, and transferable fix.
9zB8ZjixLi.main_concern: Reviewers note limited incremental novelty over prior counterfactual modality-alignment training (such as Chen et al. and MoD-DPO), missing direct comparisons against those baselines, and insufficient evidence that joint audio-visual integration is preserved on tasks genuinely requiring both modalities.

hg5szImFUP.one_liner: Combines full-sequence forward propagation of neuron-internal sensitivities with chunk-wise truncated BPTT across recurrent connections for bounded-memory RNN training.
hg5szImFUP.problem: Full BPTT requires memory linear in sequence length, TBPTT discards long-range dependencies, and forward eligibility-trace methods like e-prop ignore gradients flowing through external inter-neuron recurrent connections.
hg5szImFUP.method: Forward-Backward Propagation Through Time (FBPTT) decomposes recurrent dynamics into neuron-internal recurrence and external inter-neuron connections. It propagates neuron-internal sensitivities forward across the entire sequence while applying truncated BPTT within fixed-length sequence chunks to capture short-range cross-neuron recurrent pathways within bounded memory.
hg5szImFUP.key_idea: Couples full-sequence forward eligibility traces for diagonal neuron-internal recurrence with chunk-local truncated backpropagation through time for off-diagonal inter-neuron recurrent connections.
hg5szImFUP.evidence: Evaluated on standard artificial recurrent architectures (LSTM, GRU) and spiking neural networks (BRF, SE-adLIF) across sequential benchmarks.
hg5szImFUP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the paper clearly written and well-executed, and agree that combining forward internal traces with chunked backward propagation improves accuracy over pure TBPTT and forward-only approximations under bounded memory across RNN and SNN topologies.
hg5szImFUP.main_concern: Reviewers point out that combining forward eligibility traces or RTRL sensitivities with truncated backpropagated error signals closely resembles prior work (specifically Bellec et al.'s e-prop variation 3 and Schmidhuber 1992) that is not adequately cited or differentiated.

PCf8p7MQId.one_liner: Learns step-dependent guidance weights for loss-guided diffusion sampling via first-order truncated backpropagation through the unrolled sampler.
PCf8p7MQId.problem: Constant guidance scales in loss-guided diffusion require many sampling steps and small step weights to balance sample quality against constraint satisfaction, degrading performance at small inference budgets.
PCf8p7MQId.method: Learned End-to-End Guidance Schedules (LEEGS) optimizes a time-dependent guidance weight schedule for a given task and step budget by minimizing the guidance loss along the unrolled sampling trajectory over a small calibration set. To avoid expensive second derivatives through the diffusion score network during backpropagation, LEEGS uses a first-order gradient approximation.
PCf8p7MQId.key_idea: Optimizes per-step scalar guidance weights end-to-end through an unrolled loss-guided diffusion sampler using a first-order gradient approximation that avoids second derivatives of the score model.
PCf8p7MQId.evidence: Evaluated across image inpainting, noisy image inverse problems, face-ID-guided generation, and forward and inverse PDE problems against constant and heuristic guidance schedules.
PCf8p7MQId.claimed_gains: On noisy image inverse problems, LEEGS matches constant guidance using only 10% of the sampling steps.
PCf8p7MQId.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that learning per-step guidance scalars adds zero inference overhead, applies generally across loss-guided diffusion tasks, and improves the quality-constraint trade-off at low step counts.
PCf8p7MQId.main_concern: Reviewers note limited methodological novelty given prior work that differentiates through unrolled diffusion samplers to learn step schedules or guidance weights (such as DRaFT and Galashov et al.), as well as missing comparisons to established diffusion inverse-problem solvers like DiffPIR and RED-diff.

gRcfXsYbdL.one_liner: Samples discrete Bayesian optimization candidates from a frozen generative model tilted by a data-space acquisition function via a diffusion bridge.
gRcfXsYbdL.problem: Discrete Bayesian optimization lacks gradients for acquisition maximization, while latent-space BO makes it difficult to incorporate domain-specific kernels defined directly in the discrete data space.
gRcfXsYbdL.method: Acquisition Function-Guided Generation (AFGG) pairs a frozen pretrained generative model with a surrogate and acquisition function defined directly in the discrete data space. Instead of maximizing the acquisition function directly, AFGG samples candidates from an acquisition-tilted generative distribution embedded into a diffusion bridge that yields a smooth, posterior-averaged acquisition guidance score, instantiated with both a categorical diffusion model and an autoregressive normalizing flow.
gRcfXsYbdL.key_idea: Steers sampling of a frozen discrete generative model using gradients from a diffusion-bridge posterior average of a data-space acquisition function.
gRcfXsYbdL.evidence: Evaluated across 25 molecular optimization benchmark tasks using categorical diffusion and autoregressive normalizing flow instantiations.
gRcfXsYbdL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clean formulation that combines domain-specific data-space kernels with frozen pretrained generative models without retraining and achieves strong empirical results on molecular design benchmarks.
gRcfXsYbdL.main_concern: Reviewers question the degree of novelty over COWBOYS, note the computational overhead of repeated posterior sampling and acquisition evaluations during guided generation, and point out that experiments are limited solely to molecular optimization without empirically validating the claimed failure modes of latent-space BO.

q9Z5BD7U14.one_liner: Consolidates past multimodal agent episodes into auditable visual-textual lessons and trains a policy to apply retrieved lessons for chest X-ray report generation.
q9Z5BD7U14.problem: Retrieving raw episodic memory trajectories for MLLM chest X-ray report generation is inefficient and can introduce new clinical finding errors when retrieved cases are improperly applied.
q9Z5BD7U14.method: The authors consolidate historical multimodal agent episodes into a compact set of auditable multimodal lessons pairing textual applicability conditions with visual exemplars and source pointers. They then train the MLLM agent via reinforcement learning to incorporate retrieved lessons by rewarding corrected clinical findings and penalizing newly introduced errors.
q9Z5BD7U14.key_idea: Compresses raw multimodal agent episodes into condition-exemplar lessons and trains the report-generation agent with RL rewards that favor finding corrections and penalize newly introduced errors.
q9Z5BD7U14.evidence: Evaluated on MIMIC-CXR using 76 consolidated lessons against raw episodic retrieval (8,192 episodes), ExpeL, and ViLoMem, plus transfer tests across external X-ray datasets, agent frameworks, and base MLLMs.
q9Z5BD7U14.claimed_gains: On MIMIC-CXR, retrieving from 76 lessons improves finding-level balanced accuracy by 2.90 points compared with 1.07 points for retrieval over all 8,192 raw episodes, and policy training raises the gain over no memory to 5.18 points while reducing introduced errors from 123 to 74.
q9Z5BD7U14.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value consolidating raw cases into compact, auditable lessons linked to visual exemplars and source episodes, and note clear finding-level accuracy gains over raw episodic retrieval on MIMIC-CXR.
q9Z5BD7U14.main_concern: Reviewers point out a major clinical limitation at inference where sequential lesson testing terminates after the first modification (preventing multi-pathology corrections), alongside insufficient negative-case validation during lesson construction to filter out false-positive-inducing lessons.

UVecrvuDvP.one_liner: Compresses long LLM contexts by selecting query-relevant tokens as semantic centers and merging remaining tokens via semantic consistency weights.
UVecrvuDvP.problem: Existing soft prompt context compression methods insert learnable tokens at fixed intervals or group tokens by physical layout, introducing position bias and semantic fragmentation.
UVecrvuDvP.method: Semantic Consistency Context Compression (SeCo) shifts context compression from physical token positions to semantic space. It selects query-relevant tokens as semantic centers, assigns surrounding tokens to these centers in semantic space, and aggregates them through consistency-weighted merging into compact embeddings.
UVecrvuDvP.key_idea: Selects query-relevant tokens as semantic centers and aggregates remaining context tokens into them via semantic-consistency-weighted merging independent of physical token positions.
UVecrvuDvP.evidence: Evaluated across 14 benchmarks and two LLM backbone models against six context compression baselines (including ICAE, SAC, 500xCompressor, RAM, and COMI).
UVecrvuDvP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the query-guided semantic center selection and consistency-weighted merging framework intuitive, lightweight, and effective across the 14 evaluated benchmarks.
UVecrvuDvP.main_concern: Reviewers raise concerns about fairness and scalability in multi-turn settings because query-dependent compression must be recomputed for every new query unlike query-agnostic baselines, and note missing evaluations on standard long-context benchmarks like RULER.

rLUgyuRkBe.one_liner: Enforces multi-agent coding coordination inside the execution harness through structured artifacts, automatic finding injection, and interface mismatch checks.
rLUgyuRkBe.problem: In multi-agent repository-level code generation, free-form messages shared between agents often go unused or fail to prevent undetected deviations from agreed module interfaces.
rLUgyuRkBe.method: The Artifact-Exclusive Communication Protocol (AECP) prohibits free-form inter-agent messaging and routes all communication through structured artifacts managed by the execution harness. Triggered by tool calls, the harness automatically supplies recorded findings when agents access relevant files, screens code implementations against recorded interface commitments, and forces affected agents to revisit revised interface agreements.
rLUgyuRkBe.key_idea: Replaces free-form inter-agent chat with harness-enforced structured artifacts that automatically inject relevant findings on file access and verify code against committed module interfaces.
rLUgyuRkBe.evidence: Evaluated on Doc2Repo, NL2Repo, and CodeProjectEval across five open- and closed-source models (including Opus-4.8 and DeepSeek-V4-Flash) against single-agent and multi-agent team baselines.
rLUgyuRkBe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate moving multi-agent coordination from prompt instructions into concrete, tool-triggered execution harness rules and acknowledge the broad multi-model evaluation on repository-level coding benchmarks.
rLUgyuRkBe.main_concern: Reviewers point out that the primary controlled multi-agent baseline (Team-Freedom) performs much worse than a single agent—inflating the headline gain—while margins over stronger baselines are modest and ablations bundle shared workspace and knowledge sharing together.

jKGVnlFA3B.one_liner: Combines change-point detection with Proximal Policy Optimization to learn when to re-solve computationally expensive MILPs in real-time operations.
jKGVnlFA3B.problem: In real-time operations with high-frequency data streams, repeatedly re-solving NP-hard Mixed-Integer Linear Programs is computationally costly, while reusing stale solutions degrades decision quality under non-Markovian dynamics.
jKGVnlFA3B.method: Proximal Policy Optimization with Change Point Detection (POC) detects environmental regime shifts to select informative samples and trains a PPO policy to decide at each step whether to re-solve the underlying MILP or keep the existing solution. The paper also derives a theoretical relationship between optimal re-solving frequency and re-solving cost.
jKGVnlFA3B.key_idea: Uses change-point detection to identify environmental shifts and trains a cost-aware PPO policy to trigger MILP re-solves only when expected objective improvement outweighs solver cost.
jKGVnlFA3B.evidence: Supported by a theoretical analysis relating re-solve count to re-solving cost and empirical evaluations across eight synthetic and real-world optimization datasets.
jKGVnlFA3B.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that scheduling when to re-solve expensive MILPs under explicit computation costs is an economically important, well-formulated problem and note consistent empirical improvements across eight datasets.
jKGVnlFA3B.main_concern: Reviewers point out that training relies on clairvoyant optimal solutions (or true change points in synthetic setups) that are expensive to obtain for large MILPs, and that ablations lack simple cost-aware trigger heuristics using the same change-point or EMA estimators to isolate PPO's contribution.

j4keDnV1cs.one_liner: Matches data observation structure to visualization requirements using a formal grammar to retrieve compatible plotting examples across table layout changes.
j4keDnV1cs.problem: Similarity-based retrieval for data visualization code generation fails when tables with similar surface fields require different analyses or when valid examples are obscured by changes in table storage layout.
j4keDnV1cs.method: OmniFigure pairs a visualization example library with OmniGrammar, a formal representation that encodes the observation structure and relational requirements of an analysis independently of storage layout. OmniGrammar checks structural compatibility to retrieve applicable figures and code templates for LLM generators, evaluated on the newly introduced OmniFigureBench.
j4keDnV1cs.key_idea: Represents data tables and visualization examples in a layout-invariant observation-structure grammar to verify relational compatibility before retrieving reference code for plotting agents.
j4keDnV1cs.evidence: Evaluated on MatPlotBench, PlotCraft, and the newly introduced OmniFigureBench covering retrieval under representation changes, relation loss, and downstream visualization generation.
j4keDnV1cs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the formalization of layout-invariant relational compatibility for visualization retrieval and the joint evaluation of example recovery and incompatible-example rejection.
j4keDnV1cs.main_concern: Reviewers note that downstream generation gains over standard LLM retrieval under the same curated library are very small (e.g., 1.142 to 1.162 VLM score on MatPlotBench), layout-invariance tests mainly anonymize column names rather than testing complex table reshaping, and library construction details are under-specified.

tUqugeSeJV.one_liner: Analyzes subliminal trait transfer as steering-vector recovery under Fisher curvature, comparing hard-token NLL against full-distribution KL supervision on matched prefixes.
tUqugeSeJV.problem: Subliminal learning—where a student inherits a teacher's behavioral trait from semantically unrelated text—requires tens of thousands of examples, leaving it unclear whether small datasets lack signal coverage or suffer from hard-label token sampling noise.
tUqugeSeJV.method: Using subliminal steering with a known teacher steering vector as a controlled testbed, the authors measure cosine similarity between the teacher vector and a recovered student vector under token-level hard NLL supervision versus full-distribution soft KL supervision on identical carrier prefixes. They analyze recovery trajectories in the softmax Fisher eigenbasis to explain why initial mean gradients have similar low alignment yet iterative soft optimization recovers the trait from hundreds of examples while hard supervision stalls.
tUqugeSeJV.key_idea: Compares student recovery of a known teacher steering vector under hard-token NLL versus full-logit KL on matched prefixes through the spectrum of the softmax Fisher information matrix.
tUqugeSeJV.evidence: Evaluated in a controlled steering-vector recovery testbed comparing hard NLL and soft KL supervision across sample sizes, repeated token sampling, and Fisher eigenbasis projections.
tUqugeSeJV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the controlled matched-prefix comparison with a known ground-truth teacher steering vector and the insightful Fisher eigenbasis analysis contrasting initial gradient alignment with multi-step optimization recovery.
tUqugeSeJV.main_concern: Reviewers point out that conclusions from optimizing a low-dimensional steering vector on a frozen base model may not generalize to full-weight fine-tuning or prompt-driven subliminal learning, that scaling random datasets conflates sample volume with prefix diversity, and that parts of the Fisher formulation overlap with recent prior work.

KuPUxWwAQB.one_liner: Measures non-additive group disparity in human-AI probability integration relative to a linear-pooling additive reference via the HDDI diagnostic.
KuPUxWwAQB.problem: Auditing group disparity only in human judgments, AI predictions, or final hybrid outcomes fails to separate disparity inherited from the individual components from non-additive disparity introduced by their integration rule.
KuPUxWwAQB.method: The authors define the Human-AI Disparity Distortion Index (HDDI) for an integration rule combining human and algorithmic probabilities as the difference between the hybrid system's group disparity and the linear-pooling additive reference $(1-\lambda)D_H + \lambda D_A$. Because linear pooling yields zero HDDI by linearity of expectation, nonzero HDDI isolates group-differential departures from additive probability combination.
KuPUxWwAQB.key_idea: Computes the difference between a hybrid decision rule's group disparity and the convex combination of standalone human and AI disparities under linear probability pooling.
KuPUxWwAQB.evidence: Evaluated across three settings: simulated human-AI pairings on ACSIncome, identity-sensitive text moderation on Civil Comments, and observed human judgments on COMPAS.
KuPUxWwAQB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that HDDI is a mathematically clean, easy-to-compute diagnostic that highlights how nonlinear aggregation rules (and continuous versus binary pooling) alter group disparities relative to linear pooling.
KuPUxWwAQB.main_concern: Reviewers question the practical and normative value of the metric because HDDI is purely descriptive and non-causal, all experiments rely on the same log-odds pooling operator rather than real interactive human-AI decisions, and deviations from linear pooling do not point to actionable fairness interventions.

8QXGLg69Hh.one_liner: Detects photorealistic AI-generated images by decomposing implicit visual claims and verifying them against retrieved web evidence with a multi-agent system.
8QXGLg69Hh.problem: Modern image generators produce photorealistic images without obvious pixel artifacts or low-level visual flaws, causing conventional forensic AIGI detectors to fail when the only tell is a factual or world-knowledge inconsistency.
8QXGLg69Hh.method: The authors introduce K-AIGI-Bench, a human-curated benchmark of AI-generated images with embedded factual inconsistencies paired with topic-matched real images, and propose K-VERA, a training-free retrieval-augmented multi-agent framework. K-VERA identifies entities and scenes, decomposes implicit visual claims into verification sub-tasks, retrieves webpages and reference images, and adjudicates source evidence to issue a verdict and explanation.
8QXGLg69Hh.key_idea: Decomposes implicit factual claims in an image into search queries and uses a multi-agent web-retrieval and adjudication pipeline to detect knowledge-inconsistent AI-generated images.
8QXGLg69Hh.evidence: Evaluated on the newly constructed K-AIGI-Bench (~1,000 images across eight knowledge topics) and external AIGI benchmarks against dedicated forensic detectors and tool-free MLLM baselines.
8QXGLg69Hh.claimed_gains: Experiments on K-AIGI-Bench show that K-VERA outperforms all evaluated dedicated AIGI detectors by over 15% in balanced accuracy.
8QXGLg69Hh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that verifying world-knowledge consistency is a useful signal complementary to pixel-artifact forensics and appreciate that K-AIGI-Bench records ground-truth inconsistencies to evaluate explanation accuracy.
8QXGLg69Hh.main_concern: Reviewers point out that factual inconsistency does not uniquely identify AI generation (since staged photos, satire, or Photoshop edits also contain factual errors), web retrieval can return unreliable or AI-generated sources, and K-VERA is not compared against a single-agent MLLM given the same search tools and budget.

sZ4q7g0akL.one_liner: Combines online mirror descent with Blackwell approachability to optimize multinomial expert subset routing under sum-max bandit rewards and two-sided frequency constraints.
sZ4q7g0akL.problem: Online routing of tasks to subsets of complementary experts must maximize dimension-wise maximum rewards under aggregate bandit feedback while satisfying two-sided long-run activation frequency constraints that no fixed deterministic subset can meet.
sZ4q7g0akL.method: The paper formalizes Multinomial Subset Routing (MSR), where the learner maintains a probability distribution over K experts and samples M times with replacement per round, and proposes OMD-Approachability. The algorithm combines online mirror descent on a concave expected sum-max reward with Blackwell's approachability on a linearized surrogate to enforce two-sided long-run operational constraints.
sZ4q7g0akL.key_idea: Updates a multinomial expert sampling distribution by coupling online mirror descent on the expected sum-max reward with Blackwell approachability for long-run activation frequency bounds.
sZ4q7g0akL.evidence: Supported by theoretical bounds on objective regret, constraint violation, and the linear-surrogate approximation gap, plus an empirical evaluation on a crowdsourcing dataset.
sZ4q7g0akL.claimed_gains: Establishes O(1/sqrt(T)) objective regret and O(1/sqrt(T)) constraint violation.
sZ4q7g0akL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem formulation combining complementary sum-max expert rewards with long-run operational constraints well-motivated and appreciate the explicit quantification of the linear-surrogate approximation gap.
sZ4q7g0akL.main_concern: Reviewers question the practical naturalness of sampling experts with replacement (which yields variable subset sizes when an expert is drawn multiple times), note that the main components combine existing sum-max concavity results with standard OMD/approachability, and raise a technical concern that Lemma 2 proves distance transfer only for one-sided rather than two-sided constraints.

SVfUwagELt.one_liner: Synthesizes counterfactual image edits and distractor stimuli to test whether fMRI brain encoding representations respond specifically to a target visual concept.
SVfUwagELt.problem: Localizing brain regions via activation maximization often yields false positives because strong neural responses may be driven by correlated visual or semantic cues rather than the target concept itself.
SVfUwagELt.method: BrainTRACE is an automated framework that takes a target visual concept query and uses generative image editing models to construct controlled stimulus sets containing concept images, minimal counterfactual edits removing the target concept, and correlated distractor images. It evaluates these stimuli through an image-to-fMRI encoding model (and held-out measured fMRI data) to identify neural representations that respond specifically to the target concept over correlated alternatives.
SVfUwagELt.key_idea: Generates minimal counterfactual concept-removal image edits and correlated distractors to test candidate fMRI voxels and encoding features for concept specificity beyond raw activation magnitude.
SVfUwagELt.evidence: Evaluated using an image-to-fMRI encoding model and held-out measured fMRI data from the Natural Scenes Dataset (NSD) across known category-selective cortical regions.
SVfUwagELt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that testing concept specificity via minimal counterfactual image edits and correlated distractors addresses a genuine confounding weakness of activation maximization in computational neuroscience, and appreciate validation on held-out NSD images.
SVfUwagELt.main_concern: Reviewers point out that conclusions depend heavily on the out-of-distribution validity and potential confounding of the underlying image-to-fMRI encoding model (whose details are relegated to the appendix) and note unacknowledged overlap with a recent counterfactual fMRI editing framework (MINE).

Qq6xA8JGM7.one_liner: Trains a SQL process preference model on MCTS reasoning trajectories verified by execution and semantic constraints to guide subsequent search.
Qq6xA8JGM7.problem: MCTS-based Text-to-SQL methods typically use search feedback only for terminal candidate selection, providing limited reusable supervision for subsequent reasoning.
Qq6xA8JGM7.method: RStar-SQL performs schema-grounded MCTS to generate SQL trajectories and evaluates them using execution consistency and SQL-specific semantic signals including schema grounding, join validity, and type operator compatibility. Verified high-quality trajectories refine the policy model while preferred and dispreferred pairs train a SQL Process Preference Model to guide action selection in later MCTS rounds.
Qq6xA8JGM7.key_idea: Converts MCTS search outcomes evaluated by execution consistency and SQL semantic signals into process preference training pairs for an action-guiding preference model.
Qq6xA8JGM7.evidence: Evaluated on the LogicCat and Archer complex-reasoning Text-to-SQL benchmarks.
Qq6xA8JGM7.claimed_gains: Achieves execution accuracies of 35.41% on LogicCat and 47.82% on Archer.
Qq6xA8JGM7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that integrating SQL-specific semantic verification with MCTS trajectories to form a self-evolving training loop is practical and yields empirical gains.
Qq6xA8JGM7.main_concern: Reviewers note limited technical novelty because the framework mainly combines existing techniques from Alpha-SQL and SQL-PPM, alongside unfair comparisons against training-free baselines.

jIekruaSGc.one_liner: Compresses compensated onset-apex optical flow into a 12-dimensional FACS-guided regional motion vector classified by an RBF-SVM.
jIekruaSGc.problem: Deep micro-expression recognition models learn latent representations with high computational overhead and limited process-level interpretability for edge deployment.
jIekruaSGc.method: M2E suppresses head-motion interference, transforms compensated onset-apex optical flow into a 12-dimensional FACS-guided regional motion feature vector, and classifies expressions using a class-weighted RBF-SVM. It supports both a lightweight anchor-based configuration and a learning-based optical-flow compensation network (MEFlowNet).
jIekruaSGc.key_idea: Encodes head-motion-compensated onset-apex optical flow into a 12-dimensional FACS-guided regional motion vector for classification by a class-weighted RBF-SVM.
jIekruaSGc.evidence: Evaluated under the MEGC2019 Composite Database Evaluation protocol on the 3DB dataset (including CASME II and SMIC), with Raspberry Pi deployment experiments, ablations, and SHAP analyses.
jIekruaSGc.claimed_gains: Achieves 76.94% UF1 and 79.99% UAR on 3DB with the anchor-based configuration (outperforming LAENet by 1.26 and 5.94 percentage points), and 79.80% UF1 and 83.20% UAR when equipped with MEFlowNet.
jIekruaSGc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the compact 12-dimensional FACS-guided representation and RBF-SVM pipeline for its low computational overhead and clear region-level interpretability.
jIekruaSGc.main_concern: Reviewers point out that the method relies on fragile optical flow estimation and assumes known onset and apex frames, while several underlying components and design choices lack broad novelty or universal optimality.

BP3N5Z200j.one_liner: Decomposes prompts into atomic checklist requirements scored by an LLM or self-verifier to provide soft rewards for RL.
BP3N5Z200j.problem: Reinforcement Learning from Verifiable Rewards struggles on partially verifiable tasks where prompts contain multiple requirements or lack a single reference answer.
BP3N5Z200j.method: Soft-RLVR converts each prompt into a checklist of atomic requirements, scores candidate responses item-by-item using an LLM verifier, and trains the policy on the averaged soft reward. Soft-SVeRL extends this by using the policy itself as the verifier with explicit stabilization to prevent reward inflation.
BP3N5Z200j.key_idea: Decomposes multi-requirement prompts into atomic checklists scored item-by-item by a learned or self-verifying LLM to produce dense partial-credit RL rewards.
BP3N5Z200j.evidence: Evaluated via theoretical bias-variance analysis and experiments in a controlled instruction-following setting (IFEval) across external and self-verifying LLM verifiers.
BP3N5Z200j.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that decomposing multi-constraint instructions into atomic checklist items is an intuitive way to construct dense partial-credit rewards and appreciate the theoretical analysis of the noise-vs-partial-credit trade-off.
BP3N5Z200j.main_concern: Reviewers note a disconnect between the self-verification framing and the empirical results, as the headline gains come from large external verifiers while the self-verifying variant yields modest improvements.

JLHWcd9FHK.one_liner: Reweights traffic simulator candidate actions at test time using a contrastive preference evaluator trained on closed-loop rollout criteria.
JLHWcd9FHK.problem: Autoregressive traffic simulators trained on local ego-centric logs suffer from a local-to-global context mismatch when generating multi-agent interactions for distant non-ego vehicles.
JLHWcd9FHK.method: CRAFT operates post hoc on frozen simulators by labeling grouped closed-loop rollouts with traffic-rule and driving-quality criteria and training a Contextual Preference Evaluator (CPE) via contrastive preference learning. At inference, the CPE uses single-step lookahead to score candidate scene evolutions and reweights action probabilities.
JLHWcd9FHK.key_idea: Trains a standalone Contextual Preference Evaluator on rule-labeled closed-loop rollouts to reweight candidate simulator actions via lookahead at inference without retraining the simulator.
JLHWcd9FHK.evidence: Evaluated across three traffic simulators (CAT-K, SMART, and RLFTSim) on the Waymo Open Motion Dataset and WOSAC.
JLHWcd9FHK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the local-to-global context mismatch is well-motivated and that CRAFT offers a practical, lightweight, plug-and-play post-hoc correction that transfers across simulators.
JLHWcd9FHK.main_concern: Reviewers note that the evaluation is somewhat circular because the evaluator learns from criteria matching the closed-loop metric, while guidance degrades WOSAC kinematic realism and diversity and is bounded by the base simulator's candidate pool.

xOkRenQEWl.one_liner: Synthesizes certified temporal equilibrium policies in deterministic games by replaying stored deviation witnesses across policy candidates.
xOkRenQEWl.problem: During policy search for temporal equilibrium synthesis, repeated equilibrium certification frequently rediscovers the same profitable unilateral deviations after controller updates.
xOkRenQEWl.method: Certified Temporal Equilibrium Synthesis (CTES) combines preference-guided finite-memory policy search with a cross-profile deviation bank that stores profitable infinite behaviors as finite prefixes and repeating loops. Before invoking a complete verifier, replay checks whether current opponents reproduce a stored deviation behavior through loop closure and whether it improves the deviator's Boolean payoff.
xOkRenQEWl.key_idea: Caches profitable unilateral deviations as prefix-loop witnesses and replays them against opponent memory updates to reject candidate policy profiles before running full verification.
xOkRenQEWl.evidence: Supported by soundness and transfer proofs for finite deterministic games with Boolean linear temporal logic goals, alongside matched ablation experiments.
xOkRenQEWl.claimed_gains: Prepared witness replay increases online certification throughput by 5.6--13.5%.
xOkRenQEWl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that reusing deviation counterexamples by checking loop closure over opponent memory and re-verifying payoff improvement is theoretically sound and clearly formulated.
xOkRenQEWl.main_concern: Reviewers find the conceptual advance over standard verification caching limited, note the absence of external verification tool baselines or a learning component, and point out unclear domain motivation.

PbKQlv3crP.one_liner: Jointly pretrains a shared scale-flexible encoder across four 2D cryo-EM and cryo-ET observation types using pose-aware contrastive and masked patch objectives.
PbKQlv3crP.problem: Existing cryo-EM representation-learning methods specialize in individual observation types, limiting knowledge transfer across single-particle analysis and cryogenic electron tomography workflows.
PbKQlv3crP.method: CryoVERSE jointly pretrains a scale-flexible shared encoder on four pre-reconstruction 2D cryo-EM observation types: SPA micrographs, SPA particles, cryo-ET tilt images, and tilt-derived cryo-ET particles. It combines pose-aware contrastive learning with masked patch-level prediction to learn global and spatial features.
PbKQlv3crP.key_idea: Pretrains a single scale-flexible vision backbone across four SPA and cryo-ET 2D observation types using pose-aware contrastive learning and masked patch prediction.
PbKQlv3crP.evidence: Pretrained on a corpus of 143.7M images and evaluated on molecular structure classification, projection-pose classification, particle quality ranking, dense particle localization, and cryo-ET downstream tasks.
PbKQlv3crP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the value of unifying SPA and cryo-ET representation learning in a single shared encoder and appreciate the breadth of downstream evaluations and data curation.
PbKQlv3crP.main_concern: Reviewers argue that the central claim of cross-type transfer is weakly supported because ablations show only tiny gains from adding wide-field or cryo-ET data, with no variance reported and confounded baseline comparisons.

AkoXpUYvku.one_liner: Selects UAV navigation actions by scoring imagined visual futures and Grounding-DINO-supervised target heatmaps with a stage-aware value expert.
AkoXpUYvku.problem: Applying world-action models to language-goal aerial object navigation struggles because predicted visual futures often miss small target objects and sparse feedback fails to rank candidate futures.
AkoXpUYvku.method: FG-WVAM combines a world model that predicts visual futures and target heatmaps supervised by a frozen Grounding DINO teacher, a Future Value Expert trained with stage-aware exploration/approach labels, and an Action Expert. At inference, the Future Value Expert scores multiple imagined futures and the highest-scoring candidate drives action generation.
AkoXpUYvku.key_idea: Supervises imagined visual futures with target-weighted Grounding DINO heatmaps and scores candidate rollouts using a stage-aware value estimator to select navigation actions.
AkoXpUYvku.evidence: Evaluated on the UAV-ON and AerialDoJo aerial object navigation benchmarks across same-scene and unseen-scene splits.
AkoXpUYvku.claimed_gains: Improves success rate (SR) by 12.3 points on UAV-ON and 10.2 points on AerialDoJo.
AkoXpUYvku.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that supervising future target heatmaps and estimating stage-aware task value directly address the challenges of preserving small targets and scoring rollouts in aerial search.
AkoXpUYvku.main_concern: Reviewers highlight an unexplained performance inversion on AerialDoJo where unseen-scene success rates are substantially higher than same-scene rates across retrained methods, alongside writing clarity issues.

jJ6lqAxkf7.one_liner: Trains a multimodal agent memorization policy in two phases to ensure memory fidelity before adapting a lightweight adapter to recent task rewards.
jJ6lqAxkf7.problem: Multimodal agents receiving an unbounded stream of observations struggle to selectively memorize content that is relevant to future tasks encountered in their environment.
jJ6lqAxkf7.method: TaskMem formulates memory generation as a learnable policy trained in two phases: Phase One optimizes memory quality under basic fidelity requirements, and Phase Two occurs post-deployment by tuning a lightweight adapter on the base MLLM using rewards derived from recent environment tasks.
jJ6lqAxkf7.key_idea: Separates pre-deployment memory-fidelity training from post-deployment task-driven RL adaptation of a lightweight adapter using rewards constructed from recent environment tasks.
jJ6lqAxkf7.evidence: Evaluated on streaming reformulations of the VideoMME, EgoLife, and EgoTempo benchmarks using a Qwen3-VL backbone.
jJ6lqAxkf7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clear two-phase formulation that decouples basic memory fidelity from lightweight post-deployment task adaptation.
jJ6lqAxkf7.main_concern: Reviewers question generalization and evaluation fairness because tasks are grouped into stationary single-type adaptation blocks, backbone models and clip durations differ from baselines, and Phase Two is not cleanly isolated from simple task prompting.

Zzgyk8v2JK.one_liner: Couples a multi-stage auditable clinical reasoning pipeline with failure-driven memory evolution for medication recommendation.
Zzgyk8v2JK.problem: Existing medication recommendation systems lack decision auditability to trace patient evidence to individual drugs and correctability to learn from recurrent recommendation errors.
Zzgyk8v2JK.method: EvoMedAgent decomposes patient visits into evidence-grounded clinical problem units, performs patient-level reconciliation and independent review to form an auditable reasoning trace, and links judgments to final medications. When errors occur, a failure-driven evolution process attributes typed failures, routes scoped corrections across four memory layers, and validates updates before storing them.
Zzgyk8v2JK.key_idea: Links unit-level clinical reasoning and patient-level reconciliation into an auditable trace that drives typed failure attribution and validated multi-layer memory updates.
Zzgyk8v2JK.evidence: Evaluated on real-world clinical datasets including MIMIC-III with component ablation studies.
Zzgyk8v2JK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that decomposing multimorbid visits into structured clinical units with patient-level reconciliation and failure-driven memory updates is well-motivated for clinical decision support.
Zzgyk8v2JK.main_concern: Reviewers note limited technical novelty over existing agentic memory frameworks and point out that performance gains are confounded by restricting candidates to training-label boundaries and auxiliary retrieval/calibration tools.

pShzNEI5bp.one_liner: Transports samples from pretrained generative models toward heavy-tailed targets via a CVaR-penalized Wasserstein gradient flow.
pShzNEI5bp.problem: Learning heavy-tailed distributions for extreme events from finite samples is difficult because the tail region is severely under-sampled relative to its importance.
pShzNEI5bp.method: The CVaR-penalized Generative Particle Algorithm (CVaR-GPA) discretizes the Wasserstein gradient flow of a Lipschitz-regularized KL divergence penalized by a Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) discrepancy term. Initialized from output samples of a black-box pretrained model, it transports particles along the loss gradient without accessing the base model's internal architecture.
pShzNEI5bp.key_idea: Transports generated particles a posteriori along a discretized Wasserstein gradient flow combining Lipschitz-regularized KL divergence with a scalar-dependent CVaR tail penalty.
pShzNEI5bp.evidence: Supported by variational and subgradient theoretical analysis and empirical validation on toy and small-scale heavy-tailed domains.
pShzNEI5bp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the idea of post-hoc particle transport combining Lipschitz-regularized KL divergence with a CVaR penalty theoretically principled and original for extreme-event modeling.
pShzNEI5bp.main_concern: Reviewers criticize the paper's dense, inaccessible mathematical exposition and lack of clear algorithmic pseudocode or large-scale experimental validation.

zf3wOP0tyV.one_liner: nUniMixer learns dual-axis feature-mixing patterns and normalizes the mixing block for scalable recommendation ranking.
zf3wOP0tyV.problem: Attention, TokenMixer, and factorization-machine ranking architectures lack a common framework for understanding and improving model scaling.
zf3wOP0tyV.method: UniMixer connects the three architecture families and replaces rule-based token mixing with a Dual-Axis Heterogeneous Mixer that learns global element-wise mixing. The normalized nUniMixer block relaxes parameter-matrix constraints to improve scaling efficiency.
zf3wOP0tyV.key_idea: Parameterize fixed token-mixing rules with a learnable dual-axis mixer and normalize the resulting block.
zf3wOP0tyV.evidence: Offline and online experiments evaluate diverse recommendation tasks and application scenarios, including large-scale industrial data.
zf3wOP0tyV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the practical efficiency-performance trade-off and empirical results from learnable feature mixing in ranking models.
zf3wOP0tyV.main_concern: The technical contribution is insufficiently distinguished from closely related learnable mixing architectures and established components.

gUTgGBlHLU.one_liner: Heads of Security learns per-head attention gates that redistribute attention between trusted instructions and untrusted content.
gUTgGBlHLU.problem: Language models can follow malicious instructions embedded in untrusted content while carrying out legitimate tasks.
gUTgGBlHLU.method: HoS uses an externally supplied trust boundary and learned per-head gates to modify attention between trusted and untrusted tokens. It trains a small set of gate parameters while preserving the original model weights.
gUTgGBlHLU.key_idea: Gate pairwise attention by token trust status separately for each attention head.
gUTgGBlHLU.evidence: Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct and GPT-OSS-20B are evaluated against SecAlign++ and ASIDE using adaptive attacks, utility tests, and agentic prompt-injection benchmarks.
gUTgGBlHLU.claimed_gains: RL-Hammer reaches 97% ASR against GPT-OSS-20B and 85% against SecAlign but only 10% against HoS, while strengthened Claudini requires 3 times more FLOPs to reach the same ASR on HoS.
